content.text:
Done — the fix needed both sides, and the firmware part had a trap in it.

**Why you were seeing only the future:** the controller asked aWATTar for prices starting at *now*, so the curve it served the app was future-only. The chart's ±12 h window then had nothing to draw on the left.

**Controller** (`firmware/main/prices/`)
- `flux_prices.c`: new `FETCH_BACKFILL_S` (24 h) — fetches `now-24h … now+36h` so clients can price the last day and chart what was actually paid. Log line now reports back/ahead coverage.
- `flux_prices_awattar.c`: had to add an explicit `&end=` to the request. With `start` alone the API returns *exactly 24 h from start* — my first flash therefore produced a curve that was entirely in the past and marked `STALE`. Verified against the live API (58 intervals, 08-02 12:00 → 08-04 21:00) and on the device: **58 intervals, "now" sits at index 25 — 25 h settled behind, ~33 h ahead, not stale.**

**App**
- `energy_price_card.dart`: window is now **last 24 h + up to 12 h forecast** (the forecast tail is capped so it can't squeeze the history). Settled prices draw solid; everything right of the `now` line draws faded over a subtle wash and is labelled `FORECAST`. Price Y-axis now scales to the prices *in view* (the curve is 58 h long, so whole-curve min/max flattened it). Time gridlines walk wall-clock hours across the window instead of only where price points exist, 6 h steps when the span is wide, DST-safe.
- Readout: `import cost · 24h`, and `Ø` is now the **24 h** mean (`EnergyPrices.avgCtIn`) instead of the whole-curve mean, which now mixes past and tomorrow.
- Footnote when the controller's curve doesn't reach back yet: *"No settled prices for the last 24 h yet — forecast only"* — otherwise the empty left half is baffling.
- `device_provider.dart`: history window 12 h → 24 h so the overlay covers the whole past side; `energy_history_card.dart` relabelled to `LAST 24 HOURS` / `consumed · 24 h` accordingly.

Analyzer clean (0 errors/warnings), 93/93 tests including new `avgCtIn` coverage. Debug APK built.

**Not deployed:** no adb device is attached — the daemon restarted and both phones are gone (`no devices/emulators found`). Give me the current wireless-debugging port, or plug one in, and I'll install. Firmware is already flashed and serving the backfilled curve, so the graph will be right as soon as the app lands.

# Flux App — device modelling, control, categorisation & onboarding

**Repo:** `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app` (Flutter, package name `matter_home`, v1.3.0+9). ~22k LOC of Dart. Architecture doc: `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/ARCHITECTURE.md`; the critical design constraint is in `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/docs/controller-only-control.md`.

**Headline for your integration:** the app already has a working precedent for exactly what you want — non-Matter cloud/LAN appliances surfaced as ordinary devices. It's the Modbus path, and the key architectural fact is that *the app does almost nothing special for it*: the **Flux Controller** (ESP-based hub) does the protocol work and re-exposes such devices as synthetic Matter nodes over the same `/devices` + `/events` + `/command` CoAP contract. The app-side surface is one provisioning screen. Whether Home Connect follows that pattern (controller does OAuth + polling) or an app-side pattern (phone does OAuth) is the biggest fork in your design, and the app today has **zero** OAuth/webview/deep-link/secure-storage infrastructure.

---

## 1. Device model

### `MatterDevice` — the persisted commissioning record
`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart`

| Member | Line | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `class MatterDevice` (`@immutable`) | 65 | "Stable commissioning record… only identity and topology facts that never change without an explicit user action" |
| `final String id` | 107 | **App-local UUID** (`_uuid.v4()`), the primary key everywhere in the UI |
| `final int nodeId` | 110 | **Controller/Matter node id** — the wire identifier |
| `deviceType`, `name`, `isOnline`, `sharedWithGoogleHome`, `commissionedAt`, `lastModified`, `networkType`, `managedBy`, `roomId`, `energyRole` | 108–119 | `lastModified` exists for last-write-wins sync |
| `bool get isModbus => nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000` | 125 | **The synthetic-node-id range check.** Comment: "controller registers [Modbus devices] under a synthetic node id at/above `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` (`0x0100000000000000`) — well above the small operational node ids real Matter devices get" |

**`id` vs `nodeId`** — this distinction matters for you:
- `id` (UUID) is minted by the app in two places: `registerCommissionedDevice` (`device_provider.dart:864`) and `_reconcileWithController` (`device_provider.dart:412`). All routes (`/device/:id`), `viewFor(id)`, `findById(id)`, snapshots and rules key on it.
- `nodeId` is what every controller call takes (`toggle`, `startSubscription`, `readClusters`, `removeDevice`…) and what event streams are matched on (`_onDeviceStateEvent`: `_devices.where((d) => d.nodeId == event.nodeId)`, `device_provider.dart:671`). Reconciliation matches controller devices to local records **by `nodeId`** (`device_provider.dart:397`).
- Consequence for Home Connect: a cloud appliance will need *some* integer node id to flow through the existing pipeline unchanged, or you break the `MatterPort` contract. The Modbus precedent reserves a high range; you'd naturally want e.g. `FLUX_HOMECONNECT_NODE_BASE` and an `isCloud`/`isHomeConnect` getter beside `isModbus:125`.

### `ManagedBy` — only two values
`matter_device.dart:40–55`
```dart

  /// Commands go through the local phone SDK ([MatterChannel]).
  phone,
  /// Commands go through the Flux Controller ([FluxCoapService]).
  controller;
}
```
It has `label` ('Phone'/'Controller') and `icon` (`smartphone_outlined`/`hub_outlined`). Semantics = **which port sends commands and receives subscription events**. Default is `phone` (constructor line 76, and `fromJson` fallback line 101).

Where it actually drives behaviour:
- `_startSubscription` skips the 15 s establish-fallback timer for `ManagedBy.controller` (`device_provider.dart:824`).
- `refreshDevice` refuses to mark a controller-managed device offline on a timed-out read (`device_provider.dart:1029`).
- `registerCommissionedDevice` skips the immediate refresh for controller devices (`device_provider.dart:885`).
- `removeDevice` always tells the controller, and additionally the local channel only for non-controller devices (`device_provider.dart:1148–1155`).
- `_reconcileWithController` only auto-deletes devices with `managedBy == controller` (`device_provider.dart:455`) — controller is source of truth for those; phone-commissioned ones are never auto-removed.
- Device detail gates "accessible" on hub online for controller devices (`device_detail_screen.dart:273`).

**This is the natural extension point**: a third value (e.g. `ManagedBy.cloud`) is a small, well-contained change *if* commands go somewhere other than the controller. If the controller brokers Home Connect, you need **no** new enum value.

`NetworkType` (`matter_device.dart:11–34`): `wifi, thread, ethernet, modbus, unknown`, each with `label` and an icon-name string. `modbus` was added exactly as a non-Matter transport marker — precedent for a `cloud`/`homeConnect` member. Note `_normalizeControllerNetworkType` (`device_provider.dart:344`) repairs legacy records and returns `modbus` whenever `isModbus`.

## 2. Non-Matter devices today (Modbus / SunSpec)

**This is your template.** The proto comment is the clearest statement of the pattern — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/flux-interface/proto/flux.proto:244–251`:

> "The controller can also poll non-Matter devices over Modbus TCP (e.g. a PV inverter on the home LAN) and expose them to the app **as if they were Matter devices**: each is registered in the same device registry under a synthetic node ID (Matter-reserved range) with a real Matter `device_type`, and its readings are pushed through the same `/events` pipeline under the same attribute keys a Matter device would use. Only the provisioning surface below is Modbus-specific; `Device` / `AttrsUpdate` / `DeviceStateEvent` are reused verbatim."

Mirrored app-side at `flux_coap_service.dart:357–359`.

**(a) Declared capability** — `DeviceType` flags. Device detail composes cards purely from them (`device_detail_screen.dart:306–344`).

**(b) Discovered capability via AcceptedCommandList** — `bool onOffClusterIsControllable(List<LiveEndpoint> endpoints)` at `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/cluster_parser.dart:554`, doc at 547–553:

> "the Matter-specified way to distinguish a *controllable* On/Off cluster (device accepts On / Off / Toggle commands) from a cluster that is only present for state reporting. ## 3. Control path from the UI

### Layering
`MatterPort` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/matter_port.dart:120`) combines four narrow interfaces: `MatterSubscriptionPort` (15), `MatterCommissionPort` (26), `MatterClusterPort` (73 — every command/write/read signature, all taking `int nodeId`), `MatterFabricPort` (105). Three implementations: `MatterChannel` (local CHIP, BLE commissioning only in practice), `FluxCoapService`, `NullMatterPort` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/null_matter_port.dart:17` — every method a safe no-op).

Wiring in `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/main.dart:64–93`: `MatterClusterPort` and `MatterFabricPort` are `ProxyProvider`s over `HubConnection` resolving to `hub.service ?? nullChannel` (L80–85) — "never `localChannel`". `DeviceProvider` starts on `NullMatterPort` (L57) and adopts the real service via `attachHubConnection` (L60) → `_onHubConnectionChanged` → `adoptHubMode`.

### Tap → controller call, end to end (the toggle case)
1. **Tile/card tap.** Home grid → `DeviceCard(deviceId:, onTap:)` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/widgets/device_card.dart:21`; it `context.watch<DeviceProvider>().viewFor(deviceId)` at L29 so it rebuilds on every notification) → `context.push('/device/${id}')` (`home_screen.dart:161`, `category_screen.dart:66`). Cards are display-only; there's no inline toggle.
2. **Control widget.** `_OnOffCard` — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/device_detail/on_off_card.dart:31`: `onTap: isStale ? null : () => context.read<DeviceProvider>().toggle(view.id)`. Note controls disable on `isStale`.
3. **Provider, optimistic + rollback** — `DeviceProvider.toggle` at `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/providers/device_provider.dart:906`:
   - capability gate L913 (see §2)
   - `final currentOn = _liveCache[deviceId]?.isOn ?? false; final newOn = !currentOn;` L918 — "Use live cache as source of truth so toggle direction is always correct"
   - **optimistic:** `_mergeLiveCache(deviceId, (e) => e.merge({'onOff': newOn}));` L922
   - `final ok = await _channel.toggleDevice(device.nodeId, on: newOn);` L923
   - success → `_flushSnapshot(deviceId)` L925; failure → **rollback** `merge({'onOff': currentOn})` L928
   - `_mergeLiveCache` itself always `notifyListeners()` (L624–627)
4. **Transport** — `FluxCoapService.toggleDevice` at `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/flux_coap_service.dart:618` → `_sendCmd(nodeId, 0x0006, on ? 1 : 0, [])`.
5. **`_sendCmd`** — `flux_coap_service.dart:592–610`. Builds `$proto.DeviceCommand()..nodeId..endpointId (default 1)..clusterId..commandId..args`, `POST /command`, decodes `BoolResult.success`. Critical flag: `retryOnConnError: false` (L606) with the comment "Not idempotent: stepLevel / covering / lock commands would be applied twice if the request landed but its response was lost."
6. **Live update back.** `startSubscription(nodeId)` (`flux_coap_service.dart:450`) opens a CoAP **Observe** on `GET /events?id=<16-hex>` (L473–475) with exponential-backoff resubscribe (`_subRetryBase` 2 s → `_subRetryMax` 60 s, L446–447, `scheduleRetry` L452). Bytes → `_handleStateBytes` (L548) → `_toAppEvent` (L558) which maps `DeviceEventType` to the sealed Dart events and flattens `ev.update.attrs` into `Map<String,dynamic>` by `boolVal`/`intVal`/`longVal` (L568–574).

Devices already on-network skip the phone entirely (`matter_port.dart:32–35`).

**Registration** — `DeviceProvider.registerCommissionedDevice(CommissionResult, String name, NetworkType, {ManagedBy managedBy = ManagedBy.phone})` at `device_provider.dart:852`. **This is the function a Home Connect flow would parallel** — mint UUID, build `MatterDevice`, `_persist()`, `notifyListeners()`, start subscription. 1. **Add a Modbus device by IP** — §2, `modbus_devices_screen.dart` reached from the Energy category's `_EnergySetupCard`.
2. **Add a controller (pair the hub)** — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/add_controller_flow.dart`: `runAddControllerFlow(context, {knownControllerId})` L23 shows `AddControllerSheet` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/widgets/add_controller_sheet.dart`), parses **`flux://setup?id=<controllerId>&psk=<hex32>`** or raw hex (L33–43), `ControllerSettings.savePsk`, `hub.refreshConfiguredState()` + `hub.reconnect()`, snackbar feedback. 3. **Auto-adoption** — devices appearing in `GET /devices` are silently added by `_reconcileWithController` (`device_provider.dart:399–429`). If the controller brokers Home Connect, appliances would *appear by themselves* with no app changes beyond type/icon/category.

### Where a "connect a cloud account" flow would naturally live
Ranked by fit with existing conventions:

1. **Mirroring Modbus exactly**: a `HomeConnectDevicesScreen` under `lib/ui/screens/settings/`, launched from a new card row. But note *where* Modbus is surfaced — inside the **Energy** category, not Settings, because that's where its devices are conceptually. Appliances aren't primarily energy, so a new **Appliances** `HomeCategory` with its own setup card (copying `_EnergySetupCard`, `category_screen.dart:81`) is the most idiomatic home.
2. **Main Settings** — `settings_screen.dart` is explicitly reserved for the controller ("the phone itself has nothing the user needs to configure", L18–20). **None registered on either platform.**

`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:

`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/ios/Runner/Info.plist`:

```dart
static const _kDtlsId   = 'ctrl_dtls_id';   // :9
static const _kRzvUrl   = 'ctrl_rzv_url';   // :10 rendezvous URL (ADR-0006)
static const _kStun     = 'ctrl_stun';      // :11 (ADR-0007)
static const _kTurn     = 'ctrl_turn';      // :12 (ADR-0004)
static const _kTurnUser = 'ctrl_turn_user'; // :13
static const _kTurnPass = 'ctrl_turn_pass'; // :14
```
The **16-byte DTLS PSK** is stored as a 32-char hex string under `ctrl_psk_<hostname>` — `savePsk` L38 (`assert(psk.length == 16)`), `loadPsk` L19. Convention exists, but it's a convention, not a guarantee.

An OAuth refresh token in SharedPreferences would inherit this exposure; `flutter_secure_storage` (Keystore/Keychain) would be the right call and would be the app's first use of it.

Also relevant: the product positioning is explicitly **no-cloud**. `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/settings/remote_access_screen.dart:9` — "Flux runs no cloud: the phone connects…" and L220 — "…cloud and keeps no account of yours — your phone connects…". `docs/ios-port-plan.md:15` — "App's value is standalone, local, no-cloud control." pubspec description: "Local, private, independent." ---

# Flux App — device modelling, control, categorisation & onboarding

**Repo:** `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app` (Flutter, package name `matter_home`, v1.3.0+9). ~22k LOC of Dart. Architecture doc: `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/ARCHITECTURE.md`; the critical design constraint is in `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/docs/controller-only-control.md`.

**Headline for your integration:** the app already has a working precedent for exactly what you want — non-Matter cloud/LAN appliances surfaced as ordinary devices. It's the Modbus path, and the key architectural fact is that *the app does almost nothing special for it*: the **Flux Controller** (ESP-based hub) does the protocol work and re-exposes such devices as synthetic Matter nodes over the same `/devices` + `/events` + `/command` CoAP contract. The app-side surface is one provisioning screen. Whether Home Connect follows that pattern (controller does OAuth + polling) or an app-side pattern (phone does OAuth) is the biggest fork in your design, and the app today has **zero** OAuth/webview/deep-link/secure-storage infrastructure.

---

## 1. Device model

### `MatterDevice` — the persisted commissioning record
`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart`

| Member | Line | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `class MatterDevice` (`@immutable`) | 65 | "Stable commissioning record… only identity and topology facts that never change without an explicit user action" |
| `final String id` | 107 | **App-local UUID** (`_uuid.v4()`), the primary key everywhere in the UI |
| `final int nodeId` | 110 | **Controller/Matter node id** — the wire identifier |
| `deviceType`, `name`, `isOnline`, `sharedWithGoogleHome`, `commissionedAt`, `lastModified`, `networkType`, `managedBy`, `roomId`, `energyRole` | 108–119 | `lastModified` exists for last-write-wins sync |
| `bool get isModbus => nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000` | 125 | **The synthetic-node-id range check.** Comment: "controller registers [Modbus devices] under a synthetic node id at/above `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` (`0x0100000000000000`) — well above the small operational node ids real Matter devices get" |
| `fromJson` / `toJson` | 81 / 155 | Enums round-trip by `.name` with `orElse` fallbacks — forward/backward tolerant |
| `operator ==` / `hashCode` | 171 / 174 | **Identity is `id` only** |

**`id` vs `nodeId`** — this distinction matters for you:
- `id` (UUID) is minted by the app in two places: `registerCommissionedDevice` (`device_provider.dart:864`) and `_reconcileWithController` (`device_provider.dart:412`). All routes (`/device/:id`), `viewFor(id)`, `findById(id)`, snapshots and rules key on it.
- `nodeId` is what every controller call takes (`toggle`, `startSubscription`, `readClusters`, `removeDevice`…) and what event streams are matched on (`_onDeviceStateEvent`: `_devices.where((d) => d.nodeId == event.nodeId)`, `device_provider.dart:671`). Reconciliation matches controller devices to local records **by `nodeId`** (`device_provider.dart:397`).
- Consequence for Home Connect: a cloud appliance will need *some* integer node id to flow through the existing pipeline unchanged, or you break the `MatterPort` contract. The Modbus precedent reserves a high range; you'd naturally want e.g. `FLUX_HOMECONNECT_NODE_BASE` and an `isCloud`/`isHomeConnect` getter beside `isModbus:125`.

### `ManagedBy` — only two values
`matter_device.dart:40–55`
```dart
enum ManagedBy {
  /// Commands go through the local phone SDK ([MatterChannel]).
  phone,
  /// Commands go through the Flux Controller ([FluxCoapService]).
  controller;
}
```
It has `label` ('Phone'/'Controller') and `icon` (`smartphone_outlined`/`hub_outlined`). Semantics = **which port sends commands and receives subscription events**. Default is `phone` (constructor line 76, and `fromJson` fallback line 101).

Where it actually drives behaviour:
- `_startSubscription` skips the 15 s establish-fallback timer for `ManagedBy.controller` (`device_provider.dart:824`).
- `refreshDevice` refuses to mark a controller-managed device offline on a timed-out read (`device_provider.dart:1029`).
- `registerCommissionedDevice` skips the immediate refresh for controller devices (`device_provider.dart:885`).
- `removeDevice` always tells the controller, and additionally the local channel only for non-controller devices (`device_provider.dart:1148–1155`).
- `_reconcileWithController` only auto-deletes devices with `managedBy == controller` (`device_provider.dart:455`) — controller is source of truth for those; phone-commissioned ones are never auto-removed.
- Device detail gates "accessible" on hub online for controller devices (`device_detail_screen.dart:273`).

**This is your template.** The proto comment is the clearest statement of the pattern — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/flux-interface/proto/flux.proto:244–251`:

> "The controller can also poll non-Matter devices over Modbus TCP (e.g. a PV inverter on the home LAN) and expose them to the app **as if they were Matter devices**: each is registered in the same device registry under a synthetic node ID (Matter-reserved range) with a real Matter `device_type`, and its readings are pushed through the same `/events` pipeline under the same attribute keys a Matter device would use. Only the provisioning surface below is Modbus-specific; `Device` / `AttrsUpdate` / `DeviceStateEvent` are reused verbatim."

## 3. Control path from the UI

### Layering
`MatterPort` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/matter_port.dart:120`) combines four narrow interfaces: `MatterSubscriptionPort` (15), `MatterCommissionPort` (26), `MatterClusterPort` (73 — every command/write/read signature, all taking `int nodeId`), `MatterFabricPort` (105). Three implementations: `MatterChannel` (local CHIP, BLE commissioning only in practice), `FluxCoapService`, `NullMatterPort` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/null_matter_port.dart:17` — every method a safe no-op).

Wiring in `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/main.dart:64–93`: `MatterClusterPort` and `MatterFabricPort` are `ProxyProvider`s over `HubConnection` resolving to `hub.service ?? nullChannel` (L80–85) — "never `localChannel`". `DeviceProvider` starts on `NullMatterPort` (L57) and adopts the real service via `attachHubConnection` (L60) → `_onHubConnectionChanged` → `adoptHubMode`.

### Tap → controller call, end to end (the toggle case)
1. **Tile/card tap.** Home grid → `DeviceCard(deviceId:, onTap:)` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/widgets/device_card.dart:21`; it `context.watch<DeviceProvider>().viewFor(deviceId)` at L29 so it rebuilds on every notification) → `context.push('/device/${id}')` (`home_screen.dart:161`, `category_screen.dart:66`). Cards are display-only; there's no inline toggle.
2. **Control widget.** `_OnOffCard` — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/device_detail/on_off_card.dart:31`: `onTap: isStale ? null : () => context.read<DeviceProvider>().toggle(view.id)`. Note controls disable on `isStale`.
3. **Provider, optimistic + rollback** — `DeviceProvider.toggle` at `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/providers/device_provider.dart:906`:
   - capability gate L913 (see §2)
   - `final currentOn = _liveCache[deviceId]?.isOn ?? false; final newOn = !currentOn;` L918 — "Use live cache as source of truth so toggle direction is always correct"
   - **optimistic:** `_mergeLiveCache(deviceId, (e) => e.merge({'onOff': newOn}));` L922
   - `final ok = await _channel.toggleDevice(device.nodeId, on: newOn);` L923
   - success → `_flushSnapshot(deviceId)` L925; failure → **rollback** `merge({'onOff': currentOn})` L928
   - `_mergeLiveCache` itself always `notifyListeners()` (L624–627)
4. **Transport** — `FluxCoapService.toggleDevice` at `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/flux_coap_service.dart:618` → `_sendCmd(nodeId, 0x0006, on ? 1 : 0, [])`.
5. **`_sendCmd`** — `flux_coap_service.dart:592–610`. Builds `$proto.DeviceCommand()..nodeId..endpointId (default 1)..clusterId..commandId..args`, `POST /command`, decodes `BoolResult.success`. Critical flag: `retryOnConnError: false` (L606) with the comment "Not idempotent: stepLevel / covering / lock commands would be applied twice if the request landed but its response was lost."
6. **Live update back.** `startSubscription(nodeId)` (`flux_coap_service.dart:450`) opens a CoAP **Observe** on `GET /events?id=<16-hex>` (L473–475) with exponential-backoff resubscribe (`_subRetryBase` 2 s → `_subRetryMax` 60 s, L446–447, `scheduleRetry` L452). Bytes → `_handleStateBytes` (L548) → `_toAppEvent` (L558) which maps `DeviceEventType` to the sealed Dart events and flattens `ev.update.attrs` into `Map<String,dynamic>` by `boolVal`/`intVal`/`longVal` (L568–574).
7. **Provider ingests** — `_onDeviceStateEvent` (`device_provider.dart:670`): matches by `nodeId` (671), pattern-matches the sealed type (675) — error/resubscribing → `markStale()` + notify (676–682); `established` → cancel fallback timer + one snapshot flush per session (684–694); `update` → `_applyStateUpdate` (696).
8. **`_applyStateUpdate`** (`device_provider.dart:704`): captures prev contact state (706), merges attrs (709), runs automation hooks `_handleSwitchPress`/`_handleContactChange` (712/714), the energy-odometer accumulation for `periodicEnergyMwh` (728–742), type inference (747–756), `isOnline` false→true transition persist (760–764), `notifyListeners()` (765).

Backs `writeHeatingSetpoint` (721, thermostat 0x0201/0x0012), `writeSystemMode` (725, 0x001C), `setFanMode` (729, fan 0x0202/0x0000), `setFanPercent` (733, 0x0002). **History** — `DeviceProvider.fetchEnergyHistory()` (`device_provider.dart:167`, coalesced, last 24 h in 3600 s buckets) → `FluxCoapService.getEnergyHistory` (`flux_coap_service.dart:290`, `GET /energy/history?from&to&bucket&series`) → `EnergyHistoryData.fromProto` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/models/energy_history.dart:156`). Per-device data: `PvDeviceSeries` (L40) built from `h.deviceSeries` filtered to `ENERGY_CLASS_PV` (L200). The chart re-labels those series with the **local** name: `deviceNameForNode(s.nodeId) ?? s.name` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/home/energy_history_card.dart:221`). Drops the in-progress bucket (L167–173). KPIs `consumptionKwh` (137) and `selfSufficiencyPercent` (149).

**Prices/tariff** — `fetchEnergyPrices` (`device_provider.dart:211`) and `updateTariff` (244) over `GET/POST /prices/config` + `GET /prices` (`flux_coap_service.dart:312–338`); UI `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/home/energy_price_card.dart` and `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/settings/tariff_settings_screen.dart`.

Energy view composition — `category_screen.dart:48–53`: `HouseEnergyScene`, `EnergyHistoryCard`, `EnergyPriceCard`, `_EnergySetupCard`, then the device grid. Also `EnergyCard` on device detail (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/device_detail/energy_card.dart`, gated at `device_detail_screen.dart:345–351`).

**Relevance to Home Connect:** appliances are exactly the "load" class (`EnergyClass` 3). `EnergyRole` has no generic `appliance`/`load` member today — `carCharger` and `heatPump` are the only consumer roles, and both map to 3. Adding e.g. `EnergyRole.appliance → 3` would slot a dishwasher into both the house scene and the controller's energy log with essentially no other changes, *provided* the device reports `activePower` (Home Connect does expose power/energy for some appliances) — but note the role picker is gated on `hasEnergyMeasurement || hasLivePower` (`device_settings_screen.dart:154`), so an appliance with no power readings won't get a role picker at all.

---

## 5. Adding / onboarding a device

### Matter commissioning
**Entry points:**
- Home FAB — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/home_screen.dart:39–54`: tri-state. `noHub` → `_addHub` (L112 → `runAddControllerFlow`); `online` → `_addDevice` (L102: `QrScannerScreen` → `context.push('/commission', extra: payload)`); offline → snackbar "Can't reach your controller". Comment L23–24: "Commissioning requires a hub".
- Route `/commission` — `router.dart:20–24`, `CommissionScreen(initialPayload: state.extra as String?)`.

**`CommissionScreen`** (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/commission_screen.dart`, 2103 lines): class L23, three build modes (progress / scanning-backdrop / expert form) at L451–459. `_commission()` L395 → `_ctrl.start(CommissionConfig(...))`; on success `context.pushReplacement('/room-picker/${_ctrl.result!.id}')` (L420). Sub-widgets: `_PayloadEntry` L896, `_NetworkSection` L1132, `_ThreadDatasetPromptSheet` L1458, `_WifiCredentialPanel` L1785, method-picker (BLE/IP) extension L1981–2040.

**`CommissioningController`** (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/providers/commissioning_controller.dart`, 806 lines): ctor L178 takes `MatterCommissionPort port`, `DeviceProvider provider`, `requestBlePermissions`, `onNeedsCredentials`, `threadDataset`, `controllerService`. Enums `CommissionMethod {ble, ip}` L21, `CommissionPhase {idle, parsing, parsed, running, done, failed}` L23. `setPayload` L268, `start` L308 — **fails fast without a hub** (L311–318: "No Flux controller connected"). Progress plumbing: `_subscribeControllerProgress` L231 over `observeCommissionEvents()` (`flux_coap_service.dart:517`, Observe on `/commission/events`); 32 CHIP stage names in `kCommissionStages` (L~100) with human labels in `kCommissionStageHuman`. `reset` L613, `_onEvent` L712, `_handleCredentialsNeeded` L748.

The commission-then-handoff design: phone BLE-commissions onto a throwaway fabric, opens an ECM window, hands passcode+discriminator to the controller via `POST /commission` (`flux_coap_service.dart:402`, 150 s timeout, `retryOnConnError:false`), then removes its own fabric. Devices already on-network skip the phone entirely (`matter_port.dart:32–35`).

**Registration** — `DeviceProvider.registerCommissionedDevice(CommissionResult, String name, NetworkType, {ManagedBy managedBy = ManagedBy.phone})` at `device_provider.dart:852`. **This is the function a Home Connect flow would parallel** — mint UUID, build `MatterDevice`, `_persist()`, `notifyListeners()`, start subscription. Also `beginCommissioning():843` and `failCommissioning(error):895`.

### Non-Matter add flows that exist today
1. **Add a Modbus device by IP** — §2, `modbus_devices_screen.dart` reached from the Energy category's `_EnergySetupCard`.
2. **Add a controller (pair the hub)** — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/add_controller_flow.dart`: `runAddControllerFlow(context, {knownControllerId})` L23 shows `AddControllerSheet` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/widgets/add_controller_sheet.dart`), parses **`flux://setup?id=<controllerId>&psk=<hex32>`** or raw hex (L33–43), `ControllerSettings.savePsk`, `hub.refreshConfiguredState()` + `hub.reconnect()`, snackbar feedback. Note: this is a *custom URL scheme in a QR code*, parsed manually with `Uri.tryParse` — **not** an OS-registered deep link.
3. **Auto-adoption** — devices appearing in `GET /devices` are silently added by `_reconcileWithController` (`device_provider.dart:399–429`). If the controller brokers Home Connect, appliances would *appear by themselves* with no app changes beyond type/icon/category.

### Where a "connect a cloud account" flow would naturally live
Ranked by fit with existing conventions:

1. **Mirroring Modbus exactly**: a `HomeConnectDevicesScreen` under `lib/ui/screens/settings/`, launched from a new card row. But note *where* Modbus is surfaced — inside the **Energy** category, not Settings, because that's where its devices are conceptually. Appliances aren't primarily energy, so a new **Appliances** `HomeCategory` with its own setup card (copying `_EnergySetupCard`, `category_screen.dart:81`) is the most idiomatic home.
2. **Main Settings** — `settings_screen.dart` is explicitly reserved for the controller ("the phone itself has nothing the user needs to configure", L18–20). Adding an account panel there breaks that stated intent, *unless* the account genuinely belongs to the phone (i.e. app-side OAuth), in which case a new `ACCOUNTS` panel next to `CONTROLLER`/`ABOUT` (L37/L63) is the obvious slot — the `_label`/`_card`/`_navTile` helpers (L75–94) make it a ~10-line addition.
3. **Home FAB** — currently a strict binary (`_addHub` / `_addDevice`, `home_screen.dart:42–48`). If "add device" should offer a choice (Matter QR vs cloud account vs Modbus), this becomes a picker bottom sheet. There's an existing pattern to copy: the BLE/IP method sheet at `commission_screen.dart:1981–2040`.
4. **Router** — add a `GoRoute` in `router.dart` (~L44) if the flow should be deep-linkable/back-stackable, which matters if OAuth redirects re-enter the app.

Whichever you pick, the mandatory finish is `await context.read<DeviceProvider>().syncWithController()` (the Modbus screen does this at L132 and L161) if the controller owns the device, or a new `registerXDevice()` on `DeviceProvider` if the app does.

---

## 6. OAuth / web-auth / secrets — currently **nothing**

### pubspec.yaml
`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/pubspec.yaml` — full dependency list (16 packages):
`flutter_zxing ^2.2.1`, `go_router ^17.3.0`, `coap ^9.2.1`, `dtls2 ^0.18.1`, `http ^1.2.2`, `crypto ^3.0.0`, `package_info_plus ^10.1.0`, `permission_handler ^12.0.3`, `provider ^6.1.2`, `qr_flutter ^4.1.0`, `shared_preferences ^2.3.3`, `multicast_dns ^0.3.3`, `protobuf ^6.0.0`, `fixnum ^1.1.0`, `uuid ^4.5.1`, `connectivity_plus ^6.1.0`. Dev: `flutter_test`, `integration_test`, `very_good_analysis ^10.2.0`.

**Absent — every single one you asked about:**
- ❌ `url_launcher`
- ❌ `webview_flutter`
- ❌ `flutter_web_auth` / `flutter_web_auth_2`
- ❌ `app_links` / `uni_links`
- ❌ `flutter_secure_storage`
- ❌ any OAuth/OIDC client (`oauth2`, `openid_client`, …)
- ❌ `flutter_appauth`

The only outbound-HTTP consumer is `http` used in exactly one file: `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/flux_rendezvous.dart:6`. Everything else is CoAP/DTLS. A repo-wide grep for `oauth|cloud|token|bosch|siemens|homeconnect` across `lib/`, `docs/*.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `flux-interface/` returns only: vendor-name table entry `0x1209: 'Bosch'` (`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/matter_vendors.dart:41`), Matter's `UpdateToken` OTA command name, and `PricingConfig.api_token` (ENTSO-E day-ahead prices — `flux-interface/proto/flux.proto:494`, a controller-side field). **No prior art whatsoever.**

### Deep links / custom URL schemes
**None registered on either platform.**

`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:
- `MainActivity` has exactly one `<intent-filter>` — `MAIN` + `LAUNCHER`. **No `VIEW`/`BROWSABLE` filter, no `<data android:scheme=…>`, no App Links.** `launchMode="singleTop"`.
- Permissions: CAMERA, the BLE set, fine/coarse LOCATION, Wi-Fi/network state + INTERNET + `CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE`, FOREGROUND_SERVICE (+ `_CONNECTED_DEVICE`), POST_NOTIFICATIONS.
- Deliberately removes `com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID` via `tools:node="remove"` (long comment about Play Console's AD_ID detector) — relevant precedent: this team cares about not tripping store scanners, and adding a webview/browser-based login has store-policy implications.
- One service: `.MatterForegroundService` (`foregroundServiceType="connectedDevice"`).

`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/ios/Runner/Info.plist`:
- **No `CFBundleURLTypes`** at all → no custom scheme; also no `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes`, no Associated Domains (check `ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements` too — nothing referenced from the plist).
- Usage strings: `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription`, `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`, `NSCameraUsageDescription`. `NSBonjourServices` = `_meshcop._udp`, `_matterc._udp`.

So an OAuth authorization-code flow with a redirect back into the app requires **new platform config on both sides** (Android `<intent-filter>` with `VIEW`+`BROWSABLE`+`<data scheme="…">` or an App Link; iOS `CFBundleURLTypes` or Associated Domains) plus a new dependency (`flutter_web_auth_2` / `url_launcher`+`app_links` / `webview_flutter`). Note the app already uses `flux://setup` as a *QR payload* scheme (`add_controller_flow.dart:33`) — an obvious naming precedent (`flux://homeconnect/callback`) but currently unregistered with the OS.

### How secrets are stored today
`/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/services/controller_settings.dart` — **plain `SharedPreferences`, no encryption, no Keychain/Keystore.** All static methods, keys namespaced per controller id (the mDNS hostname):

```dart
static const _kPsk      = 'ctrl_psk';       // :8  hex32 keyed by controller ID
static const _kDtlsId   = 'ctrl_dtls_id';   // :9
static const _kRzvUrl   = 'ctrl_rzv_url';   // :10 rendezvous URL (ADR-0006)
static const _kStun     = 'ctrl_stun';      // :11 (ADR-0007)
static const _kTurn     = 'ctrl_turn';      // :12 (ADR-0004)
static const _kTurnUser = 'ctrl_turn_user'; // :13
static const _kTurnPass = 'ctrl_turn_pass'; // :14
```
The **16-byte DTLS PSK** is stored as a 32-char hex string under `ctrl_psk_<hostname>` — `savePsk` L38 (`assert(psk.length == 16)`), `loadPsk` L19. TURN long-term credentials in cleartext too (`saveTurn` L119). Also `hasAnyPsk()` L32 (drives "is a hub configured"), `clearPsk` L50, `clearController` L58, `clearAllControllers` L72 (nukes all `ctrl_*`), `loadDtlsId` L81, `firstControllerId` L141.

Two more things worth flagging for a security-sensitive addition:
- **A hardcoded dev PSK ships in the source** — `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/main.dart:34–46`: `const hubPskHex = 'a089ebcce62353bf5f84e4fb4855f7f0'` / `hubDtlsId = 'flux-controller-e25311'`, seeded under `if (kDebugMode)` with the comment "Gated to debug builds so it never ships". Convention exists, but it's a convention, not a guarantee.
- **`android:allowBackup="true"`** in the manifest — SharedPreferences (and thus the PSK) are backed up. There's even a `backup.ab` file in the repo root. An OAuth refresh token in SharedPreferences would inherit this exposure; `flutter_secure_storage` (Keystore/Keychain) would be the right call and would be the app's first use of it.

Also relevant: the product positioning is explicitly **no-cloud**. `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/settings/remote_access_screen.dart:9` — "Flux runs no cloud: the phone connects…" and L220 — "…cloud and keeps no account of yours — your phone connects…". `docs/ios-port-plan.md:15` — "App's value is standalone, local, no-cloud control." pubspec description: "Local, private, independent." A Home Connect integration is a direct tension with the stated product story, and there is user-facing copy that will need revisiting.

content.text:
Research complete. Here's the detailed report.

---

# 1. Modbus/SunSpec integration, end to end

## File layout (`firmware/main/modbus/`)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `flux_modbus.{c,h}` | Raw Modbus/TCP + Modbus/UDP MBAP framing directly over lwIP sockets — **no esp-modbus** (`firmware/main/modbus/flux_modbus.c:1-20` explains why: esp-modbus's background reconnect task flooded the default event loop and starved Thread/mDNS). One opaque handle per device (`struct flux_modbus_dev`, `flux_modbus.c:40-50`); TCP connects lazily, drops the socket on any failure. |
| `flux_modbus_frame.{c,h}` | MBAP frame build/parse. |
| `flux_sunspec.{c,h}` | SunSpec model-chain discovery + decode into `pv_value_t[PV_COUNT]`. |
| `flux_modbus_profile.{c,h}` | **The extension seam**: register-map → Matter-attribute mapping. |
| `flux_modbus_task.{c,h}` | Single poll task. |
| `flux_coap_modbus.c` | CoAP handlers (kept out of `flux_coap_handlers.c`, which is at the file-size canary). |

CMake registration: `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4` — `"modbus"` appears in **both** `SRC_DIRS` and `INCLUDE_DIRS`.

## Configuration surface

Proto (`proto/proto/flux.proto`):
```proto
// :308-317
message ModbusDeviceConfig {
    string        host         = 1;   // IP/hostname on the controller's LAN
    uint32        port         = 2;   // 0 = default 502
    uint32        unit_id      = 3;
    ModbusProfile profile      = 4;
    uint32          poll_seconds = 5; // 0 = profile default
    string          name         = 6;
    uint64          node_id      = 7; // 0 = controller assigns a synthetic node id
    ModbusTransport transport    = 8; // TCP (default) or UDP
}
```
- `ModbusProfile` `flux.proto:290-296` (SUNSPEC=0, UNKNOWN=1, VM3P75CT=2 — "SUNSPEC stays 0 for wire/NVS compatibility")
- `ModbusTransport` `flux.proto:300-303`; `ModbusCandidate` `:320-326`; `ModbusDiscovered` `:331-333`; `ModbusRawDump` `:342-351`
- nanopb bounds: `proto/proto/flux.options:75-84` (`host max_size:46`, `name max_size:64`, `candidates max_count:16`, `registers max_size:4096`)
- Important design note in `flux.proto:279-287`: only the *provisioning* messages are Modbus-specific — `Device` / `AttrsUpdate` / `DeviceStateEvent` are reused verbatim.

CoAP endpoints, registered in `firmware/main/coap/flux_coap.c:202-213`:
```
POST/DELETE modbus/devices     → hnd_modbus_devices_post / _delete
GET         modbus/discovered  → hnd_modbus_discovered_get
GET         modbus/rawdump     → hnd_modbus_rawdump_get
```

`hnd_modbus_devices_post` — `firmware/main/modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:50-128`:
1. `read_body` → `pb_decode(flux_ModbusDeviceConfig_fields)` (`:56-63`)
2. Profile whitelist (`:68-72`) and range validation **before** narrowing to `uint16/uint8` so port 70000 can't silently wrap (`:74-81`)
3. Copy into `flux_ModbusRecord`, `flux_modbus_upsert(&rec)` — assigns `node_id` when 0 (`:83-94`)
4. **Mirror into the Matter device table** so `GET /devices` lists it (`:106-121`): `d.device_type = flux_modbus_profile_device_type(profile)`, `vendor_id = 0xFFF1`, `product_id = 0x8000` (`:45-46`); rolls back the Modbus entry if `flux_device_upsert` fails (`:117`)
5. `flux_modbus_task_reload()` (`:123`), then `send_status(... 0, "ok")` — the assigned node_id is **not** returned; the app re-reads `/devices`.

## Persistence (NVS)

`firmware/main/matter/flux_state.c:786-979`, layout documented at `:788-795`:
- Namespace `"flux_mb"` (`:797`), keys `count` (u8), `id_ctr` (u64 monotonic), `mb_0..mb_N` (one `flux_ModbusRecord` blob each)
- Record struct: `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:173-182`; `FLUX_MODBUS_MAX 8` (`:155`), `FLUX_MODBUS_HOST_MAX 46` (`:156`)
- API: `flux_modbus_count/get/get_by_node/upsert/remove` (`flux_state.h:184-198`)
- Locking: `s_mb_mutex`, a **static** mutex created once at boot from `flux_state_init_factory_partition()` (`flux_state.c:52-56`, `804-810`) — never lazily (comment at `:719-722` explains the race that motivated this). `remove` compacts the slot array (`:959-970`); the monotonic `id_ctr` (not the slot index) backs the node_id so IDs survive compaction (`:876-882`).
- The `/devices` mirror lives in a separate namespace `"flux_dev"` (`flux_state.c:420`), `FLUX_DEVICES_MAX 32` (`flux_state.h:99`).

## Poll task

`firmware/main/modbus/flux_modbus_task.c`:
- `flux_modbus_task_start()` `:197-204` — **one** task, `xTaskCreate(modbus_task, "flux_modbus", 6144, NULL, 4, ...)`. Internal RAM stack, priority 4. No PSRAM here (PSRAM stacks are used elsewhere: energy-history worker `flux_coap_energy.c:395`, prices task `flux_prices.c:306`).
- Loop `:175-195`: 500 ms tick (`TASK_TICK_MS`), `flux_hangwatch_register("flux_modbus", 30 s)` + `flux_hangwatch_kick` each tick (`:181`, `:192`).
- Active set: `mb_active_t s_active[FLUX_MODBUS_MAX]` (`:31-45`), rebuilt wholesale from NVS on the `s_reload` flag (`:63-100`); `flux_modbus_task_reload()` just sets the volatile flag (`:206-209`) — no lock needed, no cross-task coap calls.
- Per-device poll `:104-171`: `flux_modbus_profile_poll()`; up to `POLL_RETRIES 2` immediate retries (skipped once `fail_count >= 5`, `:121`); exponential backoff capped at `MAX_BACKOFF_US = 120 s` (`:156-158`); socket teardown+reopen every 5th failure (`:165-170`).
- **Poll results → device state** (`:130-141`): each reading becomes `flux_events_emit_attr(node_id, rd[i].key, rd[i].which, bv, iv, lv)`; first success latches `established` and emits `DEVICE_EVENT_ESTABLISHED`; 3 consecutive failures emit `DEVICE_EVENT_RESUBSCRIBING` (hysteresis, `:149-154`).

## Profile / mapping seam

`firmware/main/modbus/flux_modbus_profile.h:35-43`:
```c
typedef struct {
    const char *key;    /* static attr key string, e.g. "activePower" */
    uint8_t     which;  /* 1=bool  2=int32  3=int64 (matches kAttrMap) */
    bool        bv; int32_t iv; int64_t lv;
} flux_modbus_reading_t;
#define FLUX_MODBUS_MAX_READINGS 6
```
- `flux_modbus_profile_create/destroy/poll/device_type/probe` (`:50-70`)
- `flux_modbus_profile.c:29` — device type presented is **`0x0510` Electrical Sensor**, not `0x0017` Solar Power, because the app renders the power card for `0x0510` (comment `:21-28`)
- Keys must match `kAttrMap` in `firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:72-110` exactly (`activePower`, `voltage`, `activeCurrent`, `cumulativeEnergyMwh`, `cumulativeEnergyExportedMwh`). Unmapped physical quantities (frequency, DC power, temperature, operating state) are deliberately dropped (`flux_modbus_profile.c:131-133`).
- Two profiles implemented: `sunspec_poll_map` (`:122-140`) and `vm3p75ct_poll_map` (`:82-106`, hand-written register map from datasheet).

Discovery (`flux_coap_modbus.c:182-441`) uses a `/24` TCP connect sweep + a paced Modbus/UDP liveness sweep, both on a spawned worker (`xTaskCreate(discover_worker, "mb_discover", 8192, ...)` `:532`) delivering via the CoAP separate-response mechanism.

---

# 2. Synthetic node IDs

## Naming + numeric convention

`firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:158-167`:
```c
#define FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE  0x0100000000000000ULL
#define flux_is_modbus_node(nid)  ((uint64_t)(nid) >= FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE)
```
The comment at `:158-165` documents the two constraints: far above the operational counter (which starts at `0x0003`, `flux_state.h:74-80`), and **bit 63 clear** — the phone app decodes `node_id` into a signed Dart int and hex-formats it for `?id=`; a negative value silently never matches.

Codified as an ADR: `docs/adr/0009-modbus-devices-as-synthetic-node-ids.md` — calls the bit-63-clear rule a **cross-repo contract** binding any *future* synthetic range (i.e. your Home Connect range too). Note `modbus_devices_plan.md:53` still documents the *original* `0xFFFFFFFF00000000` base; the ADR supersedes it.

## Is there a mixed registry?

Yes — **one** registry. `flux_DeviceRecord` in `"flux_dev"` holds Matter and Modbus devices alike (`flux_state.h:101-107`). `hnd_devices_get` (`firmware/main/coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:254-288`) has **zero** branching on node type: it enumerates `flux_device_get(i, &rec)` and fills `flux_Device`. Modbus entries also live in the separate `"flux_mb"` config registry; the two are kept in lockstep by both delete paths (`flux_coap_modbus.c:149-152` and `flux_coap_handlers.c:379-387`).

`flux_Device` / `DeviceList`: `flux.proto:244-257`; `ConnectivityState` `:237-242`.

## Attribute/reading reporting path

```
producer  →  flux_events_emit_attr()            events/flux_events.c:13-18
             (sink pointer, no CoAP dependency; ADR-0008)
sink      →  flux_coap_notify_attr()            coap/flux_coap_notify.c:486-505, sink table :545-554
queue     →  flux_coap_notify_queue (32 slots, malloc'd notify_t*)   flux_coap_internal.h:104-105
drain     →  flux_coap_drain_notify_queue()     flux_coap_notify.c:245-482  (on the CoAP task, every ≤50 ms)
             NOTIFY_TYPE_ATTR   → pending merge + cache upsert (:254-259)
             NOTIFY_TYPE_DEVICE_EVENT → connectivity state machine (:269-296)
             → coap_resource_notify_observers(s_events_resource) (:478)
observe   →  hnd_events_get()                   flux_coap_handlers.c:1013-1086
```
- `hnd_events_get` sends the **full cached attribute set** rather than deltas (rationale at `:1041-1051`), capped at 32 to match `flux.options:88`.
- Protos: `Attr` `flux.proto:357-364` (key + oneof bool/sint32/sint64), `AttrsUpdate` `:367-370`, `DeviceStateEvent` `:383-388`, `DeviceEventType` `:374-380`.
- Caches (CoAP-task-owned, fixed size): `MAX_NODE_STATES 32`, `MAX_PENDING_ATTRS 16`, `ATTR_CACHE_MAX_NODES 32`, `ATTR_CACHE_MAX_ATTRS 32` — `flux_coap_notify.c:31-43`. `flux_coap_node_forget()` (`:117-133`) swap-removes on delete/fatal error; the comment explains the bug where 32 lifetime node IDs permanently exhausted the table (every Modbus re-add mints a fresh ID).
- One cross-task reader: `flux_coap_energy_snapshot()` (`:160-183`) under `s_cache_mux`.
- Polling read paths: `GET /devices/attrs?id=` → `hnd_attrs_get` (`flux_coap_handlers.c:557`); `GET /devices/clusters?id=` branches for synthetic nodes at `flux_coap_handlers.c:477-483` → `flux_modbus_synth_cluster_dump()` (`flux_coap_modbus.c:160-180`), which fabricates BasicInformation (0x0028) + Descriptor (0x001D) JSON from the registry.

---

# 3. Command path

```
POST /command   →  hnd_command_post()               coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:1090-1127
                   pb_decode(flux_DeviceCommand_fields)
                   → flux_send_device_command_args(node_id, endpoint, cluster, command, args, n)
                   → BoolResult{success, "err=%d"}
```
- `DeviceCommand` `flux.proto:408-414`; `CommandArg` `:395-404` (`tag` is the Matter TLV field tag; `name` is log-only). Caps: `args max_count:8`, `str_val max_size:64` (`flux.options:94-98`).
- `read_body` rejects bodies > 4096 B (`flux_coap_handlers.c:153-165`).

## The dispatch layer — precise answer

**There is no abstraction, vtable, or dispatch table.** `POST /command` calls exactly one function, which is Matter-specific, and the *only* routing is a single early-return guard:

> `firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:995`
> ```c
> /* Modbus devices are not Matter nodes — there is no CASE session to invoke
>  * a command on. Read-only for now (see modbus_devices_plan.md). */
> if (flux_is_modbus_node(node_id)) return ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED;
> ```
> inside `flux_send_device_command_args()` at `flux_controller.cpp:985-1073`.

The same one-line guard pattern repeats everywhere Matter is assumed:

| file:line | function |
|---|---|
| `flux_controller.cpp:995` | `flux_send_device_command_args` (POST /command) |
| `flux_controller.cpp:1081` | `flux_send_read_request` (POST /read) |
| `flux_controller.cpp:1126` | `flux_send_write_request` (POST /write) |
| `flux_controller.cpp:469` | `flux_device_fetch_metadata` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:513` | `flux_device_remove_fabric` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:666` | `flux_read_cluster_dump` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:787` | `flux_device_open_commissioning_window` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:849` | `flux_device_subscribe` |
| `flux_coap_handlers.c:477` | `hnd_clusters_get` (only CoAP-level branch that *does* something) |
| `flux_coap_handlers.c:384` | `hnd_devices_delete` (registry lockstep) |

So: **Modbus devices are read-only today.** `/command`, `/read`, `/write` return `ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED` → `BoolResult{success:false, error:"err=262"}`. `modbus_devices_plan.md:26` records this as the deliberate decision and calls the short-circuit "the future write hook".

**Implication for Home Connect:** commanding a non-Matter device requires introducing the dispatch layer that does not exist yet. The cleanest seam that matches the repo's own architecture (ADR-0008's "domain emits, transport subscribes" direction) would be a *downward* dispatch module — e.g. a `flux_device_command_route(node_id, ...)` in a neutral location that switches on the node-ID range and calls `flux_send_device_command_args` (Matter) or a new backend — because putting the Home Connect branch inside `flux_controller.cpp` would re-introduce a Matter→cloud dependency.

---

# 4. Energy roles / classes

## Assignment and storage

- `EnergyClass` `flux.proto:461-467` (UNKNOWN/GRID/PV/LOAD/BATTERY); `EnergyRoleEntry` / `EnergyRoleMap` `:511-518` (UNKNOWN clears the override; the app sends the **full set**, replacing the stored map).
- `POST /energy/roles` → `hnd_energy_roles_post` `firmware/main/coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:324-359` (registered `flux_coap.c:219-221`).
- Storage: `flux_energy_roles_set()` / `flux_energy_role_of()` — `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.c:709-784`. One NVS blob `"energy_roles"` in namespace `"flux"` + a RAM cache, guarded by `s_roles_mutex` (created at boot, `:723-726`); cap `FLUX_ENERGY_ROLES_MAX 40` (`flux_state.h:138`); `cls==0` entries dropped (`:752`).
- Heuristic fallback + override precedence: `firmware/main/energy/flux_energy_log.c:39-70` — Modbus `VM3P75CT → "grid"`, `SUNSPEC → "pv"`, any Matter device → `"load"`; then `flux_energy_role_of()` **wins** if set (`:68-69`).

## History aggregation

- Sampling: `energy_task` `flux_energy_log.c:146-160` every `FLUX_ENERGY_SAMPLE_SEC = 10` s (`flux_energy_log.h:22`) snapshots the CoAP attr cache (`flux_coap_energy_snapshot`) and appends CSV rows to `/sdcard/energy/YYYYMMDD.csv` (columns enumerated `flux_energy_log.h:26-38`; `device_class` and `source` are the classification columns).
- Aggregation: `firmware/main/energy/flux_coap_energy.c` — `aggregate()` `:220-300`, `route()` `:97-122` (differences cumulative counters per bucket; PV sums import+export because a plug and an inverter use opposite counters, `:106-112`).
- `EnergyDeviceSeries` `flux.proto:485-490`, emitted in `process_row()` `flux_coap_energy.c:170-179` and filled in `close_bucket()` `:132-136`. **PV only**, capped at `ENERGY_MAX_SERIES 6` (`:46` / `flux.options:120`); dense (`wh_count == buckets_count`). `series=0` query param skips it (`:516`).
- Delivered via the PSRAM-stack worker + block2 cache pattern (`:328-402`, `:404-456`).
- Pure bucket math extracted for host tests: `flux_energy_agg.{c,h}` (ADR-0010).

## Load control / scheduling — none exists

- `flux_prices_at(int64_t epoch, int32_t *ueur_per_kwh)` is defined at `firmware/main/prices/flux_prices.c:354-369` and declared at `flux_prices.h:40`, and has **zero callers anywhere in the firmware** (verified by repo-wide grep — only the definition, the declaration, and a comment in `flux_prices_awattar.c:34`).
- No scheduler, no deferrable-load logic, no price-triggered writes/commands. The controller fetches, caches, and exposes prices only.
- Roadmap: `docs/epex-day-ahead-pricing.md:118-122` — "**2. Act** — price-aware scheduling on top of the energy-role system (`flux_energy_role_of`): charge the battery in the cheapest N hours, defer flexible loads." `README.md` marks phase 2 as *not yet implemented*.

---

# 5. Outbound internet capability

## The HTTPS client

`firmware/main/prices/flux_prices_http.c` — 88 lines, the whole outbound HTTP surface for prices:
```c
// :53-60
esp_http_client_config_t cfg = {
    .url               = url,
    .event_handler     = on_evt,
    .user_data         = &acc,
    .crt_bundle_attach = esp_crt_bundle_attach,
    .timeout_ms        = 15000,
    .method            = HTTP_METHOD_GET,
};
```
- **TLS verification:** Mozilla CA bundle via `esp_crt_bundle_attach` (`:10`, `:57`). `firmware/sdkconfig:2048-2054` → `CONFIG_MBEDTLS_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE=y`, `..._DEFAULT_FULL=y`, `MAX_CERTS=200`. **No certificate pinning, no client certificate, no mTLS.** Header contract at `flux_prices_http.h:1-6`.
- **Body limits:** accumulator `accum_t` (`:15-21`) grows by doubling from 4096 up to a caller-supplied `max`, sets `oom` past it (`:29-39`); caller cap `AWATTAR_MAX_BODY = 64 * 1024` (`flux_prices_awattar.c:23`). Non-2xx → `ESP_FAIL` (`:78-82`); over-cap → `ESP_ERR_NO_MEM` (`:73-77`).
- GET only — no POST/PUT helper exists, no header-setting API. A cloud API needing POST + `Authorization` headers needs a new/extended helper.

## cJSON usage pattern

`firmware/main/prices/flux_prices_awattar.c:53-90` is the canonical example: `cJSON_Parse(body)` → `free(body)` immediately → `cJSON_GetObjectItem` + `cJSON_IsNumber/IsArray` type guards → clamp before narrowing (`:85-88`) → single `cJSON_Delete(root)` (`:90`). cJSON is also used in `flux_controller.cpp:1200-1250` for cluster-dump rendering.

Provider abstraction worth copying: `flux_prices_provider.h:18-33` — a `const` struct with `name` + `fetch()`, registry array in `flux_prices.c:41-52`, lookup by config string `:46-52`. "Add a source by dropping a new `flux_prices_<name>.c` and registering its struct."

## Other outbound HTTPS

Exactly one other place: `firmware/main/remote/flux_remote_rendezvous.c` — GET poll at `:72-104` and POST at `:112-124`, both with `.crt_bundle_attach = esp_crt_bundle_attach` (`:74`, `:113`). It does set `Content-Type` and a POST field (`:116-117`), so it's the closest thing to a POST template. Note: `RemoteConfig.rendezvous_cert_pin` exists in the proto (`flux.proto:568`) but grep finds **no firmware consumer** — pinning is specified, not implemented.

## OAuth2 / bearer / refresh tokens

**None. Anywhere.** Repo-wide grep for `oauth|OAuth|bearer|Bearer|access_token|refresh_token` across `firmware/main` returns zero hits. There is no token store, no refresh timer, no expiry tracking, no `Authorization` header being set. This is the biggest genuinely new piece for Home Connect.

## Secrets storage

| NVS namespace / partition | Contents | Defined at |
|---|---|---|
| `"flux"` (default `nvs` part.) | raw fabric id, IPK, thread TLV, `energy_roles` | `flux_state.c:33` |
| `"flux_dev"` | device registry | `flux_state.c:420` |
| `"flux_mb"` | Modbus configs + id counter | `flux_state.c:797` |
| `"flux_price"` | `PricingConfig` + cached `PriceCurve` (nanopb blobs) — includes `api_token` | `flux_prices.c:25` |
| `"flux_remote"` | `RemoteConfig` blob — includes TURN `username`/`credential` | `flux_remote.c:9` |
| `"flux_c6"` | C6 image state | `c6_flasher.c:33` |
| partition `flux_factory` | DTLS PSK, serial number, RCAC private key + cert, fabric-identity mirror | `flux_state.c:48`, `flux_state.h:12-20` |
| partition `matter_factory`, `matter_kvs` | CHIP factory / operational KVS | `firmware/partitions.csv:27-30` |

- Encryption: `firmware/partitions.csv:12-30` marks `nvs`, `nvs_keys`, `otadata`, `c6_image_*`, `matter_factory`, `flux_factory`, `matter_kvs` as `encrypted`, and the header comment (`:7-9`) warns `nvs_keys` **must exist from day one**. No `nvs_flash_secure_init` call in code — flash encryption is a release-build/eFuse step, not enabled in the current `sdkconfig`. Practically: **tokens stored in NVS today are plaintext on a dev unit.**
- `PricingConfig.api_token` (`flux.proto:550`, `max_size:80`) is the existing precedent for a persisted API credential — but note **no provider actually reads it** (only the CLI sets/displays it, `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/cli.py:1703`, `:1720`). It also round-trips over `GET /prices/config` in cleartext (`flux_coap_prices.c:44-59`) — a pattern you probably do *not* want to copy for a refresh token.

**Critical gotcha for a cloud subsystem doing both TLS and NVS:** `flux_prices.c:147-152` — the prices task runs on a **PSRAM** stack (32 KiB, `xTaskCreateWithCaps(..., MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM)`, `:306`) because a TLS handshake + 64 KB cJSON parse won't fit in internal RAM. But SPI-flash writes disable the CPU cache, which unmaps PSRAM → `esp_task_stack_is_sane_cache_disabled()` aborts the whole controller. So *every* NVS call is marshalled to a short-lived internal-RAM-stack worker with an internal-RAM source buffer (`nvs_blob_read_worker` `:94-122`, `nvs_blob_write_worker` `:161-197`), synchronised with `xTaskNotifyGive`/`ulTaskNotifyTake` rather than a caller-stack semaphore (P-CONC-9 note at `:109-114`). Any Home Connect task that does HTTPS *and* persists tokens hits this exact constraint.

---

# 6. Adding a new subsystem — the mechanics

## 1. CMake

`firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4` — add the directory name to **both** lists:
```cmake
idf_component_register(SRC_DIRS     "." "matter" "thread" "coap" "modbus" "energy"
                                    "prices" "remote" "platform" "events"
                       INCLUDE_DIRS "." "matter" "thread" "coap" "modbus" "energy"
                                    "prices" "remote" "platform" "events"
                       ...)
```
No per-file listing; `SRC_DIRS` globs. New managed-component deps go in `firmware/main/idf_component.yml`. `esp_http_client`/`esp_crt_bundle`/`cJSON` are already linked (prices + rendezvous use them), so an HTTPS+JSON subsystem needs **no new dependency**.

## 2. Proto workflow

1. Edit `proto/proto/flux.proto` (new messages/enums) and `proto/proto/flux.options` (every string/bytes/repeated field **must** get a `max_size`/`max_count` — the header says "No heap, no callbacks").
2. `cd proto && make c` → `proto/Makefile:33-42` runs protoc with `protoc-gen-nanopb` and `--options-path`, emitting `proto/generated/c/flux.pb.{c,h}`.
3. `make dart` (`Makefile:44-52`) for the app bindings — needs `protoc-gen-dart`, historically absent in this env (`modbus_devices_plan.md:130`).
4. `proto/CMakeLists.txt:6-15` registers the nanopb runtime + generated code as an IDF component; `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:14` links it (`target_link_libraries(... __idf_proto)`); include path added at `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:7-8`.
5. Regenerate Python bindings for the CLI/tests too: `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/flux_pb2.py` and `tests/integration/flux_pb2.py`.

## 3. CoAP handler registration

Three mechanical edits:
1. **Declare** the prototype in `firmware/main/coap/flux_coap_internal.h` — the handler-prototype block starts at `:203`; Modbus ones are `:279-294`, prices `:311-320`. Signature is always `(coap_resource_t*, coap_session_t*, const coap_pdu_t*, const coap_string_t*, coap_pdu_t*)`.
2. **Implement** in your own file (do not grow `flux_coap_handlers.c` — it's the 1221-line split canary; see `flux_coap_modbus.c:1-12` and `flux_coap_prices.c` as the two templates).
3. **Register** in `coap_task()` in `firmware/main/coap/flux_coap.c:159-271`:
```c
r = coap_resource_init(coap_make_str_const("modbus/devices"), 0);
coap_register_handler(r, COAP_REQUEST_POST,   hnd_modbus_devices_post);
coap_register_handler(r, COAP_REQUEST_DELETE, hnd_modbus_devices_delete);
coap_add_resource(ctx, r);
```
For an observable resource, use `COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_NON` + `coap_resource_set_get_observable(r, 1)` (see `:243-248`).

Reusable helpers (declared `flux_coap_internal.h:175-195`, defined in `flux_coap_handlers.c`): `read_body` (`:153`, 4096 B cap), `parse_id_query` (`:168`, hex `?id=`), `send_status` / `send_status_ex`, `coap_send_proto`, `coap_send_proto_block2`.

## 4. Boot wiring

`firmware/main/app_main.cpp:445-478` is the ordering-sensitive tail: create module mutexes *before* `flux_coap_start()` (`:452-455`, comment explains why), then `flux_coap_start()` (`:458`), then `flux_time_start()` / `flux_energy_log_start()` / `flux_hangwatch_start()` / `flux_prices_start()` / `flux_modbus_task_start()` (`:468-478`). Anything needing wall-clock time must start after `flux_time_start()` and gate on `flux_time_is_synced()` (as the prices task does, `flux_prices.c:260`).

## 5. Patterns you'll want to reuse

- **Event push:** emit via `flux_events_emit_attr` / `flux_events_emit_device` (`events/flux_events.h:26-31`); never include `flux_coap.h` from a producer (ADR-0008, `docs/adr/0008-flux-events-sole-producer-to-transport-path.md`).
- **Slow work off the CoAP task:** `coap_register_async` + worker + `notify_t` on `flux_coap_notify_queue` + async trigger. You'll need a new `NOTIFY_TYPE_*` (`flux_coap_internal.h:19-27`) or reuse the generic `NOTIFY_TYPE_MODBUS_DISCOVERED` proto-deliver path (`flux_coap_modbus.c:708` does exactly that for rawdump). ADR-0002 and ADR-0007.
- **Big responses:** PSRAM-stack worker + block2 cache keyed on the query (`flux_coap_energy.c:404-456`, `flux_coap_modbus.c:724-769`) — required because libcoap re-invokes the handler per block for async responses.
- **Liveness:** `flux_hangwatch_register(name, budget_us)` + `flux_hangwatch_kick(id)` in the loop.
- **Pure logic → host tests:** ADR-0010, `flux_energy_agg.c` + `test/host/test_energy.c`.
- **Test + CLI surface:** `tests/integration/test_modbus.py` and the `flux-ctl modbus` command group at `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/cli.py:1370-1500` (`add` / `ls` / `rm`) are the templates.
- **Repo conventions:** `.agents/skills/fw-engineer/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/build/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/fw-review/SKILL.md`; ADR index in `docs/adr/`.

---

## Summary of the reusable pattern for Home Connect

The Modbus integration is genuinely a clean template for **read/telemetry**: allocate a new synthetic node-ID range (bit 63 clear — ADR-0009's cross-repo contract), persist configs in a new NVS namespace with a static mutex, mirror each device into the shared `"flux_dev"` registry with a Matter `device_type` the app already renders, and push readings through `flux_events_emit_attr` under existing `kAttrMap` keys.

Three things it does **not** give you:
1. **A command path.** `flux_send_device_command_args` (`flux_controller.cpp:985`) is Matter-only with a one-line reject at `:995`; the vtable/dispatch layer would have to be created.
2. **Any OAuth2/token machinery.** Zero prior art; `PricingConfig.api_token` is a static-token placeholder that no provider even reads and is echoed in cleartext over `GET /prices/config`.
3. **Any scheduling/load-control.** `flux_prices_at()` has no callers; "act on price" is documented phase 2 (`docs/epex-day-ahead-pricing.md:118-122`) and unimplemented.

Nothing was modified.

# 1. Modbus/SunSpec integration, end to end

## File layout (`firmware/main/modbus/`)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `flux_modbus.{c,h}` | Raw Modbus/TCP + Modbus/UDP MBAP framing directly over lwIP sockets — **no esp-modbus** (`firmware/main/modbus/flux_modbus.c:1-20` explains why: esp-modbus's background reconnect task flooded the default event loop and starved Thread/mDNS). One opaque handle per device (`struct flux_modbus_dev`, `flux_modbus.c:40-50`); TCP connects lazily, drops the socket on any failure. |
| `flux_modbus_frame.{c,h}` | MBAP frame build/parse. |
| `flux_sunspec.{c,h}` | SunSpec model-chain discovery + decode into `pv_value_t[PV_COUNT]`. |
| `flux_modbus_profile.{c,h}` | **The extension seam**: register-map → Matter-attribute mapping. |
| `flux_modbus_task.{c,h}` | Single poll task. |
| `flux_coap_modbus.c` | CoAP handlers (kept out of `flux_coap_handlers.c`, which is at the file-size canary). |

CMake registration: `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4` — `"modbus"` appears in **both** `SRC_DIRS` and `INCLUDE_DIRS`.

## Configuration surface

Proto (`proto/proto/flux.proto`):
```proto
// :308-317
message ModbusDeviceConfig {
    string        host         = 1;   // IP/hostname on the controller's LAN
    uint32        port         = 2;   // 0 = default 502
    uint32        unit_id      = 3;
    ModbusProfile profile      = 4;
    uint32          poll_seconds = 5; // 0 = profile default
    string          name         = 6;
    uint64          node_id      = 7; // 0 = controller assigns a synthetic node id
    ModbusTransport transport    = 8; // TCP (default) or UDP
}
```
- `ModbusProfile` `flux.proto:290-296` (SUNSPEC=0, UNKNOWN=1, VM3P75CT=2 — "SUNSPEC stays 0 for wire/NVS compatibility")
- `ModbusTransport` `flux.proto:300-303`; `ModbusCandidate` `:320-326`; `ModbusDiscovered` `:331-333`; `ModbusRawDump` `:342-351`
- nanopb bounds: `proto/proto/flux.options:75-84` (`host max_size:46`, `name max_size:64`, `candidates max_count:16`, `registers max_size:4096`)
- Important design note in `flux.proto:279-287`: only the *provisioning* messages are Modbus-specific — `Device` / `AttrsUpdate` / `DeviceStateEvent` are reused verbatim.

CoAP endpoints, registered in `firmware/main/coap/flux_coap.c:202-213`:
```
POST/DELETE modbus/devices     → hnd_modbus_devices_post / _delete
GET         modbus/discovered  → hnd_modbus_discovered_get
GET         modbus/rawdump     → hnd_modbus_rawdump_get
```

`hnd_modbus_devices_post` — `firmware/main/modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:50-128`:
1. `read_body` → `pb_decode(flux_ModbusDeviceConfig_fields)` (`:56-63`)
2. Profile whitelist (`:68-72`) and range validation **before** narrowing to `uint16/uint8` so port 70000 can't silently wrap (`:74-81`)

## Persistence (NVS)

`firmware/main/matter/flux_state.c:786-979`, layout documented at `:788-795`:
- Namespace `"flux_mb"` (`:797`), keys `count` (u8), `id_ctr` (u64 monotonic), `mb_0..mb_N` (one `flux_ModbusRecord` blob each)
- Record struct: `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:173-182`; `FLUX_MODBUS_MAX 8` (`:155`), `FLUX_MODBUS_HOST_MAX 46` (`:156`)
- API: `flux_modbus_count/get/get_by_node/upsert/remove` (`flux_state.h:184-198`)
- Locking: `s_mb_mutex`, a **static** mutex created once at boot from `flux_state_init_factory_partition()` (`flux_state.c:52-56`, `804-810`) — never lazily (comment at `:719-722` explains the race that motivated this). `remove` compacts the slot array (`:959-970`); the monotonic `id_ctr` (not the slot index) backs the node_id so IDs survive compaction (`:876-882`).

## Poll task

`firmware/main/modbus/flux_modbus_task.c`:
- `flux_modbus_task_start()` `:197-204` — **one** task, `xTaskCreate(modbus_task, "flux_modbus", 6144, NULL, 4, ...)`. Internal RAM stack, priority 4. No PSRAM here (PSRAM stacks are used elsewhere: energy-history worker `flux_coap_energy.c:395`, prices task `flux_prices.c:306`).
- Loop `:175-195`: 500 ms tick (`TASK_TICK_MS`), `flux_hangwatch_register("flux_modbus", 30 s)` + `flux_hangwatch_kick` each tick (`:181`, `:192`).
- Active set: `mb_active_t s_active[FLUX_MODBUS_MAX]` (`:31-45`), rebuilt wholesale from NVS on the `s_reload` flag (`:63-100`); `flux_modbus_task_reload()` just sets the volatile flag (`:206-209`) — no lock needed, no cross-task coap calls.
- Per-device poll `:104-171`: `flux_modbus_profile_poll()`; up to `POLL_RETRIES 2` immediate retries (skipped once `fail_count >= 5`, `:121`); exponential backoff capped at `MAX_BACKOFF_US = 120 s` (`:156-158`); socket teardown+reopen every 5th failure (`:165-170`).
- **Poll results → device state** (`:130-141`): each reading becomes `flux_events_emit_attr(node_id, rd[i].key, rd[i].which, bv, iv, lv)`; first success latches `established` and emits `DEVICE_EVENT_ESTABLISHED`; 3 consecutive failures emit `DEVICE_EVENT_RESUBSCRIBING` (hysteresis, `:149-154`).

`firmware/main/modbus/flux_modbus_profile.h:35-43`:

# 2. Synthetic node IDs

## Naming + numeric convention

`firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:158-167`:
```c
#define FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE  0x0100000000000000ULL
#define flux_is_modbus_node(nid)  ((uint64_t)(nid) >= FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE)
```
The comment at `:158-165` documents the two constraints: far above the operational counter (which starts at `0x0003`, `flux_state.h:74-80`), and **bit 63 clear** — the phone app decodes `node_id` into a signed Dart int and hex-formats it for `?id=`; a negative value silently never matches.

Codified as an ADR: `docs/adr/0009-modbus-devices-as-synthetic-node-ids.md` — calls the bit-63-clear rule a **cross-repo contract** binding any *future* synthetic range (i.e. your Home Connect range too). Note `modbus_devices_plan.md:53` still documents the *original* `0xFFFFFFFF00000000` base; the ADR supersedes it.

## Is there a mixed registry?

Yes — **one** registry. `flux_DeviceRecord` in `"flux_dev"` holds Matter and Modbus devices alike (`flux_state.h:101-107`). `hnd_devices_get` (`firmware/main/coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:254-288`) has **zero** branching on node type: it enumerates `flux_device_get(i, &rec)` and fills `flux_Device`. Modbus entries also live in the separate `"flux_mb"` config registry; the two are kept in lockstep by both delete paths (`flux_coap_modbus.c:149-152` and `flux_coap_handlers.c:379-387`).

`flux_Device` / `DeviceList`: `flux.proto:244-257`; `ConnectivityState` `:237-242`.

## Attribute/reading reporting path

```
producer  →  flux_events_emit_attr()            events/flux_events.c:13-18
             (sink pointer, no CoAP dependency; ADR-0008)
sink      →  flux_coap_notify_attr()            coap/flux_coap_notify.c:486-505, sink table :545-554
queue     →  flux_coap_notify_queue (32 slots, malloc'd notify_t*)   flux_coap_internal.h:104-105
drain     →  flux_coap_drain_notify_queue()     flux_coap_notify.c:245-482  (on the CoAP task, every ≤50 ms)
             NOTIFY_TYPE_ATTR   → pending merge + cache upsert (:254-259)
             NOTIFY_TYPE_DEVICE_EVENT → connectivity state machine (:269-296)
             → coap_resource_notify_observers(s_events_resource) (:478)
observe   →  hnd_events_get()                   flux_coap_handlers.c:1013-1086
```
- `hnd_events_get` sends the **full cached attribute set** rather than deltas (rationale at `:1041-1051`), capped at 32 to match `flux.options:88`.
- Protos: `Attr` `flux.proto:357-364` (key + oneof bool/sint32/sint64), `AttrsUpdate` `:367-370`, `DeviceStateEvent` `:383-388`, `DeviceEventType` `:374-380`.
- Caches (CoAP-task-owned, fixed size): `MAX_NODE_STATES 32`, `MAX_PENDING_ATTRS 16`, `ATTR_CACHE_MAX_NODES 32`, `ATTR_CACHE_MAX_ATTRS 32` — `flux_coap_notify.c:31-43`. `flux_coap_node_forget()` (`:117-133`) swap-removes on delete/fatal error; the comment explains the bug where 32 lifetime node IDs permanently exhausted the table (every Modbus re-add mints a fresh ID).
- One cross-task reader: `flux_coap_energy_snapshot()` (`:160-183`) under `s_cache_mux`.
- Polling read paths: `GET /devices/attrs?id=` → `hnd_attrs_get` (`flux_coap_handlers.c:557`); `GET /devices/clusters?id=` branches for synthetic nodes at `flux_coap_handlers.c:477-483` → `flux_modbus_synth_cluster_dump()` (`flux_coap_modbus.c:160-180`), which fabricates BasicInformation (0x0028) + Descriptor (0x001D) JSON from the registry.

# 3. Command path

```
POST /command   →  hnd_command_post()               coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:1090-1127
                   pb_decode(flux_DeviceCommand_fields)
                   → flux_send_device_command_args(node_id, endpoint, cluster, command, args, n)
                   → BoolResult{success, "err=%d"}
```
- `DeviceCommand` `flux.proto:408-414`; `CommandArg` `:395-404` (`tag` is the Matter TLV field tag; `name` is log-only). Caps: `args max_count:8`, `str_val max_size:64` (`flux.options:94-98`).
- `read_body` rejects bodies > 4096 B (`flux_coap_handlers.c:153-165`).

## The dispatch layer — precise answer

**There is no abstraction, vtable, or dispatch table.** `POST /command` calls exactly one function, which is Matter-specific, and the *only* routing is a single early-return guard:

> `firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:995`
> ```c
> /* Modbus devices are not Matter nodes — there is no CASE session to invoke
>  * a command on. Read-only for now (see modbus_devices_plan.md). */
> if (flux_is_modbus_node(node_id)) return ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED;
> ```
> inside `flux_send_device_command_args()` at `flux_controller.cpp:985-1073`.

The same one-line guard pattern repeats everywhere Matter is assumed:

| file:line | function |
|---|---|
| `flux_controller.cpp:995` | `flux_send_device_command_args` (POST /command) |
| `flux_controller.cpp:1081` | `flux_send_read_request` (POST /read) |
| `flux_controller.cpp:1126` | `flux_send_write_request` (POST /write) |
| `flux_controller.cpp:469` | `flux_device_fetch_metadata` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:513` | `flux_device_remove_fabric` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:666` | `flux_read_cluster_dump` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:787` | `flux_device_open_commissioning_window` |
| `flux_controller.cpp:849` | `flux_device_subscribe` |
| `flux_coap_handlers.c:477` | `hnd_clusters_get` (only CoAP-level branch that *does* something) |
| `flux_coap_handlers.c:384` | `hnd_devices_delete` (registry lockstep) |

So: **Modbus devices are read-only today.** `/command`, `/read`, `/write` return `ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED` → `BoolResult{success:false, error:"err=262"}`. `modbus_devices_plan.md:26` records this as the deliberate decision and calls the short-circuit "the future write hook".

**Implication for Home Connect:** commanding a non-Matter device requires introducing the dispatch layer that does not exist yet. The cleanest seam that matches the repo's own architecture (ADR-0008's "domain emits, transport subscribes" direction) would be a *downward* dispatch module — e.g. a `flux_device_command_route(node_id, ...)` in a neutral location that switches on the node-ID range and calls `flux_send_device_command_args` (Matter) or a new backend — because putting the Home Connect branch inside `flux_controller.cpp` would re-introduce a Matter→cloud dependency.
