I explored the controller, the shared proto, the Flutter app, and the local Matter 1.5 specs. Here is the plan.

---

# Home Connect integration — phased implementation plan

## 0. Decisions up front (the ones everything else follows from)

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Synthetic node IDs get a **kind nibble**: `kind = (nid >> 56) & 0x7F`. Modbus stays `0x01…` (unchanged on the wire), Home Connect becomes `0x02…`. `flux_is_modbus_node` is redefined as `kind==1`, and a new `flux_is_synthetic_node()` replaces it at the ~10 "not a Matter node" guards. | Keeps bit 63 clear (FW-ADR-0009 contract) and, critically, keeps `flux_is_modbus_node` *meaning* Modbus. Today the app decodes `isModbus` as `nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000`, so an HC node would silently render as a Modbus device. |
| D2 | Two dedicated tasks, both on **PSRAM stacks**, and **neither ever touches NVS**. All persistence goes through a new `platform/flux_nvs_blob.c` (extracted verbatim from `prices/flux_prices.c:94-197`). | This is the abort-the-box hazard. Making it structurally impossible on the HC tasks is cheaper than remembering it. |
| D3 | **The access token is never persisted.** Only the refresh token is. | `partitions.csv` gives `nvs` only **0x6000 = 24 KiB**, shared with the device registry, Modbus registry, price curve and remote config. A ~1–2 KB access token rewritten daily is NVS churn for zero benefit — one refresh call at boot costs one request out of a ~500/day budget. |
| D4 | SSE and REST get **separate `esp_http_client` handles**. | One handle cannot hold a streaming response and serve a request. Sharing means a TLS handshake per REST call plus an event-blind window — exactly the churn Home Connect rate-limits. |
| D5 | Control uses **real Matter clusters where a faithful mapping exists** (OnOff, OperationalState 0x0060, the Mode clusters) and an **explicit `/homeconnect/command` endpoint where it doesn't** (StartInRelative, program options). Argued in §3.3. | |
| D6 | The **command dispatch layer is a new neutral module** `devices/flux_device_cmd.c` — the command-direction twin of `flux_events`. Matter and Home Connect each *register* a backend; neither includes the other. | Adding an HC branch inside `matter/flux_controller.cpp` would make `matter → homeconnect`, the exact inversion FW-ADR-0008 exists to prevent. |
| D7 | Price-aware scheduling lives in a **new `flexload/` subsystem**, not in `homeconnect/`. | The same policy must later drive battery charging and the wallbox (`flux-wallbox-simulator` exists). `homeconnect → prices` would bake the appliance assumption into the scheduler. |
| D8 | The hub **never starts an appliance on its own initiative — it only delays a run the user already asked for.** | This one sentence is the entire safety model and it is also the user-visible contract. |

---

## Phase 0 — prerequisites (small, independently mergeable, no new features)

Ship this first; it is all refactor and it is what makes Phases 1–3 safe.

### 0.1 Synthetic node-ID kinds + FW-ADR-0014

`firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:158-167` — replace the single base:

```c
#define FLUX_SYNTH_NODE_MIN     0x0100000000000000ULL
#define FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_SHIFT   56
#define FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_MODBUS  0x01
#define FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_CLOUD   0x02   /* Home Connect + future cloud appliances */
#define FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE   ((uint64_t)FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_MODBUS << FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_SHIFT)
#define FLUX_HC_NODE_BASE       ((uint64_t)FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_CLOUD  << FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_SHIFT)
#define flux_synth_kind(nid)        ((uint8_t)(((uint64_t)(nid) >> FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_SHIFT) & 0x7F))
#define flux_is_synthetic_node(nid) ((uint64_t)(nid) >= FLUX_SYNTH_NODE_MIN)
#define flux_is_modbus_node(nid)    (flux_synth_kind(nid) == FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_MODBUS)
#define flux_is_hc_node(nid)        (flux_synth_kind(nid) == FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_CLOUD)
```

Kind ≤ 0x7F ⇒ bit 63 is structurally clear, so the FW-ADR-0009 contract is enforced by construction rather than by a comment.

Call sites that mean "not a Matter node" and must become `flux_is_synthetic_node`:
`firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:469, 513, 666, 787, 849, 995, 1081, 1126`;
`firmware/main/coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:384` (becomes a kind switch for the synthesized cluster dump), `:477` (kind switch for registry cleanup);
`firmware/main/energy/flux_energy_log.c:44` (kind switch in `classify()`).
`firmware/main/modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:141` stays `flux_is_modbus_node` — it is genuinely a Modbus-only guard.

Write `docs/adr/0014-synthetic-node-id-kinds.md` (supersedes-adjacent to 0009; cite it from `flux_state.h`).

### 0.2 Cross-repo companions — **land these before Phase 1 firmware**

- `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart:125` — `isModbus` becomes kind-based; add `isHomeConnect`. `lib/providers/device_provider.dart:345,408` `NetworkType` likewise. This change is a no-op until HC nodes exist, so it can ship early and independently.
- `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/models/device_type.dart:145` — **`0x0073 => airQualitySensor` is wrong.** Verified in `23-27351-008_Matter-1.5-Device-Library-Specification.pdf`: `0x0073` is **Laundry Washer**; Air Quality Sensor is `0x002C` (already mapped on the line below). Left unfixed, every Home Connect washer renders as an air-quality sensor. Add `dishwasher 0x0075`, `laundryWasher 0x0073`, `laundryDryer 0x007C`, `refrigerator 0x0070`, `oven 0x007B`.
- `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/cli.py:1373` — the `modbus ls`/`modbus rm` filter becomes a **range** check (`FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE ≤ id < FLUX_HC_NODE_BASE`), else `modbus ls` lists appliances.
- `tests/integration/test_modbus.py:26` already carries a **stale, wrong** `MODBUS_NODE_BASE = 0xFFFFFFFF00000000` (and the same value in its docstring). Fix it in this pass or the new range tests get written against a fiction.

### 0.3 Extract the PSRAM-safe NVS helper

New `firmware/main/platform/flux_nvs_blob.{c,h}`:

```c
esp_err_t flux_nvs_blob_get(const char *ns, const char *key, void *out, size_t *len);
esp_err_t flux_nvs_blob_set(const char *ns, const char *key, const void *buf, size_t len);
esp_err_t flux_nvs_blob_erase(const char *ns, const char *key);
esp_err_t flux_nvs_u64_get(const char *ns, const char *key, uint64_t *out);
esp_err_t flux_nvs_u64_set(const char *ns, const char *key, uint64_t v);
```

Implementation is `flux_prices.c`'s pattern moved wholesale: an internal-RAM bounce buffer (`heap_caps_malloc(MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL|MALLOC_CAP_8BIT)`) plus a short-lived 4 KiB internal-stack worker task synchronised with `xTaskNotifyGive`/`ulTaskNotifyTake` (the P-CONC-9 handoff, *not* a caller-stack semaphore). Refactor `flux_prices.c` onto it — net LOC reduction and one canonical copy of the rule.

### 0.4 The command bus (needed by Phase 2, but land it here as a pure refactor)

New dir `firmware/main/devices/` (add to **both** `SRC_DIRS` and `INCLUDE_DIRS` in `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4`).

```c
/* devices/flux_device_cmd.h */
typedef struct {
    const char *name;   /* "matter" | "homeconnect" — logging only */
    uint8_t     kind;   /* 0 = real Matter node; else flux_synth_kind() */
    esp_err_t (*invoke)(uint64_t node_id, uint32_t endpoint_id, uint32_t cluster_id,
                        uint32_t command_id, const flux_CommandArg *args, size_t n);
    esp_err_t (*write)(uint64_t node_id, uint16_t endpoint_id, uint32_t cluster_id,
                       uint32_t attr_id, const char *value_json);
    esp_err_t (*read)(uint64_t node_id, const uint32_t *ep, size_t ep_n,
                      const uint32_t *cl, size_t cl_n, const uint32_t *at, size_t at_n);
    /* Phase 3. Arrange for the *already selected* program to begin in @delay_s
     * (0 = now). Idempotent: a second call replaces the pending delay.
     * ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED if the device cannot defer. */
    esp_err_t (*defer_start)(uint64_t node_id, uint32_t delay_s, uint32_t *granted_s);
} flux_device_backend_t;

void      flux_device_cmd_register(const flux_device_backend_t *b);  /* boot-only */
esp_err_t flux_device_cmd_invoke(/* same args as invoke */);
esp_err_t flux_device_cmd_write(/* … */);
esp_err_t flux_device_cmd_read(/* … */);
esp_err_t flux_device_cmd_defer_start(uint64_t node_id, uint32_t delay_s, uint32_t *granted_s);
```

- Registry is a fixed `static const flux_device_backend_t *s_backends[4]`, written boot-only single-threaded, read lock-free — the same justification `flux_events.c`'s plain-pointer sink already documents. Lookup by `flux_synth_kind(node_id)`; unknown kind ⇒ `ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, i.e. **outwardly identical to today's behaviour**.
- `matter/flux_controller.cpp` gains a ~20-line `flux_matter_cmd_register()` wrapping the existing three functions; the `flux_is_modbus_node` guards inside them become dead code (the bus never routes a synthetic id there) and are deleted.
- `coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:1090/1131/1173` call `flux_device_cmd_*` instead of `flux_send_*`.
- Direction: `coap → devices`, `matter → devices`, `homeconnect → devices`. No peer includes a peer. Write `docs/adr/0015-flux-device-cmd-sole-transport-to-device-command-path.md` and add `s_backends` to the ownership table in `docs/threading.md`.

Merge 0.4 **before** any HC code so the diff is reviewable as "zero behaviour change".

---

## Phase 1 — monitoring only

### 1.1 New files

`firmware/main/homeconnect/` (add `"homeconnect"` to both lists in `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt`):

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `flux_homeconnect.h` | Public API: `_init()`, `_start()`, `_reload()`, config get/set, appliance list, status, `flux_hc_node_for_haid()`. Documents the **no-NVS-on-hc-tasks** invariant. |
| `flux_homeconnect.c` | Module state + mutex, state machine, backoff/quota, task creation, resync orchestration (`hc_ctl` task). |
| `flux_hc_auth.c` | The **only** module that touches the token store. `POST {base}/security/oauth/token` `grant_type=refresh_token`. |
| `flux_hc_rest.c` | Bearer/Accept-aware GET/PUT/DELETE over `esp_http_client`; bounded heap body; quota guard gate; 429/`Retry-After` extraction. |
| `flux_hc_sse.c` | `hc_sse` task: open stream, read loop, hand frames to the parser. |
| `flux_hc_sse_parse.c/.h` | **Pure** incremental SSE framer (`event:`/`data:`/`id:`/blank line). ESP-IDF-free ⇒ host-testable (FW-ADR-0010). |
| `flux_hc_map.c/.h` | **Pure** HC key/value → flux attr key/`which`/value. The analogue of `flux_modbus_profile.c`. Host-testable. |
| `flux_hc_registry.c` | `haId ↔ node_id` registry in NVS ns `flux_hc`, mirroring `flux_state.c`'s Modbus-registry idiom (own mutex, monotonic id counter, compaction on remove). Deliberately **not** in `flux_state.c` — that file is at 979 lines, one line under the ~1000-line split canary. |
| `flux_coap_homeconnect.c` | CoAP handlers (new file; `flux_coap_handlers.c` is the canary). |

### 1.2 NVS layout — ns `"flux_hc"`

| Key | Type | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `cfg` | blob | nanopb `flux_HomeConnectConfig` **without** secrets |
| `sec` | blob | raw `{ char client_secret[128]; char refresh_token[512]; int64_t obtained_at; }` — separate key so the config path never rewrites it |
| `count` | u8 | appliance count (`FLUX_HC_MAX 8`) |
| `id_ctr` | u64 | monotonic suffix for synthetic node ids (stable across compaction) |
| `ha_0`…`ha_7` | blob | `flux_HcRecord { uint64_t node_id; char ha_id[48]; uint8_t type; char name[64]; char enumber[32]; uint8_t flags; }` |
| `blk` | u64 | `blocked_until` epoch — **persisted so a crash-loop cannot hammer the API** |
| `req_n` / `req_day` | u32 | daily request counter + the day it belongs to (coalesced to ≤1 write/60 s) |

Access token: RAM only (D3). Verify headroom with `nvs_get_stats()` before shipping; if it is tight, the honest answer is a hardware-revision partition change, not a bigger blob (a `partitions.csv` change cannot be delivered by OTA).

### 1.3 Device types + registry mirror

Verified against the 1.5 Device Library: **Dishwasher 0x0075, Laundry Washer 0x0073, Laundry Dryer 0x007C, Refrigerator 0x0070, Oven 0x007B, Robotic Vacuum 0x0074.** HC `type` string → device type; `WasherDryer` → 0x0073 with a comment; unknown → 0x0000 (still listed).

Mirror into `"flux_dev"` via `flux_device_upsert()` exactly as `flux_coap_modbus.c:104-122` does, with `vendor_id = 0xFFF1`, `product_id = 0x8001` (Modbus uses `0x8000`), and roll back the HC registry entry on "device table full" — same pattern, same reason. Brand/E-number go in `name` ("Bosch Dishwasher") and in the HC-specific appliance list.

`GET /devices/clusters?id=` for a `kind==2` node returns a synthesized dump from the registry (BasicInformation + Descriptor), i.e. an `flux_hc_synth_cluster_dump()` alongside `flux_modbus_synth_cluster_dump()`, selected by the kind switch at `flux_coap_handlers.c:384`.

### 1.4 Attribute keys — and a correction to the brief

**`kAttrMap` is not on this path.** `flux_events_emit_attr()` takes the key string directly (`events/flux_events.c:13-18`); `kAttrMap` (`matter/flux_controller.cpp:72-110`) only maps Matter `(cluster_id, attr_id) → key` inside `attr_report_cb`. Modbus works today without any `kAttrMap` change — its keys coincide with real Matter attributes by design. So Home Connect monitoring works with **zero** `kAttrMap` edits; what genuinely must be added on both sides is the **app** (`DeviceLiveData` accessors + `cluster_parser` renderers), because the app ignores unknown keys.

We still add the four `kAttrMap` entries below, because those `(cluster, attr)` pairs *genuinely* carry those values, so a real Matter dishwasher will emit identical keys. We deliberately do **not** invent cluster ids for the HC-only signals.

| HC key | flux attr key | `which` | Conversion | `kAttrMap` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BSH.Common.Status.OperationState` | `operationalState` | 2 | → Matter `OperationalStateEnum` (Inactive/Ready/Finished→`0` Stopped, Run→`1` Running, Pause→`2` Paused, Error/Aborting→`3` Error, **DelayedStart→`0x80`** flux-private) | `{0x0060,0x0004,"operationalState",2}` |
| `BSH.Common.Option.RemainingProgramTime` | `countdownTime` | 2 | seconds | `{0x0060,0x0002,"countdownTime",2}` |
| `BSH.Common.Root.ActiveProgram` / `.SelectedProgram` | `currentMode` | 2 | index into the appliance's program list | `{0x0059,0x0001,…}` + `{0x0051,0x0001,…}` (Dishwasher / Laundry Washer Mode — both map to the same key) |
| `BSH.Common.Setting.PowerState` | `onOff` | 1 | On→true; Off/Standby→false | existing `{0x0006,0x0000,"onOff",1}` |
| `BSH.Common.Option.ProgramProgress` | `programProgress` | 2 | percent | — |
| `BSH.Common.Option.ElapsedProgramTime` | `elapsedS` | 2 | seconds | — |
| `BSH.Common.Option.EstimatedTotalProgramTime` | `totalProgramTimeS` | 2 | seconds | — |
| `BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative` | `startInS` | 2 | seconds | — |
| `BSH.Common.Status.DoorState` | `applianceDoorOpen` | 1 | Open→true | — |
| `BSH.Common.Status.RemoteControlStartAllowed` | `remoteStartAllowed` | 1 | bool | — |
| `BSH.Common.Status.RemoteControlActive` | `remoteControlActive` | 1 | bool | — |
| SSE `CONNECTED`/`DISCONNECTED`/`PAIRED`/`DEPAIRED` | — | — | `flux_events_emit_device(ESTABLISHED / RESUBSCRIBING / ERROR)` | — |

All keys ≤ 19 chars, inside `flux.Attr.key max_size:32` and `notify_t.attr_key[36]`. Note the hard constraint that drove the `currentMode` design: **`Attr`'s oneof has no string type**, so a program *name* cannot travel on the attribute stream. Programs are enumerated once via `GET /homeconnect/programs?id=` and referenced by index — which is exactly how Matter's Mode Base cluster works (`SupportedModes` read separately, `CurrentMode` as a uint8).

### 1.5 Tasks, stacks, memory budget

| Task | Stack | Caps | Prio | Role | hangwatch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hc_ctl` | 20 KiB | `MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM` via `xTaskCreateWithCaps` | 3 | token refresh, REST resync, command execution, registry sync; owns the token store | 180 s |
| `hc_sse` | 16 KiB | `MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM` | 3 | one long-lived stream → `flux_events_emit_*` | 180 s (must exceed the 90 s read timeout) |
| `nvs_worker` | 4 KiB | internal | 4 | transient, one per `flux_nvs_blob_*` call | — |

Why PSRAM: TLS handshake against the **full 200-cert Mozilla bundle** (`CONFIG_MBEDTLS_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE_DEFAULT_FULL=y`) plus a cJSON parse, and internal RAM is the scarce resource (`CONFIG_SPIRAM_MALLOC_RESERVE_INTERNAL=32768`, `ALWAYSINTERNAL=16384`). `flux_prices` already set this precedent at 32 KiB PSRAM. **Consequence, stated as an invariant in `flux_homeconnect.h` and in `docs/threading.md`: no `nvs_*`, `esp_flash_*` or `esp_partition_*` on `hc_ctl`/`hc_sse` — SPI-flash writes disable the cache, which unmaps PSRAM and aborts the controller.**

Why two tasks rather than one: it is not only the shared-handle problem (D4). Splitting lets `hc_sse` be a pure consumer of a mutex-protected RAM token cache with **no** persistence path at all, so the PSRAM/NVS hazard is structurally impossible on the task most likely to be edited later.

TLS budget, from the actual `firmware/sdkconfig`:

- `CONFIG_MBEDTLS_ASYMMETRIC_CONTENT_LEN=y`, `IN=16384`, `OUT=4096`, and `CONFIG_MBEDTLS_EXTERNAL_MEM_ALLOC=y` ⇒ the ~20 KiB of record buffers per session lands in **PSRAM, not internal RAM**.
- Per session ≈ 20 KiB buffers + 2–4 KiB `mbedtls_ssl_context`/session + a transient peer-cert allocation ⇒ **≈24 KiB PSRAM held for the whole SSE lifetime**, and the same again transiently during each REST call.
- Plus 36 KiB of task stacks ⇒ **steady state ≈ 60 KiB PSRAM, peak ≈ 85 KiB.** For calibration, FIX-6 in `docs/architecture-review-2026-07-30.md` describes the box surviving an ~82 KB PSRAM + ~20 KB mbedTLS leak *per pull-to-refresh*, so this is inside the envelope.
- Force the SSE line buffer (8 KiB) and REST body accumulator to PSRAM explicitly with `heap_caps_malloc(MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM)` — plain `malloc` of a sub-16 KiB block lands in internal RAM under `SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL=16384`.
- **The sharper limit is sockets, not RAM.** `CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS=16` is shared by CoAP, mDNS, Matter/CHIP, the rendezvous poller, and **up to `FLUX_MODBUS_MAX=8` Modbus pollers**. HC pins one socket permanently and two during a REST call. Raise `CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS` to 20 in `firmware/sdkconfig.defaults` as part of Phase 1, or refuse to enable HC when `flux_modbus_count() > 6`. This is the most likely "works on the bench, dies in the field with 8 meters" failure.
- Do **not** enable `CONFIG_MBEDTLS_DYNAMIC_BUFFER` to shrink the idle SSE session — it is global and would change CoAP/DTLS and Matter TLS behaviour. Out of scope.

### 1.6 The SSE client

- All-appliances stream: `GET {base}/api/homeappliances/events`. One socket for the whole home; the per-appliance variant would need N.
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer …`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, `Accept-Language: <cfg.language>`.
- Config: `.timeout_ms = 90000` (KEEP-ALIVE is ~55 s), `.crt_bundle_attach = esp_crt_bundle_attach`, `.buffer_size = 2048`, `.keep_alive_enable = true`.
- Loop shape follows `remote/flux_remote_rendezvous.c:70-90` (`esp_http_client_open` → `fetch_headers` → check status) but then loops on `esp_http_client_read()` instead of `read_response`, kicking hangwatch on every chunk. **Never** `esp_http_client_perform()` — it would never return.
- Track last-byte-received time ourselves and treat >90 s of silence as a dead connection, independent of what `read()` returns. This makes the design robust to the timeout-semantics uncertainty in §5.1.
- Framing: fixed 8 KiB buffer, CRLF- and LF-tolerant, blank line dispatches. An over-long `data:` line drops the event, logs once, and requests a resync — never grows unbounded.
- `KEEP-ALIVE` → hangwatch kick only. `STATUS`/`EVENT`/`NOTIFY` → map + emit. `CONNECTED`/`PAIRED` → `ESTABLISHED` + throttled resync (≥300 s per appliance). `DISCONNECTED` → `RESUBSCRIBING` + per-appliance `online=false` (Phase 2/3 read this). `DEPAIRED` → `DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR`, **no auto-removal** — registry and `/devices` change only on an explicit user delete, mirroring the Modbus lockstep rule.

### 1.7 Failure / backoff state machine

```
DISABLED ──enable──► NEED_AUTH ──refresh ok──► SYNCING ──► STREAMING
    ▲                    ▲                                    │
    └───disable──────────┤                                    │
                         │ invalid_grant                      │
   THROTTLED ◄── 429 / quota-403 ────────────────────────── BACKOFF
      (blocked_until persisted)                    (net err / 5xx / stream drop)
```

- **BACKOFF**: 5 s → ×3 with ±25 % jitter → cap 1800 s. Reset only after a *successfully streamed event*, not on connect — a cloud that accepts then instantly closes must still back off.
- **THROTTLED**: honour `Retry-After` clamped to 60 s…86400 s; absent ⇒ 3600 s. `blocked_until` persisted (`blk`) so a reboot cannot escape it.
- **NEED_AUTH** (`invalid_grant`): stop *all* traffic, `needs_reauth=true`, per-appliance `DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR "reauthorise"`, and **never retry a rejected refresh token** — that is the fastest route to a 24 h block.
- **Quota guard** in `flux_hc_rest.c`, ahead of every request including user commands: `min_gap 2 s`, `≤60/h`, `≤500/day`. Over-ceiling returns `ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE` **without touching the network**, and the refusal is surfaced in `BoolResult.error` rather than silently dropped.
- Boot: if `blocked_until > now` start in THROTTLED; gate the first request on `flux_time_is_synced()` exactly as `prices_task` does (token expiry and `blocked_until` are wall-clock).

Concrete failure table (chosen behaviour):

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| No credentials | `NEED_AUTH`, zero outbound traffic (opt-in, like pricing) |
| Refresh token revoked | `NEED_AUTH` + `needs_reauth`, appliances → ERROR, **no retries** |
| REST 401 mid-session | one refresh + one retry; a second 401 → `NEED_AUTH` (no loop) |
| 429 / hard block | `THROTTLED`; appliances → `RESUBSCRIBING` (not ERROR); **cached attrs retained** so the app still shows last-known values |
| Stream drop | `BACKOFF` + jitter; throttled resync on reconnect; attr cache untouched (same as Modbus) |
| Appliance DISCONNECTED | per-appliance `online=false` + `RESUBSCRIBING`; never removed |
| SNTP not synced | hold all requests, log once |
| NVS write of a new refresh token fails | **keep streaming** — the token is valid in RAM. Log loudly, set `last_error`, retry the persist on the next refresh. Cost of losing it is one re-auth after reboot, not the session. |
| Ethernet down | connect fails → `BACKOFF`; the cap bounds the churn |
| `FLUX_DEVICES_MAX`/`ATTR_CACHE_MAX_NODES` (both 32) exhausted | upsert returns `NO_MEM`; appliance skipped, warning logged, `last_error` set (mirrors "device table full" rollback) |
| Config changed while running | `flux_homeconnect_reload()` sets a flag; `hc_ctl` tears the stream down and restarts it. **Never** create a second task (`flux_modbus_task_reload` + `static bool started` idiom) |

## Phase 2 — control

### 2.1 Dispatch

Already built in Phase 0.4. Phase 2 adds `homeconnect/flux_hc_backend.c` registering `{ .kind = FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_CLOUD, … }`.

The backend runs on `hc_ctl`, not the caller: `invoke()` validates, enqueues an `hc_cmd_t` onto a length-8 queue and returns `ESP_OK` meaning **accepted, not done**. The outcome arrives as an attribute/device event. This is not a compromise — `flux_send_device_command_args()` already means only "scheduled onto the CHIP task", so the contract is unchanged. The CoAP task must never block on a cloud PUT.

### 2.2 Matter-verb mapping

| CoAP command | Home Connect action |
|---|---|
| OnOff `0x0006` cmd `0x01`/`0x00` | `PUT /settings/BSH.Common.Setting.PowerState` = `On` / `Off`\|`Standby` (allowed values learned at discovery) |
| OperationalState `0x0060` cmd `0x02` Start | `PUT /programs/active` with the currently **selected** program + carried options |
| … cmd `0x01` Stop | `DELETE /programs/active` |
| … cmd `0x00` Pause | `PUT /commands/BSH.Common.Command.PauseProgram` *(verify)* |
| … cmd `0x03` Resume | `PUT /commands/BSH.Common.Command.ResumeProgram` *(verify)* |
| Mode cluster (`0x0059` dishwasher / `0x0051` washer) cmd `0x00` ChangeToMode, arg tag 0 = `NewMode` | `PUT /programs/selected` with the program key at that index |

Attribute/command IDs verified in `23-27350-008_Matter-1.5-Application-Cluster-Specification.pdf`: OperationalState cluster `0x0060`; attrs `0x0000` PhaseList, `0x0001` CurrentPhase, `0x0002` CountdownTime, `0x0003` OperationalStateList, `0x0004` OperationalState, `0x0005` OperationalError; commands `0x00` Pause, `0x01` Stop, `0x02` Start, `0x03` Resume; states `0x00` Stopped, `0x01` Running, `0x02` Paused, `0x03` Error. Mode clusters: Dishwasher Mode `0x0059`, Laundry Washer Mode `0x0051`, Laundry Dryer Controls `0x004A`.

### 2.3 The HC-specific endpoint, and why both

`POST /homeconnect/command` ← `HomeConnectCommand { uint64 node_id; HcAction action; uint32 start_in_seconds; string program_key; }` → `BoolResult`, with `HcAction { HC_START, HC_STOP, HC_PAUSE, HC_RESUME, HC_SELECT, HC_SET_START_IN, HC_POWER_ON, HC_POWER_OFF }` (`flux.HomeConnectCommand.program_key max_size:64`).

**The trade-off, argued.** The pure-Matter option is attractive because it is *not* pretending: Matter's OperationalState and Mode clusters were written for exactly these appliances, and mapping onto them is the same move `flux_modbus_profile.h` already documents ("map the physical readings onto the Matter attribute keys + device type the app already renders"). Going Matter-only means the app's existing generic control UI, `flux-ctl cmd`, and any future *real* Matter dishwasher all work through one path — which is the whole point of FW-ADR-0009's one-device-model.

But `StartInRelative`, per-program option sets, and the selected-vs-active program distinction have **no** Matter representation. Forcing them into a fabricated cluster id would (a) collide the day a real Matter appliance appears and (b) be undiscoverable. And a manufacturer-specific cluster (`0xFC00+`) needs a vendor id we do not own, and the app would need bespoke encoders anyway — all the cost of an explicit endpoint with none of its clarity.

So the line is: **Matter clusters where a faithful mapping exists; an explicit HC endpoint where it does not.** Rejected: HC-endpoint-only (the app would need a second control path, `flux-ctl cmd` could not drive appliances, and a Matter dishwasher would be controlled differently from a Home Connect one — the two-device-concept outcome FW-ADR-0009 exists to prevent).

### 2.4 Safety gates — enforced locally, before any request

Checked in the backend so a guaranteed 403 never burns quota:

1. `remote_start_allowed == false` → refuse Start / SET_START_IN, `"enable remote start on the appliance"`.
2. `connected == false` → refuse (would 409).
3. door open → refuse Start.
4. `operationalState == Running` → refuse Start; Pause/Stop allowed.
5. One in-flight command per appliance (a 1-slot latch) so a double tap cannot produce two PUTs.
6. Quota refusal is **returned to the app**, never silently swallowed.

## Phase 3 — price-aware deferral

### 3.1 Placement and dependency direction

New `firmware/main/flexload/`: `flux_flexload.c/.h`, `flux_flex_plan.c/.h` (pure, host-tested), `flux_coap_flex.c`.

`flexload → prices` (`flux_prices_at()` — **this closes the "zero callers" gap**), `flexload → devices` (`flux_device_cmd_defer_start`), `flexload → matter/flux_state.h` (`flux_energy_role_of`, registry). Nothing depends on `flexload` except `app_main`. It never speaks HTTP and never speaks Home Connect.

### 3.2 User-visible contract

> **"Run before 07:00, in the cheapest 2 h window."**
> The hub never starts an appliance itself — it only delays a run you already started.

```proto
enum FlexLoadMode { FLEX_OFF=0; FLEX_CHEAPEST_BEFORE=1; }
message FlexLoadPolicy {
    uint64 node_id = 1;  FlexLoadMode mode = 2;
    uint32 deadline_minute = 3;   // minutes past midnight (see §3.4 on "local")
    uint32 max_delay_s = 4;       // hard cap, default 12 h
    uint32 duration_s = 5;        // 0 = ask the appliance (EstimatedTotalProgramTime)
    bool   require_user_start = 6; // default TRUE
}
message FlexLoadPolicies { repeated FlexLoadPolicy policies = 1; }
message FlexLoadPlan {
    uint64 node_id = 1;  int64 planned_start = 2;  uint32 delay_s = 3;
    sint32 avg_ueur_per_kwh = 4;  sint32 saving_ueur_per_kwh = 5;
    string reason = 6;   // "deferred" | "no price data" | "deadline too close" | …
}
message FlexLoadPlans { repeated FlexLoadPlan plans = 1; }
```
`flux.FlexLoadPolicies.policies max_count:8`, `flux.FlexLoadPlans.plans max_count:8`, `flux.FlexLoadPlan.reason max_size:48`.

Endpoints: `GET/POST /flex/policies`, `GET /flex/plan`. NVS ns `"flux_flex"`, keys `pol` (blob) and `stop_<n>` (u64 `user_stopped_at` latch).

### 3.3 Algorithm and task

`flux_flex_plan.c` (pure): slide an `n = ceil(duration/resolution)`-interval window over `[now, deadline − duration]`, minimise Σ price, ties → **earliest** (finish sooner, less risk). Require ≥2 intervals of forward coverage beyond the chosen window or fail.

Task `flux_flex`: **4 KiB internal** stack, prio 3, 60 s tick, hangwatch 120 s. No network, no NVS writes on the tick (policy writes arrive from the CoAP task). It enqueues into the HC backend and never issues HTTP itself — that is what keeps the PSRAM/NVS hazard confined to `homeconnect/`.

Trigger: `hc_sse` reports `operationalState == 0x80` (DelayedStart), or the app issues `HC_START` on a node with a policy → compute → `flux_device_cmd_defer_start(node, delay_s, &granted)`. HC implements it as `BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative` — on first start as an option on `PUT /programs/active`, and thereafter as `PUT /programs/active/options/BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative` while in DelayedStart. The Matter backend returns `ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED` (Matter has no delayed start).

Only nodes whose `flux_energy_role_of()` is `LOAD` or `UNKNOWN` are considered — never defer something the user tagged GRID/PV/BATTERY.

### 3.4 Failure modes and chosen behaviour

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **No / stale price curve** (`flux_prices_at` → `NOT_FOUND`, or `PriceCurve.stale`) | **Do not defer — start now.** `reason="no price data"`. The failure mode of a price-aware scheduler must be "behaves exactly like today", never "the dishwasher never runs". |
| Deadline past, or within `duration` | Start now, `reason="deadline too close"` |
| Optimal delay > `max_delay_s` | Clamp to `max_delay_s` |
| Appliance offline at deferral time | Keep the plan, retry on `CONNECTED`; abandon it past `deadline − duration` |
| `remote_start_allowed == false` | **Never defer** — deferring commits us to a remote start we are not permitted to make. Start now / do nothing, `reason="remote start not enabled"` |
| **User stopped the program** (Stop command, or state → Stopped/Inactive) | Plan **cancelled and not re-armed**. Persist `user_stopped_at` and ignore the node until a *new* user-initiated start. A hard latch, not a heuristic. |
| Curve refresh moves the optimum | Re-evaluate at most every 15 min; only *increase* the delay, only while still in DelayedStart, only if still before deadline. Each change is a cloud PUT = quota. |
| Quota exhausted | Deferral refused, `reason="rate limited"`; the appliance runs on whatever delay it already has |
| SNTP sync edge / clock jump | Re-evaluate all plans |

**"Local time" is a real gap.** `firmware/main/platform/flux_time.c` is UTC-only: it uses `gmtime_r` and never calls `setenv("TZ",…)`/`tzset()`. So `deadline_minute` cannot be resolved as local time today. Two honest options: (a) add `tz_offset_minutes` to the policy/config and resolve with plain arithmetic (no DST — acceptable for a "before 07:00" contract, off by an hour twice a year), or (b) implement TZ properly in `flux_time.c` via a POSIX TZ string and `localtime_r`. Recommend (b), because `PricingConfig.fetch_hour_local` (field 6) already promises local-hour scheduling and is likewise unimplemented — fix both together.

## 5. What is risky or likely wrong

1. **`esp_http_client` for a never-ending SSE stream is the single biggest assumption.** The client is request/response shaped. Unverified: `esp_http_client_read()`'s return value on socket timeout with an open chunked body; whether `esp_http_client_is_complete_data_received` interferes; how to read `Retry-After` (needs an `HTTP_EVENT_ON_HEADER` handler). The last-byte-timestamp watchdog in §1.6 makes us robust to the first two. **Fallback:** `esp_tls` + a hand-rolled minimal HTTP/1.1 request and read loop, ~200 lines — precedent exists (FW-ADR-0005 hand-rolled the MeshCoP DTLS client). Budget for it.
2. **The app's `0x0073 → airQualitySensor` collision** (`flux-app/lib/models/device_type.dart:145`) — verified wrong against the 1.5 Device Library. Every Home Connect washer renders as an air-quality sensor until fixed.
3. **The app's `isModbus` is a bare `>=` threshold** (`flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart:125`); ship the app's kind decode before the firmware or appliances land in the Modbus list.
4. **NVS is 24 KiB and unencrypted** (`CONFIG_NVS_ENCRYPTION` not set, though `partitions.csv` marks `nvs` `encrypted` for future flash encryption). A refresh token sits in plaintext flash until flash encryption is enabled in release. Measure with `nvs_get_stats()` before shipping.
5. **`CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS=16`** with 8 Modbus pollers + CoAP + mDNS + Matter + rendezvous + 2 HC. Raise it or gate HC. Most likely field-only failure.
6. **The PSRAM/NVS abort.** Mitigated structurally, but one carelessly added `nvs_set_*` on `hc_ctl` reintroduces a hard crash. Put the invariant in `flux_homeconnect.h` **and** in `docs/threading.md`, not just in a commit message.
7. **Rate-limit blocks last up to 24 h and are effectively unrecoverable.** Every retry path needs the persisted guard. Simulator-first is not optional.
8. **Verify against the live API / simulator:** Pause/Resume via `/commands/…` (support is appliance-specific); which mode cluster the Laundry Dryer and WasherDryer device types mandate; whether `haId` arrives in the SSE `id:` field or the JSON body (handle both); `items[].value` type mixing (bool / number / string per key); whether a device-flow grant exists (design the config surface so adding `POST /homeconnect/auth/start` later is purely additive).

Design the **account-linking (OAuth) bootstrap and the Flutter app UX** for integrating Bosch/Siemens **Home Connect** cloud appliances into the flux ecosystem. Repo: /home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app (Flutter app), with a companion ESP32-P4 controller at /home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-controller that owns all device runtime. Read the referenced files to ground the design. Do not modify anything — produce a plan.

## Architecture premise (assume this, do not re-litigate)
The **controller** will own the Home Connect runtime: it holds the refresh token, keeps a Server-Sent-Events stream open, exposes each appliance as a device with a synthetic node ID, and executes commands. The app's job is (a) run the interactive OAuth grant, because only the phone has a browser, (b) hand the resulting credential to the controller over the existing DTLS/CoAP channel, (c) render appliances and their controls, (d) manage the link (status, re-auth, unlink).

## Verified facts about the app (trust these references)
- **Devices**: `lib/models/matter_device.dart` — `MatterDevice` (`id` = app-local UUID, `nodeId` = controller/Matter id), `enum ManagedBy { phone, controller }` (:40), `enum NetworkType { wifi, thread, ethernet, modbus, unknown }` (:11), and the synthetic-range test `bool get isModbus => nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000` (:125).

So controller-owned appliances need **no** app-side add flow — only type/icon/control support.
- **Types**: `lib/models/device_type.dart` — 24 values, **no appliance types at all**; capability flags at :70-118 are the only thing deciding which control cards render; icons at :158-184. - **Live state is open-ended**: `lib/models/device_live_data.dart:106` `Map<String,dynamic> attrs` — new attribute keys need no model change. Read-only readouts are added by ONE entry in `_kLiveRenderers` + one `_render*` function in `lib/services/cluster_parser.dart:259-283` (doc at :193-194 says nothing else needs changing).
- **Control path**: `DeviceProvider.toggle` (`device_provider.dart:906`) does optimistic-merge → `_channel.toggleDevice(nodeId)` → rollback on failure; transport is `FluxCoapService._sendCmd` (`lib/services/flux_coap_service.dart:592`, `POST /command`, `retryOnConnError:false` because commands aren't idempotent). - Scopes are granular, including per-appliance ones (e.g. `Dishwasher-Control`), plus `IdentifyAppliance`/`Monitor`/`Settings`/`Control`.
- Rate limits are punitive (blocks lasting minutes to 24 h).

   (a) phone runs the grant in a system browser / ASWebAuthenticationSession with a registered redirect scheme, exchanges the code, then POSTs the refresh token to the controller;
   (b) phone runs only the authorize step and hands the *code* to the controller, which does the exchange (secret lives on the controller);
   (c) controller serves a small local HTTP page on the LAN and the user completes the grant against `http://<controller>/…` as the redirect target;
   (d) user pastes a token obtained out-of-band (dev-grade fallback).
   Address: a client_secret embedded in a shipped mobile app is extractable; a per-user "bring your own Home Connect developer client id/secret" model (what several Home Assistant integrations do) may be the honest option for a self-hosted product. Note the anti-pattern to avoid: `GET /prices/config` echoes `PricingConfig.api_token` in cleartext — do not repeat that for tokens.
3. **New app dependencies + platform config** actually required, with the minimum viable set, and the Android/iOS manifest/plist changes spelled out. Note whether adding a browser-based login has any app-store implications given the existing care taken over the AD_ID scanner in the manifest.
4. **Device representation & UI**: which `DeviceType` values / Matter appliance device-type IDs to add, which new live-attribute keys and `_kLiveRenderers` entries (operation state, program, remaining time, door state, power), whether appliances get a new `HomeCategory` (and how to handle the 4-button layout squeeze) or live under Energy, and what the appliance detail screen shows — including a read-only-first design that degrades gracefully when `RemoteControlStartAllowed` is false.
5. **Where the "connect Home Connect" entry point lives** in the app's information architecture, given Settings is reserved for the controller.
6. **The honesty/copy problem**: what the no-cloud claims should become, and what the UI should tell the user about what leaves the house.

Give concrete file paths, proto sketches (with .options entries), and a phased ordering where phase 1 is read-only monitoring. Call out the risks and anything needing verification against the live API.

I explored the app, the controller firmware, the shared proto contract, and verified the Matter device-type IDs against the vendored spec PDF. Here is the design.

---

# Home Connect integration — account-linking bootstrap & Flutter UX

## 0. Verification results (things the plan depends on, and three bugs found)

**Matter device-type IDs, verified against `docs/23-27351-008_Matter-1.5-Device-Library-Specification.pdf`** (§13 "appliances", and the master ID table on p.41-42):

| ID | Name |
|---|---|
| 0x0070 | Refrigerator |
| 0x0071 | Temperature Controlled Cabinet |
| 0x0072 | Room Air Conditioner |
| **0x0073** | **Laundry Washer** |
| 0x0074 | Robotic Vacuum Cleaner |
| 0x0075 | Dishwasher |
| 0x0077 | Cook Surface |
| 0x0078 | Cooktop |
| 0x0079 | Microwave Oven |
| 0x007A | Extractor Hood |
| 0x007B | Oven |
| 0x007C | Laundry Dryer |
| **0x002C** | **Air Quality Sensor** |

So `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/models/device_type.dart:147` (`0x0073 => airQualitySensor`) is **wrong** — and the correct line already exists directly below it at `:148` (`0x002C => airQualitySensor`, commented as the "Matter draft ID"; it is in fact the current, correct ID). The fix is a deletion, not a remap. Two more places carry the same confusion:

- `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/lib/ui/screens/cluster_inspector_screen.dart:40` — `0x0073: 'Air Quality Sensor'`. Also in that map: `0x0072: 'Air Purifier (alt)'` (it is Room Air Conditioner) and `0x0071: 'HEPA Filter Monitoring'` (0x0071 is the *cluster* ID for HEPA Filter Monitoring; as a *device type* it is Temperature Controlled Cabinet) — a cluster-ID/device-type-ID conflation.
- `/home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app/docs/SUPPORTED_DEVICES.md:54` lists `Air Quality Sensor | 0x0073`, and `:71` lists `Laundry Washer | 0x0073` — the same ID under two names in one document.

Regression risk of fixing it: nil in practice. `MatterDevice.toJson` persists the *enum name*, and `_reconcileWithController` (`lib/providers/device_provider.dart:430-447`) only ever repairs `networkType`/`isOnline`, never `deviceType` — so an already-adopted record would not self-heal. But nothing ships reporting 0x0073 as an air-quality sensor (the real IKEA ALPSTUGA workaround is the 0x002C line), so no migration is needed. Add `test/models/device_type_test.dart` (does not exist yet) pinning the whole ID table so this can't recur.

**Node-ID range aliasing.** `MatterDevice.isModbus` (`lib/models/matter_device.dart:125`) is an *open-ended* `nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000`, and the firmware agrees (`flux_state.h:166-167`, `flux_is_modbus_node`). Any Home Connect synthetic base placed *above* the Modbus base therefore makes every appliance test true for `isModbus` → it lands in `DeviceProvider.modbusDevices` (`:126`), gets `NetworkType.modbus` from `_normalizeControllerNetworkType` (`:345`) and `:408`, and shows up in `ModbusDevicesScreen`. This must become a bounded range test before any appliance exists.

**Payloads are unbounded-friendly.** `flux_coap.c:119-120` sets `COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP | COAP_BLOCK_SINGLE_BODY`, and the notify/attr paths `malloc` their encode buffers (`flux_coap_handlers.c:596`, `:1076`) rather than stack-allocating `flux_AttrsUpdate_size`. So both a ~1 KB credential POST and a widened `Attr` message are affordable.

**The anti-pattern is real and confirmed.** `flux_coap_prices.c:50-54` calls `flux_prices_get_config()` and `pb_encode`s the *whole* `flux_PricingConfig` on `GET /prices/config` — including `api_token` (`flux.proto` `PricingConfig.api_token = 4`, `flux.options` `max_size:80`). Cleartext echo of a user secret on a read. Nothing in the Home Connect surface may do this.

**Existing precedent for "go get credentials from a third-party website"** is *clipboard*, not browser: `remote_access_screen.dart:153-157` `_copySignupLink()` copies `https://dashboard.metered.ca/signup` and snackbars "Signup link copied — open it in your browser". This matters for §3 — it drops `url_launcher` from the required set.

**Synthetic devices need a synthesised cluster dump.** `flux_coap_handlers.c:477-484` special-cases `flux_is_modbus_node` in `GET /devices/clusters` and calls `flux_modbus_synth_cluster_dump()`, because there is no CASE session to read. Home Connect nodes need the identical treatment, or the app's `_maybeLoadReadings` → `readClusters(nodeId)` (`device_detail_screen.dart:183-186`, fired on every first open) falls into the real Matter read path.

---

## 1. Where the grant runs, and where the `client_secret` lives

### The decisive constraint, stated first

**Whoever performs the *refresh* needs the `client_secret`.** Refreshing happens forever, unattended, on the controller — that is the entire premise ("controller owns the runtime, holds the refresh token, keeps the SSE stream open"). Therefore the secret must exist on the controller **regardless of which box does the initial code exchange**.

This collapses option (a). Having the phone do the token exchange does not keep the secret off the controller; it puts it in *two* places — an extractable APK **and** the controller. Option (a) is strictly worse than (b) on exactly the axis it was supposed to win. (Unless Home Connect's refresh grant accepts a public client with no secret — see V3 — but even then I'd have the controller do the one-time exchange, because there is no benefit to the phone doing it.)

### Honest comparison

| | Secret location | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Phone does authorize + exchange, POSTs refresh token to controller** | APK **and** controller | **Reject.** Doubles exposure for zero gain (see above). A shipped `client_secret` is extractable by `apktool` in minutes; it also means one shared `client_id` for all users → one shared rate-limit bucket (see below) and one revocation event that kills the feature for everyone. |
| **(b) Phone does authorize only; hands the `code` to the controller; controller exchanges** | Controller only | **Ship this.** The code is single-use, short-lived, and bound to `redirect_uri` — safe to pass over the existing DTLS/CoAP channel. The controller never needs to *receive* the redirect, only to *echo the string* in the exchange, so a custom-scheme redirect works fine. The app can fetch the authorize URL from the controller, so **the app ships no credentials at all — not even the `client_id`.** |
| **(c) Controller serves a LAN HTTP page as the redirect target** | Controller only | **Reject.** Four independent killers: the redirect URI is registered per client in the portal and a per-household LAN IP/`.local` name isn't registrable; providers reject plain `http` on non-loopback hosts; the controller exposes no HTTP server today (CoAP/DTLS only) so this is fresh attack surface with a TLS-warning problem; `.local` resolution in mobile browsers is unreliable. **Keep one variant in reserve:** the RFC 8252 *loopback* redirect `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/cb` served by the **phone** — a legitimate fallback if custom schemes are rejected (V1). |
| **(d) Paste a token obtained out-of-band** | Controller only | **Ship as a collapsed "Advanced" affordance**, not as the primary path. It is the only way to test against the developer simulator with a `curl`-minted token, and it's the escape hatch for users who script their own. Costs ~20 lines. |

### The BYO-credentials question — this is the real decision

I would ship **(b) + bring-your-own Home Connect developer client**: the user registers their own application at `developer.home-connect.com` and enters `client_id` / `client_secret` once. Reasons, in order of weight:

1. **Rate limits make a shared `client_id` structurally unsafe.** Home Connect's limits are per-client and the penalties are blocks of minutes to 24 h. With one shipped `client_id`, a single misbehaving controller — or simply enough users — brings down every household's appliances at once, and there is nothing an affected user can do about it. BYO makes the blast radius exactly one home. This alone is sufficient.
2. **Nothing extractable ships.** No secret in the APK, no secret in the app process, no secret in `SharedPreferences`.
3. **It is already this product's established pattern.** `remote_access_screen.dart:9` and `:220`: *"use your own free account so no third party is ever in the middle"* — flux already asks users to bring their own TURN relay for exactly this reason. Asking them to bring their own Home Connect client is the same trade, made for the same stated reason, and it keeps the copy in §6 truthful rather than lawyered.
4. **A self-hosted product operating a shared cloud OAuth client on users' behalf *is* running a cloud.** Not literally, but in every way that matters to the claim.

The cost is real and should not be minimised: 5–10 minutes of web forms, and it will lose some users at the first screen. Mitigate with the setup instructions below, and by making the whole feature clearly optional and clearly labelled.

### What the setup instructions look like (screen copy, ready to use)

> **Connect Bosch / Siemens appliances**
>
> Home Connect is Bosch's cloud service. To use it, flux needs a Home Connect *developer client* — a free key you create in your own name. It takes about five minutes, once.
>
> **1.** Go to `developer.home-connect.com` and sign in with the same Bosch/Siemens account your appliances are registered to. `[Copy link]`
> **2.** Accept the developer terms, then open **Applications → Register Application**.
> **3.** Fill in:
>  · Application ID — anything, e.g. `flux-home`
>  · OAuth Flow — **Authorization Code Grant**
>  · Redirect URI — paste this exactly: `fluxhome://homeconnect/callback` `[Copy]`
>  · Home Connect User Account — the email your appliances are registered to
> **4.** Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** it gives you, and paste them below.
>
> These are stored on your Flux controller, not on your phone, and never leave your home except to talk to Bosch. `[Client ID …] [Client Secret …] [Use developer simulator ▢]`

Then a single button: **Connect account** → system browser → Bosch's own login page → back to the app.

**Design the proto so Device Flow can replace all of this.** If Home Connect supports RFC 8628 (V2 — genuinely unverified, and high-value), the entire app-side OAuth stack disappears: the controller starts the grant itself, the app displays a `user_code` plus a verification URL, and `flutter_web_auth_2` / the manifest / the plist / the redirect registration are all unnecessary. That would be a strictly better design. **Verify V2 before writing any of Phase 2.** The contract in §2 is shaped so `GET /homeconnect/device-code` is purely additive.

---

## 2. The credential-handoff contract

### Endpoints (add to the resource-map doc comment at `lib/services/flux_coap_service.dart:30-50`)

```
GET    /homeconnect/status         → HomeConnectStatus         (token-free, always safe)
POST   /homeconnect/client         ← HomeConnectClient         → StatusResponse   [LAN-only, write-only]
DELETE /homeconnect/client         → StatusResponse            (forget credentials)
GET    /homeconnect/authorize-url  → HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl   (controller builds URL + mints `state`)
POST   /homeconnect/auth           ← HomeConnectAuth           → StatusResponse   [LAN-only]
DELETE /homeconnect/auth           → StatusResponse            (unlink: wipe refresh token, close SSE)
GET    /homeconnect/appliances     → HomeConnectApplianceList  (management screen only)
```

Two-level teardown is deliberate: `DELETE /auth` unlinks the account but keeps the client credentials, so re-linking after a lapsed refresh token does not force the user to re-enter the secret. `DELETE /client` is the full forget.

**`LAN-only` is load-bearing**, per ADR-0012 (`flux-interface/docs/adr/0012-lan-only-config-writes.md`). The two writes must be refused over the remote/ICE path, and the app should refuse to *start* the flow when `hub.connectionKind == ConnectionKind.remote` and say why. An authorization code and a client secret should not traverse a TURN relay even inside DTLS.

### Proto sketch

```proto
// ─── Home Connect (Bosch/Siemens cloud appliances) ───────────────────────────
// The controller owns the entire runtime: it holds the user's OAuth client
// credentials and the rotating refresh token, keeps one SSE stream open, and
// registers each appliance as an ordinary Device under a synthetic node id
// (>= FLUX_HOMECONNECT_NODE_BASE). Live state and commands therefore reuse
// Device / AttrsUpdate / DeviceStateEvent / DeviceCommand verbatim — only the
// provisioning surface below is Home-Connect-specific (mirroring Modbus).
//
// Bring-your-own client: the credentials are the *user's* own developer
// application, not a secret shipped in the app. The phone runs only the
// interactive authorize step (it is the only box with a browser) and hands the
// single-use code over; the token exchange happens on the controller so the
// client_secret never exists on the phone.
//
// INVARIANT: no GET in this section ever returns token or secret material.
// (Contrast PricingConfig.api_token, which GET /prices/config echoes in
// cleartext — do not repeat that here.)

enum HomeConnectLinkState {
    HC_LINK_UNCONFIGURED  = 0;  // no client credentials stored
    HC_LINK_NOT_LINKED    = 1;  // credentials stored, no refresh token yet
    HC_LINK_LINKED        = 2;  // refresh token valid
    HC_LINK_REAUTH_NEEDED = 3;  // refresh failed / refresh token lapsed
    HC_LINK_RATE_LIMITED  = 4;  // provider 429; retry_after_s is set
    HC_LINK_ERROR         = 5;  // transport / provider error; see last_error
}

// Granted-scope bits, so the UI can say "monitoring only — re-authorise to
// control" instead of letting commands fail. Cheaper on nanopb than strings.
enum HomeConnectScope {
    HC_SCOPE_NONE      = 0x00;
    HC_SCOPE_IDENTIFY  = 0x01;  // IdentifyAppliance
    HC_SCOPE_MONITOR   = 0x02;  // Monitor
    HC_SCOPE_SETTINGS  = 0x04;  // Settings
    HC_SCOPE_CONTROL   = 0x08;  // Control (+ per-appliance *-Control)
}

// POST /homeconnect/client — write-only, LAN-only. Never echoed by any GET.
message HomeConnectClient {
    string client_id     = 1;
    string client_secret = 2;  // WRITE-ONLY. Never returned by any endpoint.
    string redirect_uri  = 3;  // must match the portal registration verbatim
    bool   simulator     = 4;  // target the developer simulator host
}

// GET /homeconnect/authorize-url — the controller builds the URL from the stored
// client (so the app holds no client_id) and mints + remembers the `state`
// nonce. The app opens the URL in a system browser and does nothing else.
message HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl {
    string url        = 1;
    string state      = 2;  // echoed back in POST /auth; controller validates
    uint32 ttl_s      = 3;  // how long the nonce stays valid
    uint32 scope_bits = 4;  // which HomeConnectScope bits this URL requests
}

// POST /homeconnect/auth — hand over the authorization code. The controller does
// the token exchange itself, stores the rotating refresh token in NVS, and opens
// the SSE stream. Alternative advanced path: refresh_token set, code empty.
message HomeConnectAuth {
    string code          = 1;  // single-use authorization code from the redirect
    string redirect_uri  = 2;  // echoed verbatim into the token exchange
    string state         = 3;  // validated against the minted nonce
    string refresh_token = 4;  // advanced/dev fallback: token obtained out-of-band
    string code_verifier = 5;  // reserved for PKCE, if the provider supports it
}

// GET /homeconnect/status — deliberately token-free. Timestamps only, no tokens.
// Answers from controller state; NEVER makes an outbound request to Bosch (so
// the app polling this cannot burn the provider rate-limit budget).
message HomeConnectStatus {
    HomeConnectLinkState state                     = 1;
    uint32               appliance_count           = 2;
    bool                 stream_connected          = 3;  // SSE currently up
    int64                linked_at                 = 4;  // epoch s
    int64                access_token_expires_at   = 5;  // epoch s (clock, not token)
    int64                refresh_token_expires_at  = 6;  // epoch s → "re-authorise by"
    int64                last_event_at             = 7;  // epoch s of last SSE event
    uint32               retry_after_s             = 8;  // >0 while rate-limited
    uint32               granted_scope_bits        = 9;  // HomeConnectScope bits
    string               last_error                = 10; // human-readable, no secrets
    string               account_hint              = 11; // "b***@example.com" or ""
    string               client_id_hint            = 12; // last 6 chars, to confirm which client
}

message HomeConnectAppliance {
    string ha_id           = 1;  // Home Connect haId
    uint64 node_id         = 2;  // synthetic node id it is registered as
    string name            = 3;
    string brand           = 4;  // "Bosch" | "Siemens" | ...
    string kind            = 5;  // "Dishwasher" | "Washer" | ...
    uint32 device_type     = 6;  // Matter appliance device type we mapped it to
    bool   connected       = 7;  // Home Connect `connected` flag
    bool   control_allowed = 8;  // RemoteControlActive && RemoteControlStartAllowed
}

// GET /homeconnect/appliances
message HomeConnectApplianceList {
    repeated HomeConnectAppliance appliances = 1;
}
```

**One widening of an existing message** — appliance program and phase names are inherently strings and there is no numeric encoding worth having:

```proto
message Attr {
    string key = 1;
    oneof value {
        bool   bool_val = 2;
        sint32 int_val  = 3;
        sint64 long_val = 4;
        string str_val  = 5;  // NEW: appliance program / phase labels
    }
}
```

This is additive and wire-compatible in both directions (old firmware never emits it; old apps ignore it), so it can land in the plumbing phase without a lockstep release. Cost: `flux_Attr_size` 44 → ~94, `flux_AttrsUpdate_size` 1483 → ~3.1 KB — both `malloc`'d, per §0.

### `.options` entries

```
# ─── Home Connect ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
flux.HomeConnectClient.client_id            max_size:80
flux.HomeConnectClient.client_secret        max_size:128
flux.HomeConnectClient.redirect_uri         max_size:128
flux.HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl.url            max_size:512
flux.HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl.state          max_size:64
flux.HomeConnectAuth.code                   max_size:256
flux.HomeConnectAuth.redirect_uri           max_size:128
flux.HomeConnectAuth.state                  max_size:64
flux.HomeConnectAuth.refresh_token          max_size:512   # VERIFY real length (V5)
flux.HomeConnectAuth.code_verifier          max_size:128
flux.HomeConnectStatus.last_error           max_size:128
flux.HomeConnectStatus.account_hint         max_size:64
flux.HomeConnectStatus.client_id_hint       max_size:16
flux.HomeConnectAppliance.ha_id             max_size:48
flux.HomeConnectAppliance.name              max_size:64
flux.HomeConnectAppliance.brand             max_size:16
flux.HomeConnectAppliance.kind              max_size:24
flux.HomeConnectApplianceList.appliances    max_count:16

# ─── Attr (widened) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
flux.Attr.str_val                           max_size:48    # program / phase label
```

Every bound above is a place nanopb can silently truncate. A refresh token clipped at 512 bytes produces a permanently broken link with no visible cause — the controller must length-check and fail loudly rather than accept a truncated credential.

### What the app is allowed to keep locally

**Must never be stored:** `client_secret`, `client_id`, the authorization `code`, `code_verifier`, access token, refresh token. The reason is concrete, not theoretical: `SharedPreferences` is plaintext (`lib/services/controller_settings.dart:8-14` keeps the 16-byte DTLS PSK as hex32 there) **and** `android:allowBackup="true"` is set (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:60`), so that file is copied into Google's backup — there is even a `backup.ab` in the repo root. The DTLS PSK already has this exposure; do not add a second secret to it. Because the app stores nothing, **`flutter_secure_storage` is not needed.**

**May be kept** (non-secret, UX only): the last-seen `HomeConnectLinkState` and `refresh_token_expires_at`, so the home screen can show "Re-authorise needed" before the hub answers; the public `redirect_uri` string.

**Transient only:** the `code` lives in a local variable from the moment `flutter_web_auth_2` returns until `POST /homeconnect/auth` resolves. This codebase `debugPrint`s liberally, and `flux_coap_service.dart` logs exception text on every decode failure — explicitly forbid the code/state appearing in any log line or exception message.

### How link status / expiry / re-auth is surfaced

- A small `HomeConnectProvider` (`ChangeNotifier`) polls `GET /homeconnect/status` — 30 s while the Home Connect screen is open, once on app resume otherwise. This never touches Bosch, by contract.
- The Settings row subtitle carries the state: *"Not connected"* / *"3 appliances"* / *"Re-authorise needed"* / *"Rate-limited — retry in 14 min"*.
- `refresh_token_expires_at` drives a *"Re-authorise by 12 Oct"* row, and a warning treatment inside ~7 days. A ~2-month rotating refresh token that lapses silently kills all appliance state, so this needs to be visible before it happens, not after.
- `HC_LINK_REAUTH_NEEDED` gets exactly **one** persistent surface (a tile at the top of the home list) — not a banner on every screen. Resist the nag.
- `retry_after_s > 0` must **disable** the Re-authorise / Refresh buttons with a visible countdown. Letting a user tap "retry" into a 429 is how a minutes-long block becomes a 24-hour one.
- `stream_connected == false` while the controller is online must render as *"No cloud connection"*, distinct from the generic device-offline state — otherwise users blame flux for Bosch's outage. This means extending the `accessible` computation at `device_detail_screen.dart:262-265` for appliance devices.

## 3. Dependencies and platform config

### Minimum viable set: **one package**

**`flutter_web_auth_2` (^4.x)** — and that is the whole required delta.

It gives Android Custom Tabs and iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession` behind one call, returns the full redirect URL as a `String`, and surfaces user-cancel as an exception. It also offers `preferEphemeral: true`, which matters more than it looks: without it, the OAuth session inherits whatever stale Bosch cookie the browser holds, which breaks re-auth and account switching.

**Rejected alternatives, with reasons:**

- `url_launcher` + `app_links`/`uni_links` — two packages instead of one, and the app then owns the deep-link lifecycle itself (cold-start vs. warm-start redelivery against `android:launchMode="singleTop"`). On iOS it opens Safari as a separate app, so the return trip is a full app switch. Strictly worse.
- **`webview_flutter` — reject as a design constraint, not a preference.** An embedded webview means the flux process can observe the user's Bosch password, which directly contradicts the disclosure copy in §6 ("Your Bosch login is entered on Bosch's own page — flux never sees it"). It also invites store scrutiny and may be blocked by Bosch outright.
- `oauth2` / any Dart OAuth client — unnecessary; the token exchange happens on the controller.
- `flutter_secure_storage` — unnecessary; the app stores nothing.
- `url_launcher` on its own merits — **optional.** The codebase's own precedent for sending a user to a third-party signup page is the clipboard (`remote_access_screen.dart:153-157`). Following that precedent keeps the dependency count at one. Adding `url_launcher` anyway would be a nice quality win (it would also make that existing metered.ca link tappable), but it is not required.

### Android — `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`

Inside `<application>`, after the existing `MainActivity` block (~line 82):

```xml
<!-- Home Connect OAuth: receives the redirect from the system browser.
     Custom scheme only — no https App Link, so no autoVerify / assetlinks. -->
<activity
    android:name="com.linusu.flutter_web_auth_2.CallbackActivity"
    android:exported="true">
    <intent-filter android:label="flutter_web_auth_2">
        <action   android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
        <data     android:scheme="fluxhome" />
    </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

`MainActivity` is untouched — the callback is a separate activity, so `launchMode="singleTop"` needs no change. `minSdk = 27` / `targetSdk = 35` (`android/app/build.gradle.kts`) are fine for Custom Tabs. Only if `url_launcher` is added do you also need a top-level `<queries>` block declaring `android.intent.action.VIEW` + `<data android:scheme="https" />` for Android 11+ package visibility.

**Worth doing in the same change, independently:** `android:allowBackup="false"` (or a `dataExtractionRules`/`fullBackupContent` XML excluding the prefs file). Today the DTLS PSK is backed up to Google. We store no Home Connect secret, so this isn't blocking — but when someone asks "where does the Home Connect credential live", the answer must not be "in a file Google also has a copy of."

### iOS — `ios/Runner/Info.plist`

`ASWebAuthenticationSession` with `callbackURLScheme: "fluxhome"` intercepts the scheme itself and does **not** strictly require `CFBundleURLTypes`. Register it anyway, so a redirect arriving outside the session still reaches the app and no other app can claim the scheme:

```xml
<key>CFBundleURLTypes</key>
<array>
  <dict>
    <key>CFBundleTypeRole</key>   <string>Editor</string>
    <key>CFBundleURLName</key>    <string>eu.fluxhome.oauth</string>
    <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key> <array><string>fluxhome</string></array>
  </dict>
</array>
```

No new usage-description strings — no new hardware or permission is touched. `NSBonjourServices` unchanged. No `AppDelegate.swift` / `SceneDelegate` code needed. Skip `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes` by calling `launchUrl(..., LaunchMode.externalApplication)` without `canLaunchUrl`.

### App-store implications, given the AD_ID care at `AndroidManifest.xml:33-41`

The existing `com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID` + `tools:node="remove"` exists because `play-services-base` (transitive via `play-services-threadnetwork`) trips Play Console's automated advertising-ID detector. `flutter_web_auth_2` pulls in **`androidx.browser` only** — no Play Services, no ads SDK, no new AD_ID surface — so that declaration stays valid and unchanged. Verify after adding by re-checking `app/build/outputs/logs/manifest-merger-release-report.txt` still shows AD_ID removed.

The real store risk is **declaration-shaped, not permission-shaped**, and in this order of likelihood:

1. **The store listing itself.** `store-listing.md` currently says *"Local Matter smart home control. No cloud."* and *"Every command … is sent directly to the device over your local network, every time."* Shipping a cloud integration under that headline is a Play **Deceptive Behavior / misleading-claims** exposure, and it is by far the most likely cause of a rejection or a post-hoc takedown — much more than any manifest entry. The listing copy must change in the *same* release. See §6.
2. **Play Data safety form.** Even though flux collects nothing, the form asks about data your app *shares*. A user-initiated third-party integration that transfers appliance status and commands to Bosch needs declaring. Google cross-checks this against the privacy-policy URL.
3. **Privacy policy content** must cover it (see §6) — `privacypolicy.html` §1 currently asserts *"Flux Home does not send any information to external servers"* and §4 *"no third-party services"*, both of which become false on opt-in.
4. **Apple: low risk.** Guideline 4.8 (Sign in with Apple) targets third-party *social* logins used as the app's account system — Home Connect is a device-vendor account and flux has no accounts at all. 5.1.1(v) is satisfied because the login is optional and gates only account-based features. Using `ASWebAuthenticationSession` is the *approved* pattern; a `WKWebView` login is what would attract 4.0/5.1.1 scrutiny. The App Privacy questionnaire needs the same third-party-sharing disclosure as Play.
5. `isMinifyEnabled = true` with R8 — `CallbackActivity` is referenced from the manifest so it is kept automatically, but verify a real end-to-end login in a **release** build before shipping.

### `DeviceType` additions — `lib/models/device_type.dart`

Six values in Phase 1, chosen for overlap between "appliances people actually own" and "what Home Connect covers well":

| New enum value | Matter ID | `displayName` | `icon` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dishwasher` | 0x0075 | Dishwasher | `Icons.countertops_outlined` |
| `laundryWasher` | 0x0073 | Washing Machine | `Icons.local_laundry_service_outlined` |
| `laundryDryer` | 0x007C | Tumble Dryer | `Icons.dry_cleaning_outlined` |
| `oven` | 0x007B | Oven | `Icons.microwave_outlined` |
| `refrigerator` | 0x0070 | Fridge | `Icons.kitchen_outlined` |
| `extractorHood` | 0x007A | Extractor Hood | `Icons.air_outlined` |

Optional later: `cooktop` 0x0078, `microwaveOven` 0x0079.

New capability flag `bool get isAppliance` (the 0x0070/0x0073/0x0075/0x007A/0x007B/0x007C set), alongside the existing flags at `:70-118`. **Do not add appliances to `hasOnOff` or `isSensor`** in Phase 1 — `hasOnOff` gates both the `_OnOffCard` (`device_detail_screen.dart:311-312`) *and* `DeviceProvider.toggle` (`device_provider.dart:910-913`), so it would render a toggle that does nothing.

**Lossy-mapping decision to make now (V8):** Home Connect also covers WasherDryer, CoffeeMaker, WineCooler, Freezer, CookProcessor, WarmingDrawer — none of which have a Matter device type. `Device.device_type` is just a `uint32` the controller controls, so either (i) accept approximations (WasherDryer → 0x0073) or (ii) define a **flux-private** range and extend `fromMatterDeviceTypeId` with clearly-commented entries (`0xFC01` coffeeMaker, `0xFC02` wineCooler, `0xFC03` washerDryer, `0xFC04` freezer). I'd take (ii) for the four odd ones and (i) nowhere. Either way, avoid returning `unknown`: that triggers `_resolveUnknownDeviceType` (`device_provider.dart:775-777`) → a pointless controller read per appliance on every launch.

### Node ranges and `NetworkType`

- Firmware: `#define FLUX_HOMECONNECT_NODE_BASE 0x0200000000000000ULL` next to `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` (`flux_state.h:166`).
- `lib/models/matter_device.dart:125`: `isModbus` becomes a **bounded range** (`>= 0x0100…&& < 0x0200…`); add `bool get isHomeConnect => nodeId >= 0x0200000000000000 && nodeId < 0x0300000000000000`.
- `NetworkType` (`:11`) gains `cloud` — `label => 'Home Connect'`, `icon => 'cloud'`. This lights up the "Network" row at `device_settings_screen.dart:535-536` for free, giving every appliance a permanent, honest provenance marker with zero new UI.
- `device_provider.dart:408` and `_normalizeControllerNetworkType` (`:344-352`) mint `NetworkType.cloud` for the HC range.

### Live-attribute keys

The key insight from `cluster_parser.dart:193-201`: attributes with **no** `_kLiveRenderers` entry are silently skipped from the readings grid. That gives a clean split — **grid-consumed keys get a renderer; card-consumed keys get a typed getter and no renderer** — and it means Phase 1 can ship with *zero new widgets*.

| Key | Type | Origin | Phase 1 renderer? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `opState` | int | Matter OperationalState 0x0060/0x0004 (0 Stopped, 1 Running, 2 Paused, 3 Error) | ✅ `_renderOpState` |
| `programName` | **string** | HC ActiveProgram/SelectedProgram, resolved to a label by the controller | ✅ `_renderProgram` |
| `phaseName` | **string** | 0x0060/0x0001 CurrentPhase resolved against PhaseList | ✅ `_renderPhase` |
| `remainingSeconds` | int | 0x0060/0x0002 CountdownTime | ✅ `_renderRemaining` |
| `progressPercent` | int | HC `BSH.Common.Option.ProgramProgress` (no Matter equivalent) | ✅ `_renderProgress` |
| `applianceDoorState` | int | HC `BSH.Common.Status.DoorState` (0 Open, 1 Closed) | ✅ `_renderDoorState` |
| `doorLocked` | bool | HC DoorState = Locked | ✗ typed getter only |
| `opError` | int | 0x0060/0x0005 ErrorStateID (0 = NoError) | ✗ typed getter (card shows it) |
| `remoteControlAllowed` | bool | RemoteControlActive && RemoteControlStartAllowed | ✗ typed getter (gates controls) |
| `applianceConnected` | bool | HC `connected` flag | ✗ drives `Device.reachable` instead |
| `activePower` | int | the few appliances that report it | already renders + `EnergyCard`, free |
| `tempMeasureCenti` | int | fridge/freezer compartment temps | **already renders** via `_renderTempMeasure`, free |

Two deliberate naming choices:

- **`applianceDoorState`, not the existing `doorState`.** `doorState` is *already* in the controller's `kAttrMap` (`flux_controller.cpp:91`, DoorLock 0x0101/0x0003) but has no renderer and no `DeviceLiveData` getter. Giving it one would make every real Matter door lock suddenly grow a "Door" row in its readings grid — a cross-device-type behaviour change smuggled in on an appliance ticket. Use a distinct key (exactly how Modbus profiles already work: `flux_modbus_profile.h:36`, "static attr key string"). Unifying them later is a separate, deliberate change.
- Verified in the spec: Operational State is cluster **0x0060**, attrs 0x0000–0x0005; `OperationalStateEnum` 0x00 Stopped / 0x01 Running / 0x02 Paused / 0x03 Error; commands Pause 0x00, Stop 0x01, Start 0x02, Resume 0x03. Home Connect's richer state set (Inactive, Ready, DelayedStart, Run, Pause, ActionRequired, Finished, Aborting, Error) does **not** fit in four values — which is precisely why `programName`/`phaseName` need `str_val`, and why the controller should map HC → Matter for `opState` but pass the human-readable phase through as a string.

### The appliance detail screen — read-only first, degrading gracefully

**Phase 1 (zero new widgets).** Appliances get the existing app bar plus `_ReadingsSection` for free, purely from the six renderer entries. This is exactly what the comment at `cluster_parser.dart:193-194` promises, and it makes Phase 1 genuinely small. Two prerequisites: the controller must synthesise a cluster dump for HC nodes (mirroring `flux_modbus_synth_cluster_dump`, per §0) so the first-open `readClusters` call doesn't hit the CASE path; and that dump should carry brand/model/E-number as BasicInformation, so `view.displayProductName` puts "Bosch SMV6ZCX49E" in the app-bar subtitle with no code at all.

**Phase 2: `lib/ui/screens/device_detail/appliance_card.dart`** (a `part of` file, like every other card):

- A large dot-matrix state line via the existing `DotMatrixPainter` — `RUN` / `READY` / `PAUSED` / `FINISHED` / `ERROR` / `OFF`, and `--` when `view.isStale`. Reuses the `_OnOffCard` idiom (`on_off_card.dart:26-44`) so it looks native to the app.
- Program row (`ECO 50`), phase row (`RINSE`), remaining time as `h:mm` / `mm:ss`, and a thin linear progress bar from `progressPercent`.
- A door chip: `DOOR OPEN` / `DOOR CLOSED` / `DOOR LOCKED`.
- Error row shown only when `opError != 0`, styled after `_SmokeAlarmCard`'s severity colouring (`smoke_alarm_card.dart:19-26`) — the codebase's existing read-only-card reference.
- Compose it in `device_detail_screen.dart` around `:306-344` with `if (view.deviceType.isAppliance) …`, and suppress the now-duplicated readings rows using the **exact label-filter idiom already there** for `EnergyCard` (`:344-366`).

**Graceful degradation when `RemoteControlStartAllowed` is false** — this is the normal state for most appliances most of the time, not an edge case:

- Controls are **hidden, not disabled.** A greyed button with no explanation reads as a bug.
- In their place, one inline hint row: *"Remote start is switched off on the appliance. Turn it on at the machine to start programs from here."* — the fix is physical and the copy must say so.
- Monitoring is entirely unaffected, which is the whole argument for read-only-first: the feature is useful on day one even when control is impossible.
- Separately, when `granted_scope_bits` lacks `HC_SCOPE_CONTROL`: *"Monitoring only — re-authorise to enable control"* with a direct link to the Home Connect screen. **This is a real, user-visible consequence of shipping read-only first (V9):** enabling control later needs a wider scope set, which means a second trip through the browser. Better to surface it plainly than to let commands fail.

**Phase 3 controls: Pause / Resume / Stop only.** Route them through the *existing* transport — `_sendCmd(nodeId, 0x0060, 0x00 | 0x03 | 0x01, [])` via `POST /command`, which already sets `retryOnConnError: false` (`flux_coap_service.dart:592-609`) because commands aren't idempotent. No new endpoint. The controller translates to `PUT /programs/active/…` / `DELETE /programs/active`. **Do not optimistically merge** the way `toggle` does (`device_provider.dart:920-928`): appliance state machines take seconds, the SSE stream delivers truth shortly, and an optimistic `PAUSED` that gets rejected looks broken. Use short-lived card-local pending state instead — the pattern already used for the thermostat (`device_detail_screen.dart:50-51`, `_pendingSetpt` / `_pendingMode`). Program *selection* and Start need a per-appliance program catalogue; defer, explicitly out of scope for v1.

### Category: don't add one yet

`lib/ui/widgets/category_bar.dart:16-25` builds a fixed `Row` of `Expanded` pills with 10 px gaps. At four items on a 360 dp screen each pill is ~74 px wide, holding an 18 px icon + 6 px gap + 13.5 sp text — roughly 50 px for the label, so "Appliances" ellipsizes to something like "Applia…". Visually tight, as you flagged.

Also note what happens if you do nothing: `HomeCategory.energy.matches` (`home_category.dart:36-39`) keys off `energyRole != none || hasEnergyMeasurement || hasLivePower`, and most Home Connect appliances report no power at all. So appliances would match **no** category — and that is fine. They still appear in the home-screen room grid (auto-adoption via `_reconcileWithController` already places them there) and in the dedicated Home Connect management screen. **Recommendation: Phases 1–2 add no category.** Filling the Energy grid with dishwashers that contribute nothing to the energy scene would be worse than absence.

If user testing later demands it (Phase 3), add `HomeCategory.appliances` (label "Appliances", `Icons.kitchen_outlined`, a pastel green such as `0xFFA8D5A2` — check it doesn't read as the existing yellow/orange/blue set) with `matches => v.deviceType.isAppliance`, and resolve the squeeze by changing `category_bar.dart` from `Row(Expanded)` to a **`Wrap` laying out 2×2** with `runSpacing`. That is ~6 lines, keeps every label legible, and costs one row of vertical space above the device grid. Icon-only pills and a horizontal scroller both lose more than they gain. Routing needs no change at all: `router.dart:37-43` already resolves any enum name via `HomeCategory.values.byName`, and `HomeCategory` is never persisted, so adding a value is safe.
