## 5. Where the "connect Home Connect" entry point lives

**Primary: Settings → CONTROLLER → "Home Connect"**, one `_navTile` + `_divider` after "Remote access" in `settings_screen.dart:44-49`.

This does not violate the decree at `settings_screen.dart:18-20`; it *satisfies* it. The stated principle is "the phone itself has nothing the user needs to configure" — and Home Connect is not a phone thing. The refresh token lives in the controller's NVS, the SSE stream is the controller's, the appliances are controller-owned devices with controller-assigned node IDs. It belongs next to Matter, Thread and Remote access because it is the same kind of object: a controller-scoped integration. The row's subtitle carries live state from `HomeConnectStatus`.

**Secondary, for discoverability:** nobody hunting for "add my dishwasher" opens Settings. Follow the Modbus precedent (`category_screen.dart:81-120` puts Modbus setup inside the Energy category, deliberately *not* in Settings) and fix the root cause in Phase 3: convert the home-screen FAB from "straight to the QR scanner" (`home_screen.dart:104-112`) into a small add-chooser sheet with three rows — **Scan a Matter code** / **Connect Home Connect (Bosch, Siemens)** / **Add a Modbus meter**. Reuse the sheet shape, drag handle and styling from `_ScanSheet` in `modbus_devices_screen.dart:200-220`. This costs one extra tap on the most common flow, but it also un-buries Modbus from inside the Energy card, so all three non-Matter add-paths become discoverable in one change. Do it *after* the Settings entry point exists, so the feature can ship without touching the primary add flow.

## 6. The honesty / copy problem

Four claims break for users who opt in:

| Location | Current text |
|---|---|
| `pubspec.yaml:2` | "Local, private, independent." |
| `store-listing.md:5,11` | "No cloud." / "Every command … is sent directly to the device over your local network, every time." |
| `remote_access_screen.dart:9` and `:220-227` | "Flux runs no cloud" / "Flux runs no cloud and keeps no account of yours" |
| `privacypolicy.html` §1, §4 | "does not send any information to external servers" / "no third-party services" |

The wrong fix is to water the global claim down into mush. The right fix is to make it **scoped and conditional**, which is both truer and rhetorically stronger.

**The global edit is one word:** *"Flux runs no cloud"* → **"Flux runs no cloud of its own."** Apply at `remote_access_screen.dart:9` and `:220`. That single qualifier stays literally true after Home Connect — the cloud is Bosch's, reached with the user's own developer client and their own Bosch login — while preserving the differentiator. `:220`'s *"keeps no account of yours"* can stay verbatim: it remains true, because the Home Connect account is the user's, held by Bosch, and the app never stores even the `client_id`. `pubspec.yaml`'s "Local, private, independent." also stays — BYO credentials arguably strengthen "independent".

**`store-listing.md` needs a new bullet, and the "every time" sentence needs a qualifier:**

> **Cloud-only appliances, on your terms**
> A few brands — Bosch and Siemens, through Home Connect — offer no local API at all. Flux can talk to them, using **your own** developer key and **your** Bosch account, from your controller in your home. Not from our servers; we don't have any. It's off until you switch it on, every such device is labelled in the app, and unlinking wipes the key from your controller. If you never connect one, nothing ever leaves your home.

## 1. Where the grant runs, and where the `client_secret` lives

### The decisive constraint, stated first

**Whoever performs the *refresh* needs the `client_secret`.** Refreshing happens forever, unattended, on the controller — that is the entire premise ("controller owns the runtime, holds the refresh token, keeps the SSE stream open"). Therefore the secret must exist on the controller **regardless of which box does the initial code exchange**.

This collapses option (a). Having the phone do the token exchange does not keep the secret off the controller; it puts it in *two* places — an extractable APK **and** the controller. Option (a) is strictly worse than (b) on exactly the axis it was supposed to win. (Unless Home Connect's refresh grant accepts a public client with no secret — see V3 — but even then I'd have the controller do the one-time exchange, because there is no benefit to the phone doing it.)

### Honest comparison

| | Secret location | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Phone does authorize + exchange, POSTs refresh token to controller** | APK **and** controller | **Reject.** Doubles exposure for zero gain (see above). A shipped `client_secret` is extractable by `apktool` in minutes; it also means one shared `client_id` for all users → one shared rate-limit bucket (see below) and one revocation event that kills the feature for everyone. |
| **(b) Phone does authorize only; hands the `code` to the controller; controller exchanges** | Controller only | **Ship this.** The code is single-use, short-lived, and bound to `redirect_uri` — safe to pass over the existing DTLS/CoAP channel. The controller never needs to *receive* the redirect, only to *echo the string* in the exchange, so a custom-scheme redirect works fine. The app can fetch the authorize URL from the controller, so **the app ships no credentials at all — not even the `client_id`.** |
| **(c) Controller serves a LAN HTTP page as the redirect target** | Controller only | **Reject.** Four independent killers: the redirect URI is registered per client in the portal and a per-household LAN IP/`.local` name isn't registrable; providers reject plain `http` on non-loopback hosts; the controller exposes no HTTP server today (CoAP/DTLS only) so this is fresh attack surface with a TLS-warning problem; `.local` resolution in mobile browsers is unreliable. **Keep one variant in reserve:** the RFC 8252 *loopback* redirect `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/cb` served by the **phone** — a legitimate fallback if custom schemes are rejected (V1). |
| **(d) Paste a token obtained out-of-band** | Controller only | **Ship as a collapsed "Advanced" affordance**, not as the primary path. It is the only way to test against the developer simulator with a `curl`-minted token, and it's the escape hatch for users who script their own. Costs ~20 lines. |

### The BYO-credentials question — this is the real decision

I would ship **(b) + bring-your-own Home Connect developer client**: the user registers their own application at `developer.home-connect.com` and enters `client_id` / `client_secret` once. Reasons, in order of weight:

1. **Rate limits make a shared `client_id` structurally unsafe.** Home Connect's limits are per-client and the penalties are blocks of minutes to 24 h. With one shipped `client_id`, a single misbehaving controller — or simply enough users — brings down every household's appliances at once, and there is nothing an affected user can do about it. BYO makes the blast radius exactly one home. This alone is sufficient.
2. **Nothing extractable ships.** No secret in the APK, no secret in the app process, no secret in `SharedPreferences`.
3. **It is already this product's established pattern.** `remote_access_screen.dart:9` and `:220`: *"use your own free account so no third party is ever in the middle"* — flux already asks users to bring their own TURN relay for exactly this reason. Asking them to bring their own Home Connect client is the same trade, made for the same stated reason, and it keeps the copy in §6 truthful rather than lawyered.
4. **A self-hosted product operating a shared cloud OAuth client on users' behalf *is* running a cloud.** Not literally, but in every way that matters to the claim.

The cost is real and should not be minimised: 5–10 minutes of web forms, and it will lose some users at the first screen. Mitigate with the setup instructions below, and by making the whole feature clearly optional and clearly labelled.

### What the setup instructions look like (screen copy, ready to use)

> **Connect Bosch / Siemens appliances**
>
> Home Connect is Bosch's cloud service. To use it, flux needs a Home Connect *developer client* — a free key you create in your own name. It takes about five minutes, once.
>
> **1.** Go to `developer.home-connect.com` and sign in with the same Bosch/Siemens account your appliances are registered to. `[Copy link]`
> **2.** Accept the developer terms, then open **Applications → Register Application**.
> **3.** Fill in:
>  · Application ID — anything, e.g. `flux-home`
>  · OAuth Flow — **Authorization Code Grant**
>  · Redirect URI — paste this exactly: `fluxhome://homeconnect/callback` `[Copy]`
>  · Home Connect User Account — the email your appliances are registered to
> **4.** Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** it gives you, and paste them below.
>
> These are stored on your Flux controller, not on your phone, and never leave your home except to talk to Bosch. `[Client ID …] [Client Secret …] [Use developer simulator ▢]`

Then a single button: **Connect account** → system browser → Bosch's own login page → back to the app.

**Design the proto so Device Flow can replace all of this.** If Home Connect supports RFC 8628 (V2 — genuinely unverified, and high-value), the entire app-side OAuth stack disappears: the controller starts the grant itself, the app displays a `user_code` plus a verification URL, and `flutter_web_auth_2` / the manifest / the plist / the redirect registration are all unnecessary. That would be a strictly better design. **Verify V2 before writing any of Phase 2.** The contract in §2 is shaped so `GET /homeconnect/device-code` is purely additive.

```
POST   /homeconnect/client         ← HomeConnectClient         → StatusResponse   [LAN-only, write-only]
DELETE /homeconnect/client         → StatusResponse            (forget credentials)
GET    /homeconnect/authorize-url  → HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl   (controller builds URL + mints `state`)
POST   /homeconnect/auth           ← HomeConnectAuth           → StatusResponse   [LAN-only]
DELETE /homeconnect/auth           → StatusResponse            (unlink: wipe refresh token, close SSE)
GET    /homeconnect/appliances     → HomeConnectApplianceList  (management screen only)
```

**`flutter_web_auth_2` (^4.x)** — and that is the whole required delta.

It gives Android Custom Tabs and iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession` behind one call, returns the full redirect URL as a `String`, and surfaces user-cancel as an exception. It also offers `preferEphemeral: true`, which matters more than it looks: without it, the OAuth session inherits whatever stale Bosch cookie the browser holds, which breaks re-auth and account switching.

`lib/ui/widgets/category_bar.dart:16-25` builds a fixed `Row` of `Expanded` pills with 10 px gaps. ## 5. Where the "connect Home Connect" entry point lives

**Primary: Settings → CONTROLLER → "Home Connect"**, one `_navTile` + `_divider` after "Remote access" in `settings_screen.dart:44-49`.

**Secondary, for discoverability:** nobody hunting for "add my dishwasher" opens Settings. Follow the Modbus precedent (`category_screen.dart:81-120` puts Modbus setup inside the Energy category, deliberately *not* in Settings) and fix the root cause in Phase 3: convert the home-screen FAB from "straight to the QR scanner" (`home_screen.dart:104-112`) into a small add-chooser sheet with three rows — **Scan a Matter code** / **Connect Home Connect (Bosch, Siemens)** / **Add a Modbus meter**. Reuse the sheet shape, drag handle and styling from `_ScanSheet` in `modbus_devices_screen.dart:200-220`. This costs one extra tap on the most common flow, but it also un-buries Modbus from inside the Energy card, so all three non-Matter add-paths become discoverable in one change. Do it *after* the Settings entry point exists, so the feature can ship without touching the primary add flow.

# Home Connect (Bosch/Siemens) integration into flux

## Context

flux is a local-first smart-home controller (ESP32-P4 + esp-matter + OTBR) with a Flutter app, recently pivoted toward **energy management**: it fetches EPEX day-ahead prices and logs per-device energy. `docs/epex-day-ahead-pricing.md:118-122` describes a "phase 2 — act on price" that is unimplemented; `flux_prices_at()` (`firmware/main/prices/flux_prices.c:354`) has **zero callers** today.

Home Connect appliances (dishwasher, washer, dryer) are the ideal deferrable load: the API exposes `BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative`, so a run the user has already asked for can be slid into the cheapest price window. That makes this integration both a device-coverage win and the first real consumer of the pricing subsystem.

The appliances in question are not Matter-capable (BSH's Matter rollout covers only newer fridges natively, plus some models via the Smart Kitchen Dock bridge; most existing appliances cannot be upgraded), so the cloud API is the only way to reach them.

**Intended outcome:** appliances appear as ordinary flux devices with live state, are controllable from the app, and can have their start deferred into the cheapest hours — with the token, the event stream and all control living on the controller so it works when the phone is away.

## Decisions (locked)

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Controller owns the runtime.** It holds the refresh token, keeps one Server-Sent-Events stream open, and executes all commands. The app only bootstraps auth and renders. | Must work with the phone away; price scheduling belongs next to the price data; appliances then flow through the existing `/devices` + `/events` contract with almost no app plumbing. |
| D2 | **Bring-your-own Home Connect developer client.** The user registers a free client at `developer.home-connect.com` and enters id/secret once; both are stored **only** on the controller. | Whoever refreshes needs the `client_secret`, and that is the controller — forever, unattended. Rate-limit blocks are per-client and last minutes to 24 h, so a shipped shared `client_id` would let one bad actor break every household. Nothing extractable ships in the APK. Mirrors the existing BYO-TURN pattern (`lib/ui/screens/settings/remote_access_screen.dart:9,220`). |
| D3 | **Phone does the `authorize` step only; the controller exchanges the code.** The app fetches the authorize URL *from* the controller, so the app ships no credentials at all — not even the `client_id`. | The authorization code is single-use, short-lived and redirect-bound: safe to pass over the existing DTLS/CoAP channel. Having the phone do the exchange would put the secret in *two* places for zero gain. |
| D4 | **Synthetic node IDs get a kind nibble.** Modbus stays `0x01…`; Home Connect becomes `0x02…`. | ADR-0009 makes "bit 63 clear" a cross-repo contract. Today the app's test is a bare threshold (`nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000`), so an HC node would silently render as a Modbus device. |
| D5 | **New neutral command bus** `devices/flux_device_cmd.c`; Matter and Home Connect each register a backend. | A dispatch layer does not exist — `flux_send_device_command_args()` (`firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:985`) rejects synthetic nodes at `:995`. Branching inside `flux_controller.cpp` would create a `matter → cloud` dependency, the inversion ADR-0008 exists to prevent. |
| D6 | **Matter clusters where a faithful mapping exists; an explicit HC endpoint where it doesn't.** | OnOff/OperationalState/Mode clusters were written for exactly these appliances, so a future *real* Matter dishwasher works through the same path. But `StartInRelative`, per-program option sets and selected-vs-active have no Matter representation; faking a cluster ID would collide later and be undiscoverable. |
| D7 | **Scheduling lives in a separate `flexload/` subsystem**, not in `homeconnect/`. | The same policy must later drive the battery and wallbox. |
| D8 | **The controller never starts an appliance on its own initiative — it only delays a run the user already started.** | This is the whole safety model, and it is also the user-visible contract. |

## Phase 0 — prerequisites (no new behaviour, independently mergeable)

Land these first; each is a small reviewable diff.

**0.1 App + tooling range fixes (ship first — no-ops until HC exists)**
- `flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart:125` — replace the threshold `isModbus` with kind decode; add `isHomeConnect`. Same at `lib/providers/device_provider.dart:408` (duplicated magic number) and `:345`.
- **Fix the real bug at `flux-app/lib/models/device_type.dart:147`**: `0x0073 => airQualitySensor` is wrong — `0x0073` is Matter **Laundry Washer**; Air Quality Sensor is `0x002C`, already correct on line 148. The fix is a deletion. Verified against the vendored `docs/23-27351-008_Matter-1.5-Device-Library-Specification.pdf`. Left in place, every washer renders as an air-quality sensor. Same conflation in `lib/ui/screens/cluster_inspector_screen.dart:40` and `docs/SUPPORTED_DEVICES.md:54,71`.
- `flux-controller/tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/cli.py:~1373` — `modbus ls`/`rm` must filter a **range**, not `>= base`, or they list appliances.
- `flux-controller/tests/integration/test_modbus.py:26` carries a stale wrong base (`0xFFFFFFFF00000000`); fix while touching ranges.

**0.2 Node-ID kinds** — `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:158-167`: keep `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` on the wire, add `flux_synth_kind()`, `flux_is_synthetic_node()`, `flux_is_hc_node()`, `FLUX_HC_NODE_BASE`. Kind ≤ 0x7F makes the bit-63 rule structural. Convert the ~10 "not a Matter node" guards (`flux_controller.cpp:469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126`; `coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:384,477`; `energy/flux_energy_log.c:44`) to `flux_is_synthetic_node` / kind switches. Leave `modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:141` as a genuine Modbus-only guard. New ADR.

**0.3 Extract the PSRAM-safe NVS helper** — new `firmware/main/platform/flux_nvs_blob.{c,h}`, lifted from `prices/flux_prices.c:94-197`, and refactor `flux_prices.c` onto it. This is the *abort-the-box* hazard: HTTPS tasks need PSRAM stacks, but SPI-flash writes disable the cache which unmaps PSRAM. Every NVS access must marshal to a short-lived internal-RAM worker (`xTaskNotifyGive`/`ulTaskNotifyTake`, not a caller-stack semaphore).

**0.4 Command bus** — new dir `firmware/main/devices/` (add to **both** `SRC_DIRS` and `INCLUDE_DIRS` in `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4`):

```c
typedef struct {
    const char *name;  uint8_t kind;   /* 0 = real Matter node, else flux_synth_kind() */
    esp_err_t (*invoke)(uint64_t node, uint32_t ep, uint32_t cluster, uint32_t cmd,
                        const flux_CommandArg *args, size_t n);
    esp_err_t (*write)(...);  esp_err_t (*read)(...);
    esp_err_t (*defer_start)(uint64_t node, uint32_t delay_s, uint32_t *granted_s); /* Phase 3 */
} flux_device_backend_t;
void flux_device_cmd_register(const flux_device_backend_t *b);   /* boot-only */
```
Fixed `static const flux_device_backend_t *s_backends[4]`, written boot-only, read lock-free — same justification as the `flux_events` sink pointer. `matter/flux_controller.cpp` gains a ~20-line registration wrapper; `coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:1090/1131/1173` call `flux_device_cmd_*`. Unknown kind → `ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, i.e. **outwardly identical to today**. New ADR; add `s_backends` to the ownership table in `docs/threading.md`.

## Phase 1 — account linking + monitoring

### 1a. Auth bootstrap

App flow: Settings → Home Connect → paste client id/secret (with the 5-step `developer.home-connect.com` walkthrough) → **Connect account** → `GET /homeconnect/authorize-url` → `flutter_web_auth_2` opens the system browser (`preferEphemeral: true`) → Bosch's own login page → redirect `fluxhome://homeconnect/callback?code=…&state=…` → app POSTs the code to the controller → controller exchanges it and persists only the refresh token.

- **Only one new app dependency: `flutter_web_auth_2` ^4.x.** It wraps Android Custom Tabs + iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession`. Reject `webview_flutter` as a *design constraint*: an embedded webview lets the flux process observe the user's Bosch password, contradicting the disclosure copy below.
- Platform config: Android `MainActivity` gains a `VIEW`+`BROWSABLE` intent-filter with `<data android:scheme="fluxhome"/>`; iOS `Info.plist` gains `CFBundleURLTypes`. Neither exists today.
- **Secret and code writes are LAN-only** (ADR-0012). Refuse them over the remote/ICE path, and have the app refuse to *start* the flow when `hub.connectionKind == ConnectionKind.remote`, saying why.
- `GET /homeconnect/client` and `/config` **redact** secrets to `has_client_secret` / `has_refresh_token` booleans. Explicitly do *not* copy `PricingConfig.api_token`, which round-trips in cleartext through `GET /prices/config`.
- Two-level teardown: `DELETE /homeconnect/auth` unlinks the account but keeps client credentials (so re-linking after a lapsed refresh token doesn't re-ask for the secret); `DELETE /homeconnect/client` is the full forget.
- Also ship a collapsed **Advanced → paste a token** affordance (~20 lines) — the only way to drive the developer simulator from `curl`.

### 1b. Firmware subsystem

New `firmware/main/homeconnect/` (add to both CMake lists):

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `flux_homeconnect.c/.h` | State machine, backoff, quota, task creation, resync orchestration (`hc_ctl` task). Header states the **no-NVS-on-hc-tasks** invariant. |
| `flux_hc_auth.c` | The only module touching the token store. `POST {base}/security/oauth/token`, `grant_type=refresh_token` / `authorization_code`. |
| `flux_hc_rest.c` | Bearer/Accept-aware GET/PUT/DELETE; bounded body; **quota gate ahead of every request**; 429/`Retry-After` handling. |
| `flux_hc_sse.c` | `hc_sse` task: long-lived stream, read loop. |
| `flux_hc_sse_parse.c` | **Pure** incremental SSE framer — host-testable (ADR-0010). |
| `flux_hc_map.c` | **Pure** HC key/value → flux attr key/type/value. The analogue of `flux_modbus_profile.c`. Host-testable. |
| `flux_hc_registry.c` | `haId ↔ node_id` registry, NVS ns `flux_hc`, mirroring the Modbus-registry idiom in `flux_state.c` (own mutex created at boot, monotonic id counter, compaction on remove). Deliberately **not** in `flux_state.c` — that file is one line under the split canary. |
| `flux_coap_homeconnect.c` | CoAP handlers (new file — `flux_coap_handlers.c` is the canary). |

Reuse: the HTTPS/cJSON/provider-registry patterns in `prices/flux_prices_http.c` + `flux_prices_awattar.c:53-90` + `flux_prices_provider.h:18-33`; the POST template in `remote/flux_remote_rendezvous.c:112-124`; `flux_hangwatch_register/kick`.

**Appliance → device.** Each appliance gets a `0x02…` node ID and is mirrored into the shared `"flux_dev"` registry via `flux_device_upsert()` exactly as `modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:104-122` does (`vendor_id 0xFFF1`, `product_id 0x8001`, rollback on "table full"). Device types, verified against the 1.5 spec: Dishwasher `0x0075`, Laundry Washer `0x0073`, Dryer `0x007C`, Refrigerator `0x0070`, Oven `0x007B`. `GET /devices` then lists them with zero branching; the app **auto-adopts** them via `DeviceProvider._reconcileWithController` (`device_provider.dart:399-429`) with no new add-flow.

**Attributes.** Push via `flux_events_emit_attr(node, key, which, …)`. Note a correction to a common assumption: `kAttrMap` (`flux_controller.cpp:72-110`) only maps Matter `(cluster,attr) → key` inside the report callback — it is **not** on the emit path, which is why Modbus needs no `kAttrMap` edit. Add the four entries whose `(cluster,attr)` pairs genuinely carry these values anyway, so a real Matter appliance emits identical keys.

| HC key | flux attr key | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `BSH.Common.Status.OperationState` | `operationalState` | → Matter `OperationalStateEnum`; **DelayedStart → `0x80`** (flux-private) |
| `…Option.RemainingProgramTime` | `countdownTime` | seconds |
| `…Root.ActiveProgram` / `.SelectedProgram` | `currentMode` | **index** into the appliance's program list |
| `…Setting.PowerState` | `onOff` | existing key |
| `…Option.ProgramProgress` / `ElapsedProgramTime` / `EstimatedTotalProgramTime` / `StartInRelative` | `programProgress`, `elapsedS`, `totalProgramTimeS`, `startInS` | |
| `…Status.DoorState` / `RemoteControlStartAllowed` / `RemoteControlActive` | `applianceDoorOpen`, `remoteStartAllowed`, `remoteControlActive` | bools |
| SSE `CONNECTED`/`DISCONNECTED`/`PAIRED`/`DEPAIRED` | — | `flux_events_emit_device(ESTABLISHED / RESUBSCRIBING / ERROR)`; **never auto-remove** |

Program *names* cannot travel on the attribute stream — `flux.Attr`'s oneof has no string type. So programs are enumerated once via `GET /homeconnect/programs?id=` and referenced by index, exactly as Matter's Mode Base cluster does (`SupportedModes` read separately, `CurrentMode` as a uint8).

**Tasks.** `hc_ctl` (20 KiB, `MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM`, prio 3) and `hc_sse` (16 KiB, PSRAM, prio 3), both hangwatch-registered at 180 s (must exceed the 90 s read timeout). PSRAM because a TLS handshake against the full 200-cert bundle plus a cJSON parse won't fit internal RAM — the precedent `flux_prices` already set. Splitting into two tasks isn't only about the shared-handle problem: it lets `hc_sse` be a pure consumer of a mutex-protected RAM token cache with no persistence path at all, making the PSRAM/NVS hazard structurally impossible on the task most likely to be edited later. Force the SSE line buffer and REST accumulator to PSRAM explicitly (`heap_caps_malloc(MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM)`) — sub-16 KiB `malloc` lands in internal RAM under `SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL`.

**SSE.** All-appliances stream `GET {base}/api/homeappliances/events`, one socket for the whole home. `Accept: text/event-stream`, `.timeout_ms = 90000` (KEEP-ALIVE is ~55 s), never `esp_http_client_perform()` — loop on `esp_http_client_read()`, kicking hangwatch per chunk. Track last-byte-received time *ourselves* and treat >90 s of silence as dead, independent of what `read()` returns.

**Failure machine.** `DISABLED → NEED_AUTH → SYNCING → STREAMING`, with `BACKOFF` (5 s ×3, ±25 % jitter, cap 1800 s; reset only after a *successfully streamed event*, not on connect) and `THROTTLED` (honour `Retry-After`, clamp 60 s–24 h, default 1 h). `blocked_until` is **persisted** so a crash-loop can't escape it. `invalid_grant` → `NEED_AUTH` and **never retry a rejected refresh token** — that's the fastest route to a 24 h block. Quota guard (`min_gap 2 s`, ≤60/h, ≤500/day) refuses without touching the network and the refusal is returned in `BoolResult.error`, never silently swallowed. Under throttle/stream-drop, cached attributes are **retained** so the app still shows last-known values.

**NVS ns `flux_hc`:** `cfg` (config, no secrets), `sec` (client secret + refresh token, separate key so config writes don't rewrite it), `count`, `id_ctr`, `ha_0..7`, `blk` (blocked_until), `req_n`/`req_day`. **The access token is never persisted** — the `nvs` partition is only 24 KiB and shared with the device/Modbus registries, price curve and remote config; one refresh at boot costs one request.

**Endpoints** (declared in `coap/flux_coap_internal.h`, registered in `coap_task()` at `coap/flux_coap.c:~220`): `GET/POST/DELETE /homeconnect/client`, `GET /homeconnect/authorize-url`, `POST/DELETE /homeconnect/auth`, `GET /homeconnect/status`, `POST /homeconnect/discover` (returns immediately; appliances arrive via `/events`), `GET /homeconnect/appliances`, `GET /homeconnect/programs?id=`, `DELETE /homeconnect/appliances?id=`. `DELETE /devices?id=` (`flux_coap_handlers.c:477`) must also clean the HC registry, or an appliance keeps streaming while invisible.

**Boot wiring** (`firmware/main/app_main.cpp`): `flux_homeconnect_init()` in the mutex block at `:445-455` beside the other inits (state mutex must exist before `flux_coap_start()` serves `/homeconnect/*`); `flux_homeconnect_start()` after `flux_prices_start()` at `:478`, because token expiry and `blocked_until` are wall-clock and need `flux_time_is_synced()`.

### 1c. App rendering

- New `DeviceType` values (dishwasher, laundryWasher, laundryDryer, refrigerator, oven) + icons + an `isAppliance` flag in `lib/models/device_type.dart`.
- New live readouts: one entry each in `_kLiveRenderers` + one `_render*` function in `lib/services/cluster_parser.dart:259-283` — the file's own doc comment (`:193-194`) confirms nothing else needs changing. `DeviceLiveData.attrs` is open-ended, so no model change.
- New read-only appliance card under `lib/ui/screens/device_detail/`, modelled on `smoke_alarm_card.dart`: operation state, program, remaining time / progress, door, and a clear "enable Remote Start on the appliance" hint when `remoteStartAllowed` is false.
- **No new `HomeCategory` yet.** Most appliances report no power, so `HomeCategory.energy.matches` won't claim them and they'll live in the home-screen room grid plus the Home Connect management screen. Filling the Energy grid with dishwashers that contribute nothing to the energy scene would be worse than absence. If wanted later: adding a 4th value squeezes `category_bar.dart`'s fixed `Row(Expanded)` (~74 px pills at 360 dp → "Applia…"); switch it to a 2×2 `Wrap`, ~6 lines. Routing needs no change (`router.dart:37-43` resolves any enum name).
- **Entry point:** Settings → CONTROLLER → "Home Connect", one `_navTile` after "Remote access" (`settings_screen.dart:44-49`), subtitle carrying live `HomeConnectStatus`. This *satisfies* rather than violates the "phone has nothing to configure" decree at `:18-20` — the token, stream and devices are all controller-scoped, so it belongs next to Matter/Thread/Remote access. Discoverability is a Phase 3 follow-up: convert the home FAB (`home_screen.dart:104-112`) into a three-row add-chooser (Matter code / Home Connect / Modbus meter), reusing the sheet shape from `modbus_devices_screen.dart:200-220` — which also un-buries Modbus from inside the Energy card.

## Phase 2 — control

- `homeconnect/flux_hc_backend.c` registers `{ .kind = FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_CLOUD, … }` on the Phase 0.4 bus. `invoke()` validates, enqueues onto a length-8 queue on `hc_ctl`, and returns `ESP_OK` meaning **accepted, not done** — the outcome arrives as an attribute event. That is not a compromise: `flux_send_device_command_args()` already only means "scheduled onto the CHIP task". The CoAP task must never block on a cloud PUT.
- Matter-verb mapping (cluster/command IDs verified against the vendored 1.5 Application Cluster spec): OnOff `0x0006` on/off → `PUT /settings/BSH.Common.Setting.PowerState`; OperationalState `0x0060` Start `0x02` → `PUT /programs/active`, Stop `0x01` → `DELETE /programs/active`, Pause `0x00` / Resume `0x03` → `PUT /commands/BSH.Common.Command.{Pause,Resume}Program` *(verify — appliance-specific)*; Mode cluster ChangeToMode → `PUT /programs/selected`.
- Plus `POST /homeconnect/command` ← `HomeConnectCommand{node_id, action, start_in_seconds, program_key}` for what Matter cannot express (`StartInRelative`, program options, selected-vs-active). A manufacturer-specific cluster was rejected: it needs a vendor ID we don't own and the app would need bespoke encoders anyway — all the cost of an explicit endpoint with none of its clarity.
- **Safety gates enforced locally, before any request** (so a guaranteed 403 never burns quota): refuse Start unless `remoteStartAllowed`; refuse when disconnected or door open; refuse Start while already Running; one in-flight command per appliance so a double-tap can't produce two PUTs; return quota refusals to the app.
- App: wire the appliance card's actions through `DeviceProvider` following the optimistic-merge-then-rollback shape of `toggle` (`device_provider.dart:906`), keeping `retryOnConnError: false` (commands aren't idempotent).

## Phase 3 — price-aware deferral

New `firmware/main/flexload/`: `flux_flexload.c`, `flux_flex_plan.c` (**pure**, host-tested), `flux_coap_flex.c`. Dependencies point outward only: `flexload → prices` (**the first caller of `flux_prices_at()`**), `flexload → devices` (`defer_start`), `flexload → flux_state.h` (`flux_energy_role_of`). It never speaks HTTP and never mentions Home Connect.

**User-visible contract:** *"Run before 07:00, in the cheapest 2 h window. The hub never starts an appliance itself — it only delays a run you already started."*

- Policy per node: mode, `deadline_minute`, `max_delay_s` (default 12 h), `duration_s` (0 = ask the appliance via `EstimatedTotalProgramTime`), `require_user_start` (default true). NVS ns `flux_flex`. Endpoints `GET/POST /flex/policies`, `GET /flex/plan` (exposes chosen start, delay, expected saving and a `reason` string for the UI).
- Algorithm: slide an `n = ceil(duration/resolution)` window over `[now, deadline − duration]`, minimise summed price, ties → **earliest**. Require ≥2 intervals of forward coverage beyond the window. Task: 4 KiB **internal** stack, 60 s tick, no network, no NVS on the tick.
- Trigger: `hc_sse` reports `operationalState == 0x80` (DelayedStart), or an `HC_START` on a node with a policy → `flux_device_cmd_defer_start()`. HC implements it as `StartInRelative` — as an option on `PUT /programs/active` at start, then via `PUT /programs/active/options/…` while in DelayedStart. The Matter backend returns `NOT_SUPPORTED`.
- Only nodes whose `flux_energy_role_of()` is LOAD or UNKNOWN are considered.
- **Failure behaviour, chosen:** no/stale price curve → **start now** (`reason="no price data"`) — a price-aware scheduler must degrade to "behaves exactly like today", never to "the dishwasher never runs". Deadline too close → start now. Optimum > `max_delay_s` → clamp. Appliance offline → hold the plan, retry on `CONNECTED`, abandon past `deadline − duration`. `remoteStartAllowed == false` → **never defer** (deferring commits us to a remote start we're not permitted to make). **User stopped the program → plan cancelled and not re-armed**, latched in NVS until a new user-initiated start. Re-evaluate at most every 15 min and only ever *increase* the delay (each change is a cloud PUT = quota).
- **Known gap:** `platform/flux_time.c` is UTC-only (`gmtime_r`, no `setenv("TZ")`/`tzset()`), so `deadline_minute` can't be resolved as local time today. `PricingConfig.fetch_hour_local` already promises local-hour scheduling and is likewise unimplemented — fix both together with a POSIX TZ string and `localtime_r`.

## Proto workflow

New messages: `HomeConnectClient`, `HomeConnectConfig`, `HomeConnectAuth`, `HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl`, `HomeConnectStatus`, `HomeConnectAppliance(+List)`, `HomeConnectProgram(+List)`, `HomeConnectCommand`, `FlexLoadPolicy(+List)`, `FlexLoadPlan(+List)`; enums `HomeConnectState`, `HomeConnectType`, `HcAction`, `FlexLoadMode`. **Every** string/bytes/repeated field needs a `max_size`/`max_count` in `flux.options` (no heap, no callbacks). Keep the program list a **separate** message keyed per appliance — nested, the appliance list would exceed 10 KB and force block2.

The shared proto is a submodule checked out as `flux-controller/proto` and `flux-app/flux-interface` (upstream `~/workspace/flux/flux-proto`). **These checkouts are currently diverged — never blind-copy between them; edit each deliberately.** Then regenerate: `cd proto && make c` (nanopb), `make dart` (needs `~/.pub-cache/bin` on PATH), plus `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/flux_pb2.py` and `tests/integration/flux_pb2.py`.

## Verification

1. **Verify before writing Phase 1 auth code:** does Home Connect support RFC 8628 Device Flow? If yes, the *entire* app-side OAuth stack disappears — no `flutter_web_auth_2`, no manifest/plist changes, no redirect registration — and the controller runs the grant itself while the app just shows a code and URL. That is strictly better; the contract above is shaped so `GET /homeconnect/device-code` is purely additive.
2. **Simulator first, always.** Point `base_url` at the developer simulator until the backoff machine is proven, *including* the crash-loop case (cut power during BACKOFF, confirm `blocked_until` survives). Live rate-limit blocks last up to 24 h and are effectively unrecoverable.
3. Host tests (ADR-0010): `firmware/test/host/test_hc_sse_parse.c` and `test_hc_map.c` — the framer and the mapper are where a silent bug hides. Plus `test_flex_plan.c` for the window search.
4. `flux-ctl hc {client,auth,config,status,discover,ls,rm}` and `flux-ctl flex {policies,plan}`, modelled on the `modbus` group (`cli.py:1370-1500`), so every phase is testable without the app.
5. `tests/integration/test_homeconnect.py`, gated on a `--hc-refresh-token`/`--hc-simulator` option in the existing `conftest.py` style. Assert: config round-trip **redacts** secrets; `/devices` lists the appliance with the right `device_type`; `/devices/attrs` carries the expected keys; `enabled=false` produces zero outbound traffic.
6. End-to-end on hardware: flash (`cd firmware && source esp-env.sh && idf.py build && idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash` — stop `serial_logger.py` first, it holds the port), link the account, confirm the appliance appears in the app, toggle power, then set a deferral policy and confirm the chosen window matches `flux-ctl prices` by hand.
7. App: `flutter analyze` clean (0 errors/warnings) and `flutter test` green; `flutter build apk` **before** install (a plain install ships a stale cached APK).

## Positioning / copy

The app currently claims flux runs no cloud (`remote_access_screen.dart:9,220`; pubspec "Local, private, independent"). That claim has to become precise rather than lawyered: flux itself still runs no cloud and holds no account of yours, **and** Home Connect is Bosch's cloud, opt-in, using *your* developer client, with appliance state and commands travelling between your controller and Bosch. The Home Connect screen should say plainly what leaves the house, and note that the Bosch login is entered on Bosch's own page so flux never sees it (which is exactly why an embedded webview is rejected).

## Risks

1. **`esp_http_client` for a never-ending SSE stream is the biggest assumption** — the client is request/response shaped. Unverified: `esp_http_client_read()`'s return on socket timeout with an open chunked body, and how to read `Retry-After` (needs an `HTTP_EVENT_ON_HEADER` handler). The last-byte-timestamp watchdog makes us robust to the first. **Budget the fallback:** `esp_tls` + hand-rolled minimal HTTP/1.1, ~200 lines — precedent exists (ADR-0005 hand-rolled the MeshCoP DTLS client).
2. **`CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS=16`** is shared by CoAP, mDNS, Matter, the rendezvous poller and up to 8 Modbus pollers; HC pins one permanently and two during a REST call. Raise it to 20 in `sdkconfig.defaults` or refuse to enable HC above 6 Modbus devices. This is the most likely "works on the bench, dies in the field" failure.
3. **NVS is 24 KiB and not actually encrypted** (`partitions.csv` marks it encrypted for future flash encryption, but `CONFIG_NVS_ENCRYPTION` is unset) — the refresh token sits in plaintext flash on a dev unit. Measure headroom with `nvs_get_stats()` before shipping; if tight, the honest fix is a partition change, which **cannot** be delivered by OTA.
4. **The PSRAM/NVS abort** is mitigated structurally, but one carelessly added `nvs_set_*` on `hc_ctl` reintroduces a hard crash. Put the invariant in `flux_homeconnect.h` *and* `docs/threading.md`, not just a commit message.
5. `FLUX_DEVICES_MAX` and `ATTR_CACHE_MAX_NODES` (both 32) are now shared across Matter + Modbus + Home Connect.
6. **To verify against the live API/simulator:** Pause/Resume command support (appliance-specific); whether `haId` arrives in the SSE `id:` field or the JSON body (handle both); `items[].value` type mixing (bool/number/string per key); which Mode cluster the Dryer and WasherDryer types mandate; and that **`StartInRelative` availability is per program and per appliance** and cannot be sent with a program *selection* — read `GET /programs/available/{key}` at discovery and surface `supports_delayed_start`, or Phase 3 silently does nothing for some appliances.
7. BYO credentials will lose some users at the first screen. Mitigated by the walkthrough copy and by keeping the feature clearly optional.

# Home Connect (Bosch/Siemens) integration into flux

## Context

flux is a local-first smart-home controller (ESP32-P4 + esp-matter + OTBR) with a Flutter app, recently pivoted toward **energy management**: it fetches EPEX day-ahead prices and logs per-device energy. `docs/epex-day-ahead-pricing.md:118-122` describes a "phase 2 — act on price" that is unimplemented; `flux_prices_at()` (`firmware/main/prices/flux_prices.c:354`) has **zero callers** today.

Home Connect appliances (dishwasher, washer, dryer) are the ideal deferrable load: the API exposes `BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative`, so a run the user has already asked for can be slid into the cheapest price window. That makes this integration both a device-coverage win and the first real consumer of the pricing subsystem.

The appliances in question are not Matter-capable (BSH's Matter rollout covers only newer fridges natively, plus some models via the Smart Kitchen Dock bridge; most existing appliances cannot be upgraded), so the cloud API is the only way to reach them.

**Intended outcome:** appliances appear as ordinary flux devices with live state, are controllable from the app, and can have their start deferred into the cheapest hours — with the token, the event stream and all control living on the controller so it works when the phone is away.

## Decisions (locked)

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Controller owns the runtime.** It holds the refresh token, keeps one Server-Sent-Events stream open, and executes all commands. The app only bootstraps auth and renders. | Must work with the phone away; price scheduling belongs next to the price data; appliances then flow through the existing `/devices` + `/events` contract with almost no app plumbing. |
| D2 | **Bring-your-own Home Connect developer client.** The user registers a free client at `developer.home-connect.com` and enters id/secret once; both are stored **only** on the controller. | Whoever refreshes needs the `client_secret`, and that is the controller — forever, unattended. Rate-limit blocks are per-client and last minutes to 24 h, so a shipped shared `client_id` would let one bad actor break every household. Nothing extractable ships in the APK. Mirrors the existing BYO-TURN pattern (`lib/ui/screens/settings/remote_access_screen.dart:9,220`). |
| D3 | **Phone does the `authorize` step only; the controller exchanges the code.** The app fetches the authorize URL *from* the controller, so the app ships no credentials at all — not even the `client_id`. | The authorization code is single-use, short-lived and redirect-bound: safe to pass over the existing DTLS/CoAP channel. Having the phone do the exchange would put the secret in *two* places for zero gain. |
| D4 | **Synthetic node IDs get a kind nibble.** Modbus stays `0x01…`; Home Connect becomes `0x02…`. | ADR-0009 makes "bit 63 clear" a cross-repo contract. Today the app's test is a bare threshold (`nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000`), so an HC node would silently render as a Modbus device. |
| D5 | **New neutral command bus** `devices/flux_device_cmd.c`; Matter and Home Connect each register a backend. | A dispatch layer does not exist — `flux_send_device_command_args()` (`firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:985`) rejects synthetic nodes at `:995`. Branching inside `flux_controller.cpp` would create a `matter → cloud` dependency, the inversion ADR-0008 exists to prevent. |
| D6 | **Matter clusters where a faithful mapping exists; an explicit HC endpoint where it doesn't.** | OnOff/OperationalState/Mode clusters were written for exactly these appliances, so a future *real* Matter dishwasher works through the same path. But `StartInRelative`, per-program option sets and selected-vs-active have no Matter representation; faking a cluster ID would collide later and be undiscoverable. |
| D7 | **Scheduling lives in a separate `flexload/` subsystem**, not in `homeconnect/`. | The same policy must later drive the battery and wallbox. |
| D8 | **The controller never starts an appliance on its own initiative — it only delays a run the user already started.** | This is the whole safety model, and it is also the user-visible contract. |

## Phase 0 — prerequisites (no new behaviour, independently mergeable)

Land these first; each is a small reviewable diff.

**0.1 App + tooling range fixes (ship first — no-ops until HC exists)**
- `flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart:125` — replace the threshold `isModbus` with kind decode; add `isHomeConnect`. Same at `lib/providers/device_provider.dart:408` (duplicated magic number) and `:345`.
- **Fix the real bug at `flux-app/lib/models/device_type.dart:147`**: `0x0073 => airQualitySensor` is wrong — `0x0073` is Matter **Laundry Washer**; Air Quality Sensor is `0x002C`, already correct on line 148. The fix is a deletion. Verified against the vendored `docs/23-27351-008_Matter-1.5-Device-Library-Specification.pdf`. Left in place, every washer renders as an air-quality sensor. Same conflation in `lib/ui/screens/cluster_inspector_screen.dart:40` and `docs/SUPPORTED_DEVICES.md:54,71`.
- `flux-controller/tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/cli.py:~1373` — `modbus ls`/`rm` must filter a **range**, not `>= base`, or they list appliances.
- `flux-controller/tests/integration/test_modbus.py:26` carries a stale wrong base (`0xFFFFFFFF00000000`); fix while touching ranges.

**0.2 Node-ID kinds** — `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:158-167`: keep `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` on the wire, add `flux_synth_kind()`, `flux_is_synthetic_node()`, `flux_is_hc_node()`, `FLUX_HC_NODE_BASE`. Kind ≤ 0x7F makes the bit-63 rule structural. Convert the ~10 "not a Matter node" guards (`flux_controller.cpp:469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126`; `coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:384,477`; `energy/flux_energy_log.c:44`) to `flux_is_synthetic_node` / kind switches. Leave `modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:141` as a genuine Modbus-only guard. New ADR.

**0.3 Extract the PSRAM-safe NVS helper** — new `firmware/main/platform/flux_nvs_blob.{c,h}`, lifted from `prices/flux_prices.c:94-197`, and refactor `flux_prices.c` onto it. This is the *abort-the-box* hazard: HTTPS tasks need PSRAM stacks, but SPI-flash writes disable the cache which unmaps PSRAM. Every NVS access must marshal to a short-lived internal-RAM worker (`xTaskNotifyGive`/`ulTaskNotifyTake`, not a caller-stack semaphore).

**0.4 Command bus** — new dir `firmware/main/devices/` (add to **both** `SRC_DIRS` and `INCLUDE_DIRS` in `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4`):

```c
typedef struct {
    const char *name;  uint8_t kind;   /* 0 = real Matter node, else flux_synth_kind() */
    esp_err_t (*invoke)(uint64_t node, uint32_t ep, uint32_t cluster, uint32_t cmd,
                        const flux_CommandArg *args, size_t n);
    esp_err_t (*write)(...);  esp_err_t (*read)(...);
    esp_err_t (*defer_start)(uint64_t node, uint32_t delay_s, uint32_t *granted_s); /* Phase 3 */
} flux_device_backend_t;
void flux_device_cmd_register(const flux_device_backend_t *b);   /* boot-only */
```
Fixed `static const flux_device_backend_t *s_backends[4]`, written boot-only, read lock-free — same justification as the `flux_events` sink pointer. `matter/flux_controller.cpp` gains a ~20-line registration wrapper; `coap/flux_coap_handlers.c:1090/1131/1173` call `flux_device_cmd_*`. Unknown kind → `ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED`, i.e. **outwardly identical to today**. New ADR; add `s_backends` to the ownership table in `docs/threading.md`.

## Phase 1 — account linking + monitoring

### 1a. Auth bootstrap

App flow: Settings → Home Connect → paste client id/secret (with the 5-step `developer.home-connect.com` walkthrough) → **Connect account** → `GET /homeconnect/authorize-url` → `flutter_web_auth_2` opens the system browser (`preferEphemeral: true`) → Bosch's own login page → redirect `fluxhome://homeconnect/callback?code=…&state=…` → app POSTs the code to the controller → controller exchanges it and persists only the refresh token.

- **Only one new app dependency: `flutter_web_auth_2` ^4.x.** It wraps Android Custom Tabs + iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession`. Reject `webview_flutter` as a *design constraint*: an embedded webview lets the flux process observe the user's Bosch password, contradicting the disclosure copy below.
- Platform config: Android `MainActivity` gains a `VIEW`+`BROWSABLE` intent-filter with `<data android:scheme="fluxhome"/>`; iOS `Info.plist` gains `CFBundleURLTypes`. Neither exists today.
- **Secret and code writes are LAN-only** (ADR-0012). Refuse them over the remote/ICE path, and have the app refuse to *start* the flow when `hub.connectionKind == ConnectionKind.remote`, saying why.
- `GET /homeconnect/client` and `/config` **redact** secrets to `has_client_secret` / `has_refresh_token` booleans. Explicitly do *not* copy `PricingConfig.api_token`, which round-trips in cleartext through `GET /prices/config`.
- Two-level teardown: `DELETE /homeconnect/auth` unlinks the account but keeps client credentials (so re-linking after a lapsed refresh token doesn't re-ask for the secret); `DELETE /homeconnect/client` is the full forget.
- Also ship a collapsed **Advanced → paste a token** affordance (~20 lines) — the only way to drive the developer simulator from `curl`.

### 1b. Firmware subsystem

New `firmware/main/homeconnect/` (add to both CMake lists):

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `flux_homeconnect.c/.h` | State machine, backoff, quota, task creation, resync orchestration (`hc_ctl` task). Header states the **no-NVS-on-hc-tasks** invariant. |
| `flux_hc_auth.c` | The only module touching the token store. `POST {base}/security/oauth/token`, `grant_type=refresh_token` / `authorization_code`. |
| `flux_hc_rest.c` | Bearer/Accept-aware GET/PUT/DELETE; bounded body; **quota gate ahead of every request**; 429/`Retry-After` handling. |
| `flux_hc_sse.c` | `hc_sse` task: long-lived stream, read loop. |
| `flux_hc_sse_parse.c` | **Pure** incremental SSE framer — host-testable (ADR-0010). |
| `flux_hc_map.c` | **Pure** HC key/value → flux attr key/type/value. The analogue of `flux_modbus_profile.c`. Host-testable. |
| `flux_hc_registry.c` | `haId ↔ node_id` registry, NVS ns `flux_hc`, mirroring the Modbus-registry idiom in `flux_state.c` (own mutex created at boot, monotonic id counter, compaction on remove). Deliberately **not** in `flux_state.c` — that file is one line under the split canary. |
| `flux_coap_homeconnect.c` | CoAP handlers (new file — `flux_coap_handlers.c` is the canary). |

Reuse: the HTTPS/cJSON/provider-registry patterns in `prices/flux_prices_http.c` + `flux_prices_awattar.c:53-90` + `flux_prices_provider.h:18-33`; the POST template in `remote/flux_remote_rendezvous.c:112-124`; `flux_hangwatch_register/kick`.

**Appliance → device.** Each appliance gets a `0x02…` node ID and is mirrored into the shared `"flux_dev"` registry via `flux_device_upsert()` exactly as `modbus/flux_coap_modbus.c:104-122` does (`vendor_id 0xFFF1`, `product_id 0x8001`, rollback on "table full"). Device types, verified against the 1.5 spec: Dishwasher `0x0075`, Laundry Washer `0x0073`, Dryer `0x007C`, Refrigerator `0x0070`, Oven `0x007B`. `GET /devices` then lists them with zero branching; the app **auto-adopts** them via `DeviceProvider._reconcileWithController` (`device_provider.dart:399-429`) with no new add-flow.

**Attributes.** Push via `flux_events_emit_attr(node, key, which, …)`. Note a correction to a common assumption: `kAttrMap` (`flux_controller.cpp:72-110`) only maps Matter `(cluster,attr) → key` inside the report callback — it is **not** on the emit path, which is why Modbus needs no `kAttrMap` edit. Add the four entries whose `(cluster,attr)` pairs genuinely carry these values anyway, so a real Matter appliance emits identical keys.

| HC key | flux attr key | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `BSH.Common.Status.OperationState` | `operationalState` | → Matter `OperationalStateEnum`; **DelayedStart → `0x80`** (flux-private) |
| `…Option.RemainingProgramTime` | `countdownTime` | seconds |
| `…Root.ActiveProgram` / `.SelectedProgram` | `currentMode` | **index** into the appliance's program list |
| `…Setting.PowerState` | `onOff` | existing key |
| `…Option.ProgramProgress` / `ElapsedProgramTime` / `EstimatedTotalProgramTime` / `StartInRelative` | `programProgress`, `elapsedS`, `totalProgramTimeS`, `startInS` | |
| `…Status.DoorState` / `RemoteControlStartAllowed` / `RemoteControlActive` | `applianceDoorOpen`, `remoteStartAllowed`, `remoteControlActive` | bools |
| SSE `CONNECTED`/`DISCONNECTED`/`PAIRED`/`DEPAIRED` | — | `flux_events_emit_device(ESTABLISHED / RESUBSCRIBING / ERROR)`; **never auto-remove** |

Program *names* cannot travel on the attribute stream — `flux.Attr`'s oneof has no string type. So programs are enumerated once via `GET /homeconnect/programs?id=` and referenced by index, exactly as Matter's Mode Base cluster does (`SupportedModes` read separately, `CurrentMode` as a uint8).

**Tasks.** `hc_ctl` (20 KiB, `MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM`, prio 3) and `hc_sse` (16 KiB, PSRAM, prio 3), both hangwatch-registered at 180 s (must exceed the 90 s read timeout). PSRAM because a TLS handshake against the full 200-cert bundle plus a cJSON parse won't fit internal RAM — the precedent `flux_prices` already set. Splitting into two tasks isn't only about the shared-handle problem: it lets `hc_sse` be a pure consumer of a mutex-protected RAM token cache with no persistence path at all, making the PSRAM/NVS hazard structurally impossible on the task most likely to be edited later. Force the SSE line buffer and REST accumulator to PSRAM explicitly (`heap_caps_malloc(MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM)`) — sub-16 KiB `malloc` lands in internal RAM under `SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL`.

**SSE.** All-appliances stream `GET {base}/api/homeappliances/events`, one socket for the whole home. `Accept: text/event-stream`, `.timeout_ms = 90000` (KEEP-ALIVE is ~55 s), never `esp_http_client_perform()` — loop on `esp_http_client_read()`, kicking hangwatch per chunk. Track last-byte-received time *ourselves* and treat >90 s of silence as dead, independent of what `read()` returns.

**Failure machine.** `DISABLED → NEED_AUTH → SYNCING → STREAMING`, with `BACKOFF` (5 s ×3, ±25 % jitter, cap 1800 s; reset only after a *successfully streamed event*, not on connect) and `THROTTLED` (honour `Retry-After`, clamp 60 s–24 h, default 1 h). `blocked_until` is **persisted** so a crash-loop can't escape it. `invalid_grant` → `NEED_AUTH` and **never retry a rejected refresh token** — that's the fastest route to a 24 h block. Quota guard (`min_gap 2 s`, ≤60/h, ≤500/day) refuses without touching the network and the refusal is returned in `BoolResult.error`, never silently swallowed. Under throttle/stream-drop, cached attributes are **retained** so the app still shows last-known values.

**NVS ns `flux_hc`:** `cfg` (config, no secrets), `sec` (client secret + refresh token, separate key so config writes don't rewrite it), `count`, `id_ctr`, `ha_0..7`, `blk` (blocked_until), `req_n`/`req_day`. **The access token is never persisted** — the `nvs` partition is only 24 KiB and shared with the device/Modbus registries, price curve and remote config; one refresh at boot costs one request.

**Endpoints** (declared in `coap/flux_coap_internal.h`, registered in `coap_task()` at `coap/flux_coap.c:~220`): `GET/POST/DELETE /homeconnect/client`, `GET /homeconnect/authorize-url`, `POST/DELETE /homeconnect/auth`, `GET /homeconnect/status`, `POST /homeconnect/discover` (returns immediately; appliances arrive via `/events`), `GET /homeconnect/appliances`, `GET /homeconnect/programs?id=`, `DELETE /homeconnect/appliances?id=`. `DELETE /devices?id=` (`flux_coap_handlers.c:477`) must also clean the HC registry, or an appliance keeps streaming while invisible.

**Boot wiring** (`firmware/main/app_main.cpp`): `flux_homeconnect_init()` in the mutex block at `:445-455` beside the other inits (state mutex must exist before `flux_coap_start()` serves `/homeconnect/*`); `flux_homeconnect_start()` after `flux_prices_start()` at `:478`, because token expiry and `blocked_until` are wall-clock and need `flux_time_is_synced()`.

### 1c. App rendering

- New `DeviceType` values (dishwasher, laundryWasher, laundryDryer, refrigerator, oven) + icons + an `isAppliance` flag in `lib/models/device_type.dart`.
- New live readouts: one entry each in `_kLiveRenderers` + one `_render*` function in `lib/services/cluster_parser.dart:259-283` — the file's own doc comment (`:193-194`) confirms nothing else needs changing. `DeviceLiveData.attrs` is open-ended, so no model change.
- New read-only appliance card under `lib/ui/screens/device_detail/`, modelled on `smoke_alarm_card.dart`: operation state, program, remaining time / progress, door, and a clear "enable Remote Start on the appliance" hint when `remoteStartAllowed` is false.
- **No new `HomeCategory` yet.** Most appliances report no power, so `HomeCategory.energy.matches` won't claim them and they'll live in the home-screen room grid plus the Home Connect management screen. Filling the Energy grid with dishwashers that contribute nothing to the energy scene would be worse than absence. If wanted later: adding a 4th value squeezes `category_bar.dart`'s fixed `Row(Expanded)` (~74 px pills at 360 dp → "Applia…"); switch it to a 2×2 `Wrap`, ~6 lines. Routing needs no change (`router.dart:37-43` resolves any enum name).
- **Entry point:** Settings → CONTROLLER → "Home Connect", one `_navTile` after "Remote access" (`settings_screen.dart:44-49`), subtitle carrying live `HomeConnectStatus`. This *satisfies* rather than violates the "phone has nothing to configure" decree at `:18-20` — the token, stream and devices are all controller-scoped, so it belongs next to Matter/Thread/Remote access. Discoverability is a Phase 3 follow-up: convert the home FAB (`home_screen.dart:104-112`) into a three-row add-chooser (Matter code / Home Connect / Modbus meter), reusing the sheet shape from `modbus_devices_screen.dart:200-220` — which also un-buries Modbus from inside the Energy card.

## Phase 2 — control

- `homeconnect/flux_hc_backend.c` registers `{ .kind = FLUX_SYNTH_KIND_CLOUD, … }` on the Phase 0.4 bus. `invoke()` validates, enqueues onto a length-8 queue on `hc_ctl`, and returns `ESP_OK` meaning **accepted, not done** — the outcome arrives as an attribute event. That is not a compromise: `flux_send_device_command_args()` already only means "scheduled onto the CHIP task". The CoAP task must never block on a cloud PUT.
- Matter-verb mapping (cluster/command IDs verified against the vendored 1.5 Application Cluster spec): OnOff `0x0006` on/off → `PUT /settings/BSH.Common.Setting.PowerState`; OperationalState `0x0060` Start `0x02` → `PUT /programs/active`, Stop `0x01` → `DELETE /programs/active`, Pause `0x00` / Resume `0x03` → `PUT /commands/BSH.Common.Command.{Pause,Resume}Program` *(verify — appliance-specific)*; Mode cluster ChangeToMode → `PUT /programs/selected`.
- Plus `POST /homeconnect/command` ← `HomeConnectCommand{node_id, action, start_in_seconds, program_key}` for what Matter cannot express (`StartInRelative`, program options, selected-vs-active). A manufacturer-specific cluster was rejected: it needs a vendor ID we don't own and the app would need bespoke encoders anyway — all the cost of an explicit endpoint with none of its clarity.
- **Safety gates enforced locally, before any request** (so a guaranteed 403 never burns quota): refuse Start unless `remoteStartAllowed`; refuse when disconnected or door open; refuse Start while already Running; one in-flight command per appliance so a double-tap can't produce two PUTs; return quota refusals to the app.
- App: wire the appliance card's actions through `DeviceProvider` following the optimistic-merge-then-rollback shape of `toggle` (`device_provider.dart:906`), keeping `retryOnConnError: false` (commands aren't idempotent).

## Phase 3 — price-aware deferral

New `firmware/main/flexload/`: `flux_flexload.c`, `flux_flex_plan.c` (**pure**, host-tested), `flux_coap_flex.c`. Dependencies point outward only: `flexload → prices` (**the first caller of `flux_prices_at()`**), `flexload → devices` (`defer_start`), `flexload → flux_state.h` (`flux_energy_role_of`). It never speaks HTTP and never mentions Home Connect.

**User-visible contract:** *"Run before 07:00, in the cheapest 2 h window. The hub never starts an appliance itself — it only delays a run you already started."*

- Policy per node: mode, `deadline_minute`, `max_delay_s` (default 12 h), `duration_s` (0 = ask the appliance via `EstimatedTotalProgramTime`), `require_user_start` (default true). NVS ns `flux_flex`. Endpoints `GET/POST /flex/policies`, `GET /flex/plan` (exposes chosen start, delay, expected saving and a `reason` string for the UI).
- Algorithm: slide an `n = ceil(duration/resolution)` window over `[now, deadline − duration]`, minimise summed price, ties → **earliest**. Require ≥2 intervals of forward coverage beyond the window. Task: 4 KiB **internal** stack, 60 s tick, no network, no NVS on the tick.
- Trigger: `hc_sse` reports `operationalState == 0x80` (DelayedStart), or an `HC_START` on a node with a policy → `flux_device_cmd_defer_start()`. HC implements it as `StartInRelative` — as an option on `PUT /programs/active` at start, then via `PUT /programs/active/options/…` while in DelayedStart. The Matter backend returns `NOT_SUPPORTED`.
- Only nodes whose `flux_energy_role_of()` is LOAD or UNKNOWN are considered.
- **Failure behaviour, chosen:** no/stale price curve → **start now** (`reason="no price data"`) — a price-aware scheduler must degrade to "behaves exactly like today", never to "the dishwasher never runs". Deadline too close → start now. Optimum > `max_delay_s` → clamp. Appliance offline → hold the plan, retry on `CONNECTED`, abandon past `deadline − duration`. `remoteStartAllowed == false` → **never defer** (deferring commits us to a remote start we're not permitted to make). **User stopped the program → plan cancelled and not re-armed**, latched in NVS until a new user-initiated start. Re-evaluate at most every 15 min and only ever *increase* the delay (each change is a cloud PUT = quota).
- **Known gap:** `platform/flux_time.c` is UTC-only (`gmtime_r`, no `setenv("TZ")`/`tzset()`), so `deadline_minute` can't be resolved as local time today. `PricingConfig.fetch_hour_local` already promises local-hour scheduling and is likewise unimplemented — fix both together with a POSIX TZ string and `localtime_r`.

## Proto workflow

New messages: `HomeConnectClient`, `HomeConnectConfig`, `HomeConnectAuth`, `HomeConnectAuthorizeUrl`, `HomeConnectStatus`, `HomeConnectAppliance(+List)`, `HomeConnectProgram(+List)`, `HomeConnectCommand`, `FlexLoadPolicy(+List)`, `FlexLoadPlan(+List)`; enums `HomeConnectState`, `HomeConnectType`, `HcAction`, `FlexLoadMode`. **Every** string/bytes/repeated field needs a `max_size`/`max_count` in `flux.options` (no heap, no callbacks). Keep the program list a **separate** message keyed per appliance — nested, the appliance list would exceed 10 KB and force block2.

The shared proto is a submodule checked out as `flux-controller/proto` and `flux-app/flux-interface` (upstream `~/workspace/flux/flux-proto`). **These checkouts are currently diverged — never blind-copy between them; edit each deliberately.** Then regenerate: `cd proto && make c` (nanopb), `make dart` (needs `~/.pub-cache/bin` on PATH), plus `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/flux_pb2.py` and `tests/integration/flux_pb2.py`.

## Verification

1. **Verify before writing Phase 1 auth code:** does Home Connect support RFC 8628 Device Flow? If yes, the *entire* app-side OAuth stack disappears — no `flutter_web_auth_2`, no manifest/plist changes, no redirect registration — and the controller runs the grant itself while the app just shows a code and URL. That is strictly better; the contract above is shaped so `GET /homeconnect/device-code` is purely additive.
2. **Simulator first, always.** Point `base_url` at the developer simulator until the backoff machine is proven, *including* the crash-loop case (cut power during BACKOFF, confirm `blocked_until` survives). Live rate-limit blocks last up to 24 h and are effectively unrecoverable.
3. Host tests (ADR-0010): `firmware/test/host/test_hc_sse_parse.c` and `test_hc_map.c` — the framer and the mapper are where a silent bug hides. Plus `test_flex_plan.c` for the window search.
4. `flux-ctl hc {client,auth,config,status,discover,ls,rm}` and `flux-ctl flex {policies,plan}`, modelled on the `modbus` group (`cli.py:1370-1500`), so every phase is testable without the app.
5. `tests/integration/test_homeconnect.py`, gated on a `--hc-refresh-token`/`--hc-simulator` option in the existing `conftest.py` style. Assert: config round-trip **redacts** secrets; `/devices` lists the appliance with the right `device_type`; `/devices/attrs` carries the expected keys; `enabled=false` produces zero outbound traffic.
6. End-to-end on hardware: flash (`cd firmware && source esp-env.sh && idf.py build && idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash` — stop `serial_logger.py` first, it holds the port), link the account, confirm the appliance appears in the app, toggle power, then set a deferral policy and confirm the chosen window matches `flux-ctl prices` by hand.
7. App: `flutter analyze` clean (0 errors/warnings) and `flutter test` green; `flutter build apk` **before** install (a plain install ships a stale cached APK).

## Positioning / copy

The app currently claims flux runs no cloud (`remote_access_screen.dart:9,220`; pubspec "Local, private, independent"). That claim has to become precise rather than lawyered: flux itself still runs no cloud and holds no account of yours, **and** Home Connect is Bosch's cloud, opt-in, using *your* developer client, with appliance state and commands travelling between your controller and Bosch. The Home Connect screen should say plainly what leaves the house, and note that the Bosch login is entered on Bosch's own page so flux never sees it (which is exactly why an embedded webview is rejected).

## Risks

1. **`esp_http_client` for a never-ending SSE stream is the biggest assumption** — the client is request/response shaped. Unverified: `esp_http_client_read()`'s return on socket timeout with an open chunked body, and how to read `Retry-After` (needs an `HTTP_EVENT_ON_HEADER` handler). The last-byte-timestamp watchdog makes us robust to the first. **Budget the fallback:** `esp_tls` + hand-rolled minimal HTTP/1.1, ~200 lines — precedent exists (ADR-0005 hand-rolled the MeshCoP DTLS client).
2. **`CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS=16`** is shared by CoAP, mDNS, Matter, the rendezvous poller and up to 8 Modbus pollers; HC pins one permanently and two during a REST call. Raise it to 20 in `sdkconfig.defaults` or refuse to enable HC above 6 Modbus devices. This is the most likely "works on the bench, dies in the field" failure.
3. **NVS is 24 KiB and not actually encrypted** (`partitions.csv` marks it encrypted for future flash encryption, but `CONFIG_NVS_ENCRYPTION` is unset) — the refresh token sits in plaintext flash on a dev unit. Measure headroom with `nvs_get_stats()` before shipping; if tight, the honest fix is a partition change, which **cannot** be delivered by OTA.
4. **The PSRAM/NVS abort** is mitigated structurally, but one carelessly added `nvs_set_*` on `hc_ctl` reintroduces a hard crash. Put the invariant in `flux_homeconnect.h` *and* `docs/threading.md`, not just a commit message.
5. `FLUX_DEVICES_MAX` and `ATTR_CACHE_MAX_NODES` (both 32) are now shared across Matter + Modbus + Home Connect.
6. **To verify against the live API/simulator:** Pause/Resume command support (appliance-specific); whether `haId` arrives in the SSE `id:` field or the JSON body (handle both); `items[].value` type mixing (bool/number/string per key); which Mode cluster the Dryer and WasherDryer types mandate; and that **`StartInRelative` availability is per program and per appliance** and cannot be sent with a program *selection* — read `GET /programs/available/{key}` at discovery and surface `supports_delayed_start`, or Phase 3 silently does nothing for some appliances.
7. BYO credentials will lose some users at the first screen. Mitigated by the walkthrough copy and by keeping the feature clearly optional.

The plan is written. Summary of what it commits to and the notable findings:

**Shape:** Phase 0 prerequisites (all zero-behaviour-change) → Phase 1 account linking + read-only monitoring → Phase 2 control → Phase 3 price-aware deferral. The controller owns the runtime; the app only bootstraps OAuth and renders.

**Three things worth knowing before you read it:**

1. **flux has no command path for non-Matter devices at all.** `flux_send_device_command_args()` rejects synthetic node IDs with a one-line guard, and there's no dispatch layer — Modbus devices are read-only today. Control therefore requires building a neutral command bus first, which the plan does as a pure refactor in Phase 0 so the Home Connect diff stays reviewable.

2. **A real bug found on the way:** `device_type.dart:147` maps `0x0073` → `airQualitySensor`, but `0x0073` is Matter's Laundry Washer — Air Quality Sensor is `0x002C`, already correct on the line below. Every Home Connect washer would render as an air-quality sensor. Same conflation in `cluster_inspector_screen.dart` and `SUPPORTED_DEVICES.md`.

3. **One verification could delete a whole workstream:** if Home Connect supports RFC 8628 Device Flow, the entire app-side OAuth stack goes away — no `flutter_web_auth_2`, no Android intent-filter, no iOS `CFBundleURLTypes`, no redirect registration. The docs site is JS-heavy and searches didn't confirm it either way. The contract is shaped so adding `GET /homeconnect/device-code` later is purely additive, but this is the first thing to check.

**Biggest technical risk:** `esp_http_client` is request/response shaped and we need a never-ending SSE stream on it. Mitigated with a self-tracked last-byte watchdog, with a budgeted ~200-line `esp_tls` fallback (precedent: ADR-0005 hand-rolled the MeshCoP DTLS client). Second risk is prosaic but likelier to bite in the field: `LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS=16` shared with 8 Modbus pollers, CoAP, mDNS, Matter and the rendezvous poller.

Phase 3 is also the first caller `flux_prices_at()` has ever had, which is the point — it turns the pricing work into something that acts.

# Home Connect (Bosch/Siemens) integration into flux

## Context

flux is a local-first smart-home controller (ESP32-P4 + esp-matter + OTBR) with a Flutter app, recently pivoted toward **energy management**: it fetches EPEX day-ahead prices and logs per-device energy. `docs/epex-day-ahead-pricing.md:118-122` describes a "phase 2 — act on price" that is unimplemented; `flux_prices_at()` (`firmware/main/prices/flux_prices.c:354`) has **zero callers** today.

Home Connect appliances (dishwasher, washer, dryer) are the ideal deferrable load: the API exposes `BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative`, so a run the user has already asked for can be slid into the cheapest price window. That makes this integration both a device-coverage win and the first real consumer of the pricing subsystem.

The appliances in question are not Matter-capable (BSH's Matter rollout covers only newer fridges natively, plus some models via the Smart Kitchen Dock bridge; most existing appliances cannot be upgraded), so the cloud API is the only way to reach them.

**Intended outcome:** appliances appear as ordinary flux devices with live state, are controllable from the app, and can have their start deferred into the cheapest hours — with the token, the event stream and all control living on the controller so it works when the phone is away.

## Decisions (locked)

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Controller owns the runtime.** It holds the refresh token, keeps one Server-Sent-Events stream open, and executes all commands. The app only bootstraps auth and renders. | Must work with the phone away; price scheduling belongs next to the price data; appliances then flow through the existing `/devices` + `/events` contract with almost no app plumbing. |
| D2 | **Bring-your-own Home Connect developer client.** The user registers a free client at `developer.home-connect.com` and enters id/secret once; both are stored **only** on the controller. | Whoever refreshes needs the `client_secret`, and that is the controller — forever, unattended. Rate-limit blocks are per-client and last minutes to 24 h, so a shipped shared `client_id` would let one bad actor break every household. Nothing extractable ships in the APK. Mirrors the existing BYO-TURN pattern (`lib/ui/screens/settings/remote_access_screen.dart:9,220`). |
| D3 | **Phone does the `authorize` step only; the controller exchanges the code.** The app fetches the authorize URL *from* the controller, so the app ships no credentials at all — not even the `client_id`. | The authorization code is single-use, short-lived and redirect-bound: safe to pass over the existing DTLS/CoAP channel. Having the phone do the exchange would put the secret in *two* places for zero gain. |
| D4 | **Synthetic node IDs get a kind nibble.** Modbus stays `0x01…`; Home Connect becomes `0x02…`. | ADR-0009 makes "bit 63 clear" a cross-repo contract. Today the app's test is a bare threshold (`nodeId >= 0x0100000000000000`), so an HC node would silently render as a Modbus device. |
| D5 | **New neutral command bus** `devices/flux_device_cmd.c`; Matter and Home Connect each register a backend. | A dispatch layer does not exist — `flux_send_device_command_args()` (`firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp:985`) rejects synthetic nodes at `:995`. Branching inside `flux_controller.cpp` would create a `matter → cloud` dependency, the inversion ADR-0008 exists to prevent. |
| D6 | **Matter clusters where a faithful mapping exists; an explicit HC endpoint where it doesn't.** | OnOff/OperationalState/Mode clusters were written for exactly these appliances, so a future *real* Matter dishwasher works through the same path. But `StartInRelative`, per-program option sets and selected-vs-active have no Matter representation; faking a cluster ID would collide later and be undiscoverable. |
| D7 | **Scheduling lives in a separate `flexload/` subsystem**, not in `homeconnect/`. | The same policy must later drive the battery and wallbox. |
| D8 | **The controller never starts an appliance on its own initiative — it only delays a run the user already started.** | This is the whole safety model, and it is also the user-visible contract. |

## Phase 1 — account linking + monitoring

### 1a. Auth bootstrap

App flow: Settings → Home Connect → paste client id/secret (with the 5-step `developer.home-connect.com` walkthrough) → **Connect account** → `GET /homeconnect/authorize-url` → `flutter_web_auth_2` opens the system browser (`preferEphemeral: true`) → Bosch's own login page → redirect `fluxhome://homeconnect/callback?code=…&state=…` → app POSTs the code to the controller → controller exchanges it and persists only the refresh token.

- **Only one new app dependency: `flutter_web_auth_2` ^4.x.** It wraps Android Custom Tabs + iOS `ASWebAuthenticationSession`. Reject `webview_flutter` as a *design constraint*: an embedded webview lets the flux process observe the user's Bosch password, contradicting the disclosure copy below.
- Platform config: Android `MainActivity` gains a `VIEW`+`BROWSABLE` intent-filter with `<data android:scheme="fluxhome"/>`; iOS `Info.plist` gains `CFBundleURLTypes`. Neither exists today.
- **Secret and code writes are LAN-only** (ADR-0012). Refuse them over the remote/ICE path, and have the app refuse to *start* the flow when `hub.connectionKind == ConnectionKind.remote`, saying why.
- `GET /homeconnect/client` and `/config` **redact** secrets to `has_client_secret` / `has_refresh_token` booleans. Explicitly do *not* copy `PricingConfig.api_token`, which round-trips in cleartext through `GET /prices/config`.
- Two-level teardown: `DELETE /homeconnect/auth` unlinks the account but keeps client credentials (so re-linking after a lapsed refresh token doesn't re-ask for the secret); `DELETE /homeconnect/client` is the full forget.
- Also ship a collapsed **Advanced → paste a token** affordance (~20 lines) — the only way to drive the developer simulator from `curl`.

### 1b. Firmware subsystem

New `firmware/main/homeconnect/` (add to both CMake lists):

| File | Responsibility |

| `flux_hc_auth.c` | The only module touching the token store. `POST {base}/security/oauth/token`, `grant_type=refresh_token` / `authorization_code`. |
| `flux_hc_rest.c` | Bearer/Accept-aware GET/PUT/DELETE; bounded body; **quota gate ahead of every request**; 429/`Retry-After` handling. |
| `flux_hc_sse.c` | `hc_sse` task: long-lived stream, read loop. |
| `flux_hc_sse_parse.c` | **Pure** incremental SSE framer — host-testable (ADR-0010). |
| `flux_hc_map.c` | **Pure** HC key/value → flux attr key/type/value. The analogue of `flux_modbus_profile.c`. Host-testable. |
| `flux_hc_registry.c` | `haId ↔ node_id` registry, NVS ns `flux_hc`, mirroring the Modbus-registry idiom in `flux_state.c` (own mutex created at boot, monotonic id counter, compaction on remove). Deliberately **not** in `flux_state.c` — that file is one line under the split canary. |
