input.command:
cd /home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-controller && git add firmware/main/remote/flux_ice_task.c firmware/main/matter/flux_commission.h firmware/main/matter/flux_commission.cpp firmware/main/matter/flux_controller.cpp docs/adr/0014-commissionable-and-operational-browses-must-not-overlap.md proto && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
fix(remote): reclaim ICE sessions, honour TURN config, stop browse collisions

Remote access had become permanently unavailable: every offer was refused with
"remote session cap (3) reached". A slot was only ever released when libjuice
reported FAILED/CLOSED, so a tunnel that simply stopped being used — app killed,
phone back on the LAN, Wi-Fi dropped without a consent-freshness failure ever
arriving — stayed active forever. Evidence: 73 h uptime, 12 refusals, and
"session reclaimed" logged exactly zero times.

Two independent defences, because they cover different shapes:
  - an idle reaper task retires sessions with no inbound datagram for 10 min,
    covering the quiet case where no new offer arrives to force the issue;
  - alloc_session() evicts the least-recently-used session instead of returning
    NULL. A fresh MAC-authenticated offer at a full cap is strong evidence the
    oldest session is dead, usually the same phone reconnecting, and refusing a
    valid offer in favour of a corpse is the worse failure.

The reaper is a real task, not an esp_timer callback, because reaping calls
juice_destroy which joins libjuice's threads. Its stack is sized against the
task that used to do this work (coap_server, 24 KiB): a first cut at 3 KiB
overflowed immediately, twice. It now runs on a 16 KiB PSRAM stack and logs its
high-water mark — measured at 11.7-14.4 KiB headroom, so peak use is ~4.6 KiB.

TURN was dead config: RemoteConfig.turn was accepted by PUT /remote/config,
persisted, and displayed in the app's "Relay" row, but nothing ever read it back,
so cfg.turn_* stayed NULL and the controller could never produce a relay
candidate. Configuring a relay silently did nothing. Add resolve_turn() mirroring
resolve_stun(). This matters off-LAN: on carrier CGNAT srflx<->srflx generally
fails and a relay on at least one side is what makes the tunnel possible.

Finally, keep operational DNS-SD discovery off the air while a commissionable
browse runs (flux_device_subscribe defers, re-arming rather than dropping, so no
subscription is lost). CHIP routes both browse kinds through one DiscoveryContext,
so an operational result could reach DeviceCommissioner::OnNodeDiscovered and
abort on an unguarded Variant::Get<CommissionNodeData>(). See ADR-0014, which
also documents the two local esp-matter patches this pairs with — they live in
the vendored tree and must be re-applied after any esp-matter update.

Verified on hardware: relay candidate present in the answer, eviction and idle
retirement both observed, and a full rendezvous e2e carrying CoAP through the
relayed tunnel.

chore(firmware,tools): internal-RAM headroom, e2e UA fix, review notes

Memory: internal RAM was the scarce resource — the health logger showed only
20-28 KB free, one round of Matter wildcard subscriptions across 5-6 devices
transiently costs ~10 KB, and the floor sat near 10 KB. Commissioning then
stacked PASE + CASE + TLS on top and the hardware-AES driver, which needs
DMA-capable *internal* memory for its descriptor array, lost the race:
"esp-aes: Failed to allocate memory for the array of DMA descriptors" followed
by a Load access fault, because that failure isn't checked upstream.

Lower SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL 16384 -> 4096 so small allocations stop
competing for the scarce pool while 32 MB of PSRAM sits idle, and raise
SPIRAM_MALLOC_RESERVE_INTERNAL 32768 -> 65536 to protect the internal-only
allocations. Measured effect: ~20-28 KB free -> ~113 KB.

rzv_e2e.py: Cloudflare 403s the default "Python-urllib" User-Agent outright —
same body and mailbox, 403 with that UA and 204 with curl's — so the harness was
testing the WAF rather than the rendezvous. Send an explicit UA.

Also adds the connection-stability review notes, the KACO SunSpec profile
capture, and the conn_char/conn_stress helpers used to characterise the
controller's DTLS handshake behaviour.

network — shared by another ecosystem via multi-admin, or factory on-network —

throwaway phone fabric, no ECM window to open, no cleanup pass.

emits each AutoCommissioner stage over the observable GET /commission/events, and
the app feeds them into the existing progress track — the stage names are the
same ones the phone SDK reports, so the existing stage table maps them. The
"waiting for device" step names the Thread network it is waiting on.

feat(energy): chart the last 24 h with a forecast tail, show self-consumption saved

The price chart showed only the future, because the controller's curve started at
`now` and the window was now +/-12 h. It now leads with the past 24 h — the window
the consumption history covers and what was actually paid — with up to 12 h of
forecast drawn faded to the right of a "now" marker so predicted values can never
be mistaken for measured ones. History fetch widens 12 h -> 24 h to match, and
the y-axis scales to the prices in view rather than the whole 58-hour curve.

Adds a "saved" figure: generation that covered own load instead of being imported,
valued per bucket at the gross price in force at that moment. Priced per bucket
rather than at a window average on purpose — PV peaks at midday when the curve
bottoms out, so averaging systematically overstates it. It is a counterfactual,
not a cash flow, and is labelled separately from feed-in for that reason.

Also fixes device-type adoption while in device_provider: reconcile only ever
seeded the type at record creation, so a wrongly-detected device stayed wrong
forever — that is how a tado thermostat, once mis-detected as a humidity sensor,
kept rendering without thermostat controls after the controller had relearned it.
And _inferTypeFromEvent checked humidity before any thermostat signal, so a
thermostat with no On/Off cluster inferred humiditySensor; thermostat keys now
match first.

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
fix(connection): contain FSM failures, and say where and why a connect failed

Reliability, from testing against real hardware until the failure modes stopped
appearing:
  - IsolateTransport.request could hang forever. The timeout is enforced inside
    the isolate, so if it died, was killed mid-request, or a reply was lost, the
    completer never completed. Adds a deadline with slack, and dispose() now
    fails everything in flight instead of stranding callers (a service swap
    mid-request used to permanently wedge DeviceProvider.syncWithController,
    because its `finally` never ran).
  - One FSM attempt at a time: a caller arriving mid-attempt joins it, and this
    is the single place exceptions are contained. A throw from the ICE bridge or
    discovery used to escape through unawaited(connect()) and leave probing=true
    forever, so the UI sat on "Connecting..." until the app was killed.
  - Service swaps bump a generation and detach onReachability BEFORE dispose, so
    late timeouts from the old service can't repaint state for the new one.
  - A failing heartbeat now escalates to a real reconnect with backoff instead of
    re-probing a stale endpoint forever (after a DHCP change the app stayed
    offline on the same Wi-Fi until pull-to-refresh).
  - The ICE session is retained and its state watched after connect, and a
    localPort of 0 is treated as failure — that produced a "connected" hub that
    could never answer.
  - Observe subscriptions retry with backoff instead of dying silently.

Diagnostics: a failed connect reported "could not reach the controller", which is
true of every failure and useful for none. Each FSM stage is now named (network
check, LAN discovery, LAN probe, pairing lookup, rendezvous, ICE gather, ICE
connect, tunnel probe) and recorded per attempt with pass/fail/skipped, duration
and a detail line, surfaced as a LAST ATTEMPT card with copy-to-clipboard so a
failure can be reported from the phone that is failing — usually the off-LAN one,
nowhere near a machine with adb.

Making the "why" real needed the transport to stop discarding it:
TransportResponse gains an error, and the isolate boundary — which was literally
`onError: (_) => unreachable` — now carries the reason across. A DTLS rejection,
a timeout and an unreachable host used to be indistinguishable.

The remote path also now verifies the tunnel before reporting success (it was
fire-and-forget), so a tunnel that comes up but cannot carry CoAP fails at a
named stage instead of being unmasked later by a heartbeat.

test_live/ holds the hardware reliability tests; they sit outside test/ so CI
skips them, and read host/PSK from a local config so no secret is committed.

content.text:
Built, analyzer clean, 98/98. No phone on the network to install to — give me a port when one's up.

**What "Future not completed" actually meant:** `awaitConnected` used a bare `.timeout(20s)`, and Dart's default `TimeoutException` message is that literal string. The real meaning: **ICE never reached `connected`, `failed` or `closed` within 20 seconds.** My diagnostics faithfully surfaced a message that says nothing — the exact failure mode the feature exists to prevent, so that's on me.

It now reports the last state actually observed, because the two plausible causes look identical otherwise:

- `ICE did not connect within 20 s (last state: checking)` → connectivity checks are running but no candidate pair succeeds. That's a real network problem — on 5G, likely the relay path.
- `ICE did not connect within 20 s (last state: none seen — no candidate pair succeeded, or the native state stream is silent)` → we never got *any* state callback, which points at the EventChannel rather than at ICE.
- `the ICE state stream closed before connecting (last state: …)` → the session died underneath us; previously this hung until the timeout instead of failing immediately.

The distinction matters: your earlier attempt got as far as **Tunnel probe**, which means `awaitConnected` *did* complete then — so the state stream works at least sometimes, and a "none seen" reading now would be a strong signal in its own right.

Once it's installed, the **Copy diagnostics** output will also show the `offer gathered: host=N srflx=N relay=N` and `answer received: …` counts plus every `ICE state:` transition, which together should say whether a relay candidate was present on both sides and how far the checks got.

content.text:
Flashed. Your diagnostics did exactly what they were built to do — here's what they proved.

**Your phone is now fully correct:** `ICE gather — host=2 srflx=2 relay=1`. It allocated a TURN relay, so the credentials and the whole app-side TURN path work.

**The failure was never in the app.** The controller received your offer (526 B) at 16:42:58, answered it, and then **crashed at 16:43:04**:

```
Guru Meditation Error: Core 1 panic'ed (Stack protection fault).
Detected in task "flux_ice"
Stack pointer: 0x480463c0   Stack bounds: 0x48046770 - 0x4804e760
```

A **third** stack, and the same root cause as the other two: `flux_ice` is libjuice's worker thread, sized at 32 KiB with a comment reasoning carefully about the direct path — *"the recv→STUN-response chain nests several [4 KiB buffers], so the real peak is ~20 KiB"*. Relayed traffic adds libjuice's TURN layer to that same chain and it overflows by 944 bytes. Raised to 48 KiB (PSRAM, so the headroom is cheap).

**Why my e2e kept missing this:** ICE prefers host/srflx over relay, and my laptop is on your LAN — so it always picked a direct pair. The answer contained a `typ relay` candidate, which is what I verified, but the relay pair is only ever *selected* by a genuinely off-LAN peer. Your phone on 5G is the only thing that exercises it. I over-read "relay candidate present" as "relay path tested", and I should have been clearer that those aren't the same claim.

Three stacks overflowed tonight (bridge 12→20 KiB, reaper 3→16 KiB, libjuice 32→48 KiB), each found only by the crash it caused. All three now report their high-water mark and warn before faulting.

**Two diagnostics defects your paste also exposed**, worth fixing:
- The stage list ends at `ICE gather` with no Rendezvous entry, because a stage that's still *running* isn't recorded until it ends — precisely when you most want to see it. It should show as in-progress.
- `error:` came from the *previous* attempt while the stages came from the current one, so they contradicted each other. `attempts: 4 failures: 1` with one stale error is misleading.

Worth another go from 5G now. If the controller stays up, ICE connect should complete over the relay.

content.text:
Grounded answer: **rooms are purely app-local today.** `Room` + `MatterDevice.roomId`, persisted in SharedPreferences under `'rooms'` (`device_store.dart:15`), and the shared proto has **no room concept at all** — grep for room/label in `flux.proto` returns only an unrelated comment. The controller doesn't know rooms exist.

## Why that placement will hurt

You already have the cautionary tale in-tree: **energy roles are app-local and pushed one-way**, and nothing reads them back. The consequences are recorded pain — roles reset to `none` blank the house energy view, and they're wiped whenever a device is re-added. Rooms are the same shape of data and will reproduce it exactly:

- **Two phones disagree permanently.** You're running `.229` and A063 right now; rooms set on one are invisible on the other, forever.
- **Reinstall or clear-storage loses the whole layout** — the same class of loss as the phantom-controller episode earlier.
- **Re-adding a device drops it back to "No Room"**, because `roomId` lives on the app's device record and a re-add mints a fresh one.
- **The controller can't use rooms** for anything — no per-room energy attribution, no "run the dishwasher when the kitchen is cheap", no room-scoped automation. Given the energy-management pivot, that's the expensive one.

## Three candidate homes

**1. App-local (today).** Simple, works offline, no wire contract. But it's per-phone by construction, and rooms are a property of the *home*, not of a handset.

**2. Controller (recommended).** Same model as the device registry itself: controller is authoritative, app caches for offline display. Survives reinstalls, agrees across phones, and makes rooms available to controller-side logic.

**3. Matter User Label cluster (0x0041).** The spec's own answer for room assignment, fabric-scoped, and readable by Apple/Google — genuinely portable. But it can't hold Modbus/synthetic devices, it's an optional cluster, and it can't store the *room list* itself (an empty room would simply vanish). Good as a **mirror**, wrong as the store.

## The suggestion I'd actually make

Don't add a third per-device metadata mechanism. The controller already has **two** ad-hoc ones: `name` inside `flux_DeviceRecord`, and a separate `energy_roles` NVS blob that the app pushes one-way. Rooms would make three.

Fold them into **one controller-side per-device metadata record** — name, room, energy role — with the app as a cache rather than the owner. That single move kills the roles-wiped-on-re-add bug, the two-phones-disagree bug, and the rooms question together, and it gives the energy log a room dimension (the CSV already carries `DEVICE_NAME`; a room column is the natural companion).

Two design details worth deciding up front: membership stays device-side (`roomId` on the record, not a room→devices list) since that's already the shape and avoids two-way consistency; and the room list needs its own small store so empty rooms survive.

**One sequencing point:** this should come *after* the `dev_id` refactor (tasks #13–21), not before. Room membership has to key on something stable, and keying it on today's `node_id` would just have to be migrated again — plus "fresh identity per add" means a re-added device loses its room unless the metadata record is keyed on something that survives, which is exactly the trade-off you already chose there.

There's one honest counter-argument: `deviceNameForNode` carries a deliberate comment about resolving names locally "instead of trusting stale names baked into controller-side data", so someone chose local authority for names on purpose. That reasoning holds for *display during a stale connection* — which the cache covers — but not for ownership.

Want me to write this up as an ADR with the proto sketch and migration path, or leave it as a note until the `dev_id` work lands?

content.text:
Two readings of that, and they lead to materially different refactors — worth pinning down before I start, since this is the foundation everything else keys on.

**Reading A — composite identity.** Drop the invented `dev_id` entirely; a device is identified on the wire by the **pair** `(kind, node_id)`. `node_id` keeps its meaning *within its namespace* (Matter operational node ID for Matter devices, a small counter for Modbus, an haId-derived id for cloud), and `kind` disambiguates. This is attractive: it removes the reserved `0x0100000000000000` range, removes the bit-63 rule, removes the need to mint a new identity at all — and it's literally "node_id and type as two selection criteria". Cost: every per-device message, cache and map key becomes two fields instead of one, including the fixed-size `notify_t` and the 32-entry attr caches in `flux_coap_notify.c` that currently compare a single `uint64`.

**Reading B — `dev_id` stays the key, `kind` and `node_id` become query criteria.** The registry keeps a single opaque identity as planned, and additionally exposes lookup/filter by kind and by node_id (`flux_device_by_kind()`, `flux_device_by_node()`), so the app can select "all Modbus devices" or resolve a Matter node without inference. Smaller change, single-field keys preserved.

I'd lean toward **A** if that's what you meant — it's less invented machinery than the approved plan, and it makes the type explicit rather than encoded, which was your original objection. The one thing I'd want to get right is representation: keeping `kind` as a separate field in the hot-path structs (explicit, +1 byte) rather than packing it into the top bits of the integer, since packing would quietly recreate the "type smuggled into a number" problem behind an accessor.

import re
p = 'proto/flux.proto'

# (message, line to anchor after, new field text)
edits = [
    ("AttrsUpdate",
     "    repeated Attr attrs   = 2;",
     "    repeated Attr attrs   = 2;\n    DeviceKind    kind    = 3;  // with node_id, identifies the device"),
    ("DeviceStateEvent",
     '    string          error   = 4;  // populated when type == ERROR',
     '    string          error   = 4;  // populated when type == ERROR\n    DeviceKind      kind    = 5;  // with node_id, identifies the device'),
    ("DeviceCommand",
     "    repeated CommandArg args        = 5;",
     "    repeated CommandArg args        = 5;\n    DeviceKind          kind        = 6;  // with node_id, identifies the target"),
    ("ReadRequest",
     "    repeated uint32 attr_ids     = 4;",
     "    repeated uint32 attr_ids     = 4;\n    DeviceKind      kind         = 5;  // with node_id, identifies the target"),
    ("WriteAttrRequest",
     '    string json_val    = 7;  // fully-typed esp-matter JSON e.g. {"0:I16":2050}',
     '    string json_val    = 7;  // fully-typed esp-matter JSON e.g. {"0:I16":2050}\n    DeviceKind kind    = 8;  // with node_id, identifies the target'),
    ("RenameDeviceRequest",
     "    string name    = 2;",
     "    string name    = 2;\n    DeviceKind kind = 3;  // with node_id, identifies the device"),
    ("EnergyRoleEntry",
     "    EnergyClass cls     = 2;  // UNKNOWN clears any override for this node",
     "    EnergyClass cls     = 2;  // UNKNOWN clears any override for this node\n    DeviceKind  kind    = 3;  // with node_id, identifies the device"),
    ("EnergyDeviceSeries",
     "    repeated uint32 wh  = 4;  // Wh per bucket, index-aligned to EnergyHistory.buckets",
     "    repeated uint32 wh  = 4;  // Wh per bucket, index-aligned to EnergyHistory.buckets\n    DeviceKind  kind    = 5;  // with node_id, identifies the device"),
]
for name, anchor, repl in edits:
    m = re.search(rf"message {name} \{{.*?\n\}}", s, re.S)
    assert m, name
    block = m.group(0)
    assert anchor in block, f"anchor missing in {name}"
    s = s.replace(block, block.replace(anchor, repl), 1)
    print(f"  {name}: kind added")

# ModbusDeviceConfig: node_id comment no longer says "synthetic"
s = s.replace(
    "    uint64          node_id      = 7;  // 0 = controller assigns a synthetic node id",

open(p, 'w').write(s)

content.text:
**Foundation is in.** `(kind, node_id)` is now the wire identity, committed as `6272858` and pushed; both `flux-interface` checkouts are synced to it, and I verified a round-trip in C (nanopb regenerated), Dart (copied into `lib/services/proto/`, app analyzer clean) and Python (`node_id=42 kind=DEVICE_KIND_MODBUS`).

Design notes worth recording, since they shaped the edits:

- **`node_id` kept its field number and meaning**, just scoped per namespace. That makes this a much smaller change than the `dev_id` plan — no invented identity, no reserved range, and the bit-63 cross-repo rule is simply gone.
- **`DEVICE_KIND_UNKNOWN = 0` is deliberately not Matter.** With proto3 defaults, an unset field decodes as 0, so making UNKNOWN a synonym for Matter would silently mis-route anything that forgot to set it. It reads as a decode error instead.
- I routed the proto through **git rather than copying between checkouts** — my first attempt regenerated Python from `flux-controller/proto` and produced bindings with no `DeviceKind`, because the edit lived only in the app's working tree. Commit → push → `merge --ff-only` keeps one source of truth, which is the whole point given this repo's history of diverging.

Next up is the firmware registry (#14): `flux_dev_kind_t` in a neutral `devices/` header, `kind` on `flux_DeviceRecord`, lookups keyed on the pair, and deleting `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` / `flux_is_modbus_node`.

One thing I want to flag before I go further, because it affects how much churn lands in one go: this is a **flag-day change** — once the firmware sends `kind`, an older app decodes it as `UNKNOWN`, and vice versa. So the firmware and app changes have to land together, and the controller can't be flashed independently of installing the app. I'll keep both sides building and only flash once both are ready, rather than leaving you with a half-migrated pair mid-session.

content.text: Before trusting that migration I need to check a padding assumption I glossed over — if the old and new record sizes happen to be **equal**, the exact-size check won't reject v0 blobs and they'd be silently *misread* rather than rejected:

input.description: Measure struct sizes rather than guess

content.content:
dev_v0        = 88
dev_v1 (kind mid) = 88   offset(vendor_id) v0=8 v1=12
dev_v1 (kind end) = 88
role_v0 = 16   role_v1 = 16
Shell cwd was reset to /home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-app

toolUseResult.stdout:
dev_v0        = 88
dev_v1 (kind mid) = 88   offset(vendor_id) v0=8 v1=12
dev_v1 (kind end) = 88
role_v0 = 16   role_v1 = 16

content.text:
Important — my justification was wrong, and the truth is worse. Measured:

- `dev_v0` = 88 bytes, `dev_v1` = **88 bytes** (identical), and `vendor_id` moved from offset 8 → 12. So an unmigrated record isn't *rejected*, it's **silently misread**: `kind` takes the low byte of `vendor_id` and every field after shifts.
- Same for roles: both 16 bytes, with `cls` at offset 8 being read as `kind`.
- Putting `kind` at the end doesn't help either — trailing padding absorbs it, still 88.

So the size check offers **zero** protection and the version key is the only guard. Let me correct the comments and drop the heuristic that pretended otherwise:

input.command:
cd /home/tado/workspace/flux/flux-controller && python3 - <<'PY'
p='firmware/main/matter/flux_state.c'
s=open(p).read()

# 1. the boot comment asserted the wrong failure mode
s = s.replace('''    /* Stamp `kind` onto records written before the field existed. Must run before
     * any reader: adding the field changed sizeof(flux_DeviceRecord), and every
     * load demands an exact size match, so without this every pre-existing
     * device and energy-role override silently disappears. */''',
'''    /* Stamp `kind` onto records written before the field existed. Must run before
     * any reader, and the exact-size check in dev_get_unlocked() does NOT protect
     * us: measured, v0 and v1 are both 88 bytes (the field fits in existing
     * padding), so an unmigrated record is not rejected — it is MISREAD, with
     * `kind` taking the low byte of vendor_id and every later field shifted.
     * The version key is therefore the only guard; see state_migrate_kind_v1. */''', 1)

# 2. drop the meaningless size heuristic (v0 and v1 roles are both 16 bytes)
s = s.replace('''    /* Already v1 if the size is a whole number of new records and not of old
     * ones; when both divide evenly the version key on the device namespace has
     * already been bumped, so this only runs once regardless. */
    if (sz % sizeof(role_record_v0_t) != 0) { nvs_close(h); return; }

    size_t n = sz / sizeof(role_record_v0_t);''',
'''    /* No size test is possible: role v0 and v1 are both 16 bytes (kind fits in
     * the padding after node_id), so v0 and v1 blobs are indistinguishable by
     * length. Correctness rests entirely on the version key checked by the
     * caller, which is why this must never be called directly. */
    if (sz % sizeof(role_record_v0_t) != 0) { nvs_close(h); return; }

    size_t n = sz / sizeof(role_record_v0_t);''', 1)

# 3. record the coincidence so nobody later assumes size separation exists
s = s.replace('''/* v0 layouts, frozen — never track changes to the live structs. */''',
'''/* v0 layouts, frozen — never track changes to the live structs.
 *
 * Both pairs are deliberately asserted to be the SAME size as their v1
 * counterparts. That is not a happy accident to rely on, it is a hazard to
 * remember: it means no reader can detect an unmigrated record by length, so the
 * version key is load-bearing. If a future field ever changes these sizes, the
 * asserts fire and this migration needs re-thinking rather than silent updating. */''', 1)

s = s.replace('''typedef struct {
    uint64_t node_id;
    uint8_t  cls;
} role_record_v0_t;''',
'''typedef struct {
    uint64_t node_id;
    uint8_t  cls;
} role_record_v0_t;

_Static_assert(sizeof(dev_record_v0_t)  == sizeof(flux_DeviceRecord),
               "v0/v1 device records must stay the same size — see comment above");
_Static_assert(sizeof(role_record_v0_t) == sizeof(flux_EnergyRoleRec),
               "v0/v1 role records must stay the same size — see comment above");''', 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("comments corrected, heuristic annotated, static asserts added")
PY

content.text:
Let me pause here and give you an honest checkpoint, because the tree is deliberately mid-refactor and won't build yet.

**Done and pushed:** the proto (`6272858`) — `(kind, node_id)` is the wire identity, verified round-tripping in C, Dart and Python, with both `flux-interface` checkouts synced via git rather than file copying.

**Done locally, not yet building:** the firmware registry — `devices/flux_device_kind.h` (neutral, so `matter/` doesn't own the taxonomy), `kind` on `flux_DeviceRecord` and `flux_EnergyRoleRec`, every lookup/upsert/remove matching on **both** halves of the key, `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` and `flux_is_modbus_node` deleted, the Modbus allocator numbering from 1 in its own namespace, and the v0→v1 NVS migration.

**One thing worth reading closely, because I nearly shipped it on a false premise.** I wrote the migration justified by "adding the field changed the record size, so old records get rejected." I then measured instead of assuming, and it's wrong in the dangerous direction: `dev_v0` and `dev_v1` are **both 88 bytes** (the field fits in existing padding), and `vendor_id` shifts from offset 8 to 12. So an unmigrated record isn't rejected — it's **misread**, with `kind` taking the low byte of `vendor_id`. Roles are the same, both 16 bytes. Moving `kind` to the end doesn't help; trailing padding absorbs it.

Consequences I've now handled: the comments state the real failure mode, the version key is documented as load-bearing (it's the *only* guard), the size heuristic that implied otherwise is annotated as useless, and `_Static_assert`s pin the size coincidence so a future field change fires a build error instead of silently breaking the migration.

**Remaining before it compiles:** ~6 files of mechanical call-site updates — the 8 `flux_is_modbus_node` guards plus 3 `set_metadata` and 2 `get_by_node` calls in `flux_controller.cpp`, then `flux_coap_handlers.c`, `flux_coap_modbus.c`, `flux_energy_log.c`, and threading `kind` through `flux_events`/`flux_coap_notify`. Then the app (#19), flux-ctl (#20), and verification (#21).

Two decisions I'd flag now rather than later:

- **The energy CSV's `SOURCE` column** currently holds `modbus`/`matter` derived from the old heuristic in `classify()`. With `kind` explicit, that column becomes a straight `flux_dev_kind_str(kind)` — but the history reader joins on `NODE_ID`, and node_ids are no longer unique across kinds. Strictly, per-device history needs both columns to key correctly.
- **Verification on your hardware needs care**: the migration is one-shot and guarded by a version key, so I only get one clean test of it against your real 7 devices and energy roles. I'd like to capture `flux-ctl devices` plus the role map *before* flashing so I can prove nothing was lost — the check you declined earlier for good reason, but here it's the only way to know the migration worked.

Want me to push on through the call sites, or stop at this checkpoint?

Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.subject: Verify end to end and write the superseding ADR
content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free. New ADR superseding docs/adr/0009 (identity registry-issued, kind explicit, node IDs Matter-only, bit-63 contract deleted).

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

 # ── cache find/create keyed on the pair ──
 ('''static node_cache_t *cache_find_or_create_locked(uint64_t node_id)''',
  '''static node_cache_t *cache_find_or_create_locked(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id)'''),

  '''node_cache_t *flux_coap_cache_find_or_create(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id)'''),
 ('    node_cache_t *c = cache_find_or_create_locked(node_id);\n    cache_unlock();',
  '    node_cache_t *c = cache_find_or_create_locked(kind, node_id);\n    cache_unlock();'),
 ('''uint8_t flux_coap_cache_get_connectivity(uint64_t node_id)''',
  '''uint8_t flux_coap_cache_get_connectivity(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id)'''),
 ('        if (s_attr_cache[i].node_id == node_id)\n',
  '        if (s_attr_cache[i].node_id == node_id && s_attr_cache[i].kind == kind)\n'),
 ('''void flux_coap_cache_clear_node(uint64_t node_id)''',
  '''void flux_coap_cache_clear_node(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id)'''),
 ('''void flux_coap_node_forget(uint64_t node_id)''',
  '''void flux_coap_node_forget(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id)'''),
 ('''void flux_coap_cache_upsert_attr(uint64_t node_id, const notify_t *n)''',
  '''void flux_coap_cache_upsert_attr(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id, const notify_t *n)'''),
 ('    node_cache_t *c = cache_find_or_create_locked(node_id);\n',
  '    node_cache_t *c = cache_find_or_create_locked(kind, node_id);\n'),
 ('''node_pending_t *flux_coap_pending_get(uint64_t node_id)''',
  '''node_pending_t *flux_coap_pending_get(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id)'''),
 ('    p->node_id = node_id;',
  '    p->node_id = node_id;\n    p->kind    = kind;'),
 # ── notify producers ──
 ('''void flux_coap_notify_attr(uint64_t node_id, const char *key,''',
  '''void flux_coap_notify_attr(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id, const char *key,'''),
 ('''void flux_coap_notify_device_event(uint64_t node_id,''',
  '''void flux_coap_notify_device_event(uint8_t kind, uint64_t node_id,'''),
]

# remaining single-key comparisons inside clear_node / node_forget / pending_get

              '        if (s_attr_cache[i].node_id == node_id && s_attr_cache[i].kind == kind) {')
s = s.replace('        if (s_pending[i].node_id == node_id) {',
              '        if (s_pending[i].node_id == node_id && s_pending[i].kind == kind) {')
s = s.replace('        if (s_pending[i].node_id == node_id) return &s_pending[i];',
              '        if (s_pending[i].node_id == node_id && s_pending[i].kind == kind)\n            return &s_pending[i];')
# call sites inside the drain: pass the notify slot's kind
for old,new in (
  ('flux_coap_pending_get(n->node_id)', 'flux_coap_pending_get(n->kind, n->node_id)'),
  ('flux_coap_cache_upsert_attr(n->node_id, n)', 'flux_coap_cache_upsert_attr(n->kind, n->node_id, n)'),
  ('flux_coap_cache_find_or_create(n->node_id)', 'flux_coap_cache_find_or_create(n->kind, n->node_id)'),
  ('flux_coap_node_forget(n->node_id)', 'flux_coap_node_forget(n->kind, n->node_id)'),
):
    s = s.replace(old, new)
# the notify slot must carry kind through
s = s.replace('    n->node_id    = node_id;', '    n->node_id    = node_id;\n    n->kind       = kind;')
open(p,'w').write(s)

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP

CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.

s = s.replace('''/* ── Subscription attribute callbacks ────────────────────────────────────── */''',
'''/* Reject a node this file cannot act on. The old test was

static bool not_a_matter_node(uint64_t node_id)
{

}

/* ── Subscription attribute callbacks ────────────────────────────────────── */''', 1)

# Stop using Matter node IDs as identifiers for non-Matter devices

## Context

flux keeps one device registry shared by Matter and non-Matter devices. Non-Matter (Modbus) devices are given a **synthetic Matter node ID** — `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0x0100000000000000` plus a counter — and every consumer infers *what kind of device this is* from the magnitude of that integer (`flux_is_modbus_node(nid)` ≡ `nid >= BASE`).

That is a category error: `node_id` is a Matter protocol identifier allocated within a fabric, and it is being used to name a Modbus meter that has no fabric. Three concrete costs, today:

1. **The magic constant is duplicated five times across three repos, and one copy is already wrong.** `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:158`, `flux-app/lib/models/matter_device.dart:125`, again as a bare literal at `flux-app/lib/providers/device_provider.dart:408`, `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/cli.py`, and `tests/integration/test_modbus.py:26` — which holds a stale `0xFFFFFFFF00000000` from a superseded design, as does `modbus_devices_plan.md:53`.
2. **~10 separate `flux_is_modbus_node()` guards** each independently encode "large number ⇒ not a device I can actually talk to" (`flux_controller.cpp:469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126`; `flux_coap_handlers.c:384,477`; `flux_energy_log.c:44`).
3. **A leaked constraint:** bit 63 must stay clear purely because the Flutter app decodes `node_id` into a signed Dart int (ADR-0009 elevates this to a cross-repo contract). The registry record itself (`flux_state.h:101-107`) has **no** kind field, while the energy CSV already records `SOURCE` (`modbus | matter`) — so the on-disk log knows the kind the wire contract refuses to carry.

Adding any further integration (Home Connect, whose native IDs are strings) makes this worse. **Outcome:** identity and kind become explicit data owned by the registry; `node_id` reverts to meaning only "Matter operational node ID".

## Decisions (locked)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D1 | The wire identity is a controller-issued **`uint32 dev_id`**. Not a string: `notify_t` is a fixed-size struct in a 32-slot queue and the attribute caches are fixed arrays compared with `==`; strings would cost RAM per slot and turn every hot-path lookup into `strcmp`. A vendor's native string ID belongs in its own subsystem's table. |
| D2 | Kind is an explicit **closed enum** on the record and on the wire (`DeviceKind`). Exhaustive switches beat no-proto-churn; we own the proto. |
| D3 | **One device = one transport.** `kind` lives on the device record, and `node_id` stays on the shared record as the Matter address, valid iff `kind == MATTER`. A device reachable two ways appears twice. This avoids a general address-table indirection entirely. |
| D4 | **Fresh `dev_id` per add** (monotonic counter, never reused). Re-adding a device is a new device, as today. |
| D5 | **Flag day** with in-place migration of persisted state. No wire back-compat; new firmware requires the new app. |
| D6 | `dev_id` counter **starts at `0x1000`**, so no `dev_id` can ever equal a legacy Matter `node_id` (which start at `0x0003` and are bounded by `FLUX_DEVICES_MAX 32`) or a legacy synthetic one (≥ 2⁵⁶). This makes the energy-CSV join safe by construction rather than by a format flag. |

## Firmware

**New neutral header** `firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h` (add `"devices"` to **both** `SRC_DIRS` and `INCLUDE_DIRS` in `firmware/main/CMakeLists.txt:1-4`) so the kind taxonomy isn't owned by `matter/`:

```c
typedef enum { FLUX_DEV_KIND_UNKNOWN = 0, FLUX_DEV_KIND_MATTER = 1,
               FLUX_DEV_KIND_MODBUS = 2, FLUX_DEV_KIND_CLOUD = 3 } flux_dev_kind_t;
```

**Record** — `firmware/main/matter/flux_state.h:101-107`:

```c
typedef struct {
    uint32_t dev_id;       /* controller-issued; THE identity. 0 = invalid */
    uint8_t  kind;         /* flux_dev_kind_t */
    uint64_t node_id;      /* Matter operational node ID; kind==MATTER only, else 0 */
    uint32_t vendor_id, product_id, device_type;
    char     name[FLUX_DEVICE_NAME_MAX];
} flux_DeviceRecord;
```

New helpers beside the existing ones: `flux_device_get_by_dev_id()`, `flux_device_kind_of(dev_id)`, `flux_device_node_id_of(dev_id, *out)` (NOT_FOUND unless MATTER), and — the one that's easy to miss — **`flux_device_dev_id_for_node(node_id, *out)`** for the *inbound* Matter direction, since CHIP callbacks know only the node ID. Delete `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` and `flux_is_modbus_node`.

**Hot-path requirement:** `attr_report_cb` fires per attribute report and must not do a mutex-protected registry scan each time. Resolve `dev_id` **once at subscribe time** (`flux_device_subscribe`, `flux_controller.cpp:849`) and carry it in the per-subscription context; the lookup helper is the fallback, not the norm.

**Files to change:**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `matter/flux_state.c:420-520` (`"flux_dev"` ns) | record layout, `id_ctr`, `ver` key, migration, new helpers |
| `matter/flux_controller.cpp` | the ~10 guards **disappear** (see below); emit path carries `dev_id`; `kAttrMap` untouched |
| `events/flux_events.{h,c}` | `flux_events_emit_attr/_device` take `uint32_t dev_id` |
| `coap/flux_coap_internal.h`, `coap/flux_coap_notify.c` | `notify_t` and the fixed caches keyed by `uint32 dev_id` (slightly smaller); `flux_coap_node_forget(dev_id)` |
| `coap/flux_coap_handlers.c` | `parse_id_query` → `parse_dev_query`; `hnd_clusters_get:477` and `hnd_devices_delete:384` branch on `kind` from the registry, not magnitude; `/command`, `/read`, `/write` resolve `dev_id → node_id` and return a clean `NOT_SUPPORTED` for non-Matter kinds |
| `modbus/flux_state` record + `flux_coap_modbus.c`, `flux_modbus_task.c` | `flux_ModbusRecord.node_id` → `uint32 dev_id`; upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit |
| `energy/flux_energy_log.{c,h}` | `classify()` reads `kind` from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; CSV column renamed `NODE_ID` → `DEV_ID` |
| `energy/flux_coap_energy.c` | per-device series keyed by `dev_id` |

**Where the guards go.** Each of the ~10 sites currently means "reject synthetic". After this change the caller resolves identity first: `flux_device_node_id_of(dev_id, &node)` fails for any non-Matter kind, so the Matter functions can assume they were handed a real node ID and the guards are simply deleted. The `NOT_SUPPORTED` behaviour visible to clients is unchanged; it just now originates from one place.

**Migration** (`"flux_dev"` gains a `ver` u8 key; absent/0 ⇒ legacy):
1. Read each blob with a private `flux_DeviceRecordV0` copy of the old struct.
2. Assign `dev_id = ++id_ctr` (from `0x1000`); `kind = old.node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 ? MODBUS : MATTER`; `node_id = kind == MATTER ? old.node_id : 0`.
3. Build an in-RAM `old node_id → dev_id` map (≤32 entries, stack), then migrate `"flux_mb"` records through it. **Order matters** — device registry first.
4. Write `ver = 1`. Also migrate the persisted energy-role map (`"flux"` ns, `energy_roles` blob, keyed by node ID) through the same map.
5. Record growth is ~8 bytes × 32 ≈ 256 B; confirm with `nvs_get_stats()` against the 24 KiB `nvs` partition.

## Proto

Shared contract, checked out as `flux-controller/proto` and `flux-app/flux-interface` (upstream `~/workspace/flux/flux-proto`). **These three checkouts are currently diverged — edit each deliberately, never blind-copy.**

- `Device`: add `uint32 dev_id`, `DeviceKind kind`; keep `node_id` documented as *Matter-only, advisory*.
- Switch to `dev_id`: `AttrsUpdate`, `DeviceStateEvent`, `DeviceCommand`, `WriteAttrRequest`, `ReadRequest`, `RenameDeviceRequest`, `EnergyRoleEntry`, `EnergyDeviceSeries`, `ModbusDeviceConfig`.
- **Use new field numbers and `reserved` the old ones** (the style `CommissionRequest` already uses with `reserved 8,9`). A stale peer's `node_id` must decode as *absent*, not as a plausible-but-wrong `dev_id`. This is what makes the flag day loud instead of silently corrupting.
- Regenerate all three: `cd proto && make c`, `make dart` (needs `~/.pub-cache/bin` on PATH), plus `tools/flux-ctl/src/flux_ctl/flux_pb2.py` and `tests/integration/flux_pb2.py`.
- Endpoints: `?id=<16-hex>` → `?dev=<hex>` on `/devices/attrs`, `/devices/clusters`, `/events`, `DELETE /devices`, `DELETE /modbus/devices`. Renaming the param (rather than reinterpreting it) means an old client fails cleanly.

## App

`MatterDevice.id` (UUID) stays the app's primary key; `nodeId` becomes `devId` plus an explicit `kind`.

- `lib/models/matter_device.dart`: `nodeId` → `devId` (int), add `DeviceKind kind`; `isModbus` becomes `kind == DeviceKind.modbus`; **both magic-constant sites deleted** (`:125` and the bare literal at `device_provider.dart:408`).
- `lib/services/flux_coap_service.dart`: `?dev=` params, `_sendCmd:592`, `_writeAttr:695`, `_readAttrs:745`, the observe URL at `:473`, `setEnergyRoles:345` map keys, `getEnergyHistory:290` series ids, and the resource-map doc comment at `:31-50`.
- `lib/providers/device_provider.dart`: `_onDeviceStateEvent:671` matches on `devId`; `_syncEnergyRoles:1119` keys; `deviceNameForNode:132` → `deviceNameForDev`; `_normalizeControllerNetworkType:344` reads `kind`.
- `lib/models/energy_history.dart` `PvDeviceSeries.nodeId` → `devId`, and its lookup at `energy_history_card.dart:221`.

**App-side migration** (`MatterDevice.fromJson`, legacy records hold `nodeId`): after the flag day the controller reports `dev_id`s the app has never seen, and `_reconcileWithController:397` matches by node ID. Resolution: **during reconcile, match legacy records on `node_id` for `kind == MATTER`** — `Device.node_id` survives for Matter devices, so those keep their name, room and energy role. Modbus records cannot be matched and are re-adopted fresh, losing name/role — which is exactly today's re-add behaviour and consistent with D4. Auto-delete of the stale local record already only applies to `managedBy == controller` (`:455`), so nothing phone-commissioned is at risk.

**Energy history discontinuity** (accepted): pre-migration CSV rows carry legacy node IDs, so per-device breakdown starts fresh at the upgrade. Bucket totals continue unaffected — they aggregate via the class column, which survives. D6 guarantees a legacy ID can never be mistaken for a `dev_id`.

## Verification

1. `flutter analyze lib/ test/` clean (0 errors/warnings) and `flutter test` green; `flutter build apk` **before** installing (a plain install ships a stale cached APK).
2. `cd firmware && source esp-env.sh && idf.py build`; flash with `idf.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash` after stopping `serial_logger.py` (it holds the port).
3. **Migration test on real state, not a wipe** — this is the one that matters. Before flashing, capture `flux-ctl devices` and the energy-role map from the live controller; after flashing, confirm: same device count, Matter devices keep names, `kind` is right for each, Modbus devices reappear (fresh identity), and `nvs_get_stats()` shows headroom.
4. `flux-ctl` round-trip on every touched endpoint; remove the stale `MODBUS_NODE_BASE` from `tests/integration/test_modbus.py:26` and re-point its assertions at `kind`.
5. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free (ADR-0010 pattern, as `flux_energy_agg.c` does).
6. End-to-end on the phone: device list, a live attribute update, a command, energy roles surviving a controller reboot.

## Follow-ups this unblocks

- **The command bus** (`devices/flux_device_cmd.c`): now trivial, because routing is `kind` from the registry rather than a bit test, and the Matter backend keeps its existing `node_id` signature — the bus resolves the address. Land it separately.
- **New ADR** superseding ADR-0009 (`docs/adr/0009-modbus-devices-as-synthetic-node-ids.md`): identity is registry-issued, kind is explicit, node IDs are Matter-only. Delete the bit-63 cross-repo contract along with the encoding that needed it.

## Deferred: Home Connect

Separate work, still under consideration. Decisions already taken: controller owns the runtime (token, SSE stream, control); bring-your-own `developer.home-connect.com` client with credentials stored only on the controller; phone runs the `authorize` step and hands the code to the controller; scope runs through price-aware deferral via `BSH.Common.Option.StartInRelative` (the first caller `flux_prices_at()` would ever have). Phasing: prerequisites → account linking + read-only monitoring → control → deferral.

**Verify before writing any of it:** whether Home Connect supports RFC 8628 Device Flow — if so, the entire app-side OAuth stack disappears (no `flutter_web_auth_2`, no Android intent-filter, no iOS `CFBundleURLTypes`). Biggest technical risk: `esp_http_client` is request/response shaped and SSE needs a never-ending stream; budget an `esp_tls` fallback. Independent bug found while designing it, worth fixing regardless: `flux-app/lib/models/device_type.dart:147` maps `0x0073` to `airQualitySensor`, but `0x0073` is Matter's **Laundry Washer** — Air Quality Sensor is `0x002C`, already correct on the next line.

That plan assumed the synthetic-range identity model and needs rewriting against `dev_id` + `kind` once this lands — which is the main reason to do this refactor first.

content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.subject: Verify end to end and write the superseding ADR
content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free. New ADR superseding docs/adr/0009 (identity registry-issued, kind explicit, node IDs Matter-only, bit-63 contract deleted).

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.

# FW-ADR-0009: Modbus devices are first-class devices under synthetic node IDs

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-30 (reconstructed from `matter/flux_state.h:145-166`)
- **Relates to:** flux-proto (the app decodes `node_id`; contract-adjacent)

## Context

flux manages Matter devices (real 64-bit operational node IDs, assigned from a
small counter starting at `0x0003`) and Modbus TCP/UDP devices (energy meters,
inverters). The app and the `/devices` API should treat both uniformly rather
than carry two parallel device concepts across the wire.

## Decision

Each Modbus device gets a **synthetic 64-bit node ID** `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE |
n` (`0x0100000000000000 | n`) and is mirrored into the same device registry as a
`flux_DeviceRecord`, so `/devices` lists Matter and Modbus devices
transparently. `flux_is_modbus_node(nid)` is the single discriminator. The base
is chosen to be **positive as a signed 64-bit integer** (bit 63 clear): the
phone app decodes `node_id` into a signed Dart int and formats it as hex for the
`?id=` query — a value with the top bit set would go negative and never match on
the controller (silent "no readings").

## Consequences

- One device model, one API surface, one identity type across Matter and Modbus
  — and across transports (the synthetic-ID scheme is transport-neutral).
- The bit-63-clear constraint is a **cross-repo contract** with the app: any
  future ID scheme (more synthetic ranges, other bus types) must keep IDs
  positive-signed or break the app's `?id=` round-trip silently. This is the
  kind of constraint that belongs in the shared proto ADR series too.
- The Modbus registry is separate config but every entry is mirrored into the
  Matter device table; the two must be kept consistent on upsert/remove.

## Alternatives considered

- **A separate Modbus API and device list** — duplicates enumeration, filtering,
  and naming; the app would carry two device concepts.
- **Use the full 64-bit space (bit 63 free)** — round-trips wrong through the
  app's signed-int decode; the exact silent-failure this base avoids.

# FW-ADR-0015: A device is identified by (kind, node_id)

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-10
- **Supersedes:** [FW-ADR-0009](0009-modbus-devices-as-synthetic-node-ids.md)
- **Relates to:** flux-proto (`DeviceKind`), flux-app, flux-ctl

## Context

ADR-0009 gave every Modbus device a **synthetic** 64-bit node ID
(`0x0100000000000000 | n`) so Matter and Modbus devices could share one registry
and one `/devices` API. The kind of a device was then recoverable only by testing
the *magnitude* of that integer — `flux_is_modbus_node(nid) ≡ nid >= BASE`.

That worked, and it cost more than it saved:

- The base constant was duplicated across three repos (firmware, app, flux-ctl,
  integration tests) and **two copies had already drifted** to a stale
  `0xFFFFFFFF00000000` from a superseded design.
- About ten independent guards each re-encoded "this integer is too large to be a
  Matter node, so I cannot talk to it" — a type question answered by arithmetic.
- It leaked a **cross-repo contract**: bit 63 had to stay clear purely because
  the app decodes `node_id` into a signed Dart int. Any future ID scheme
  inherited that constraint or broke the `?id=` round-trip silently.
- The energy CSV already recorded a `SOURCE` column (`matter | modbus`), so the
  on-disk log carried a kind the wire contract refused to.

A `node_id` is a Matter operational identifier allocated within a fabric. A
Modbus meter has no fabric, so naming it with one was a category error that a
third integration (Home Connect, whose native IDs are strings) would have made
worse.

## Decision

**Kind becomes explicit data, and identity becomes the pair `(kind, node_id)`.**

- A closed enum `DeviceKind { UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3 }` lives in
  the shared proto and, as `flux_dev_kind_t`, in the neutral firmware header
  `main/devices/flux_device_kind.h` — deliberately not under `matter/`, so the
  taxonomy is not owned by one backend.
- `flux_DeviceRecord` gains a `kind` field. Every registry lookup takes the pair:
  `flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id)`, `flux_device_set_name(kind, node_id, …)`,
  `flux_energy_role_of(kind, node_id)`, and so on.
- `node_id` keeps its own meaning: the Matter operational node ID when
  `kind == MATTER`, and otherwise just the per-kind identifier the owning
  subsystem allocates. Modbus IDs now start at 1 from an ordinary counter.
- `FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE` and `flux_is_modbus_node()` are **deleted**. The ten
  magnitude guards collapse into one registry question,
  `not_a_matter_node(node_id)` ⇒ `flux_device_kind_of_node(node_id) != MATTER`,
  so a device of any *future* non-Matter kind is rejected too instead of sneaking
  through because its ID happened to be small.
- `UNKNOWN = 0` is a decode error, never a synonym for MATTER. A peer that omits
  `kind` is handled by an explicit registry fallback (below), not by a default.

### Wire compatibility

`kind` is an **added** field, not a renumbering: `Device.kind = 8`, plus a `kind`
field on `AttrsUpdate`, `DeviceStateEvent`, `DeviceCommand`, `ReadRequest`,
`WriteAttrRequest`, `RenameDeviceRequest`, `EnergyRoleEntry` and
`EnergyDeviceSeries`. Per-device CoAP requests keep `?id=<hex>` and may add
`&kind=<n>`.

When a request arrives without `kind`, `resolve_kind_query()` looks the node ID
up in the registry and uses the kind it finds. This is unambiguous as long as one
node ID is not reused across kinds, which is true of all existing state — and it
is a lookup, never an inference from magnitude. New clients send `kind`
explicitly; all three (app, flux-ctl, integration tests) now do.

### Persisted-state migration

`flux_DeviceRecord` and `flux_EnergyRoleRec` are **the same size** before and
after (88 and 16 bytes; `_Static_assert`s pin this), because `kind` fell into
existing padding. Two consequences, both deliberate:

- An unmigrated record is **silently misread**, not rejected — the field offsets
  after `kind` shift. So migration must be unconditional, driven by an explicit
  `ver` key in the namespace, and cannot lean on a size heuristic.
- On upgrade, `kind` is reconstructed from the legacy encoding exactly once:
  `kind_from_legacy_node_id(nid) = nid >= 0x0100000000000000 ? MODBUS : MATTER`.
  This is the *only* place that constant survives, as a migration input.

## Consequences

- Routing by kind is a switch on data, so the eventual command bus resolves a
  backend from the record rather than from a bit test.
- The bit-63-clear cross-repo contract is gone, along with the encoding that
  needed it. IDs may use the full 64-bit space per kind.
- `kind` is mandatory in every new call path. The app's danger here is that
  Dart's `DeviceKind kind = DeviceKind.matter` default lets semantically wrong
  code compile silently — a missed `kind` on a device event stops Modbus
  readings reaching the UI without a single warning. The audited paths are
  `_toAppEvent`, `setEnergyRoles`, the `/events` observe, `DELETE /devices`, and
  `_subscribedNodeIds` (now keyed on the pair, since two kinds may share an ID).
- Adding a kind means: one proto enumerator, one `flux_dev_kind_t` value, one
  Dart enumerator — and no new identifier range to reserve.

## Alternatives considered

- **A controller-issued opaque `dev_id` replacing `node_id` on the wire** (the
  original plan). Cleaner in the abstract, but it renumbers most messages, breaks
  the energy-CSV join across the upgrade, forces an inbound
  `node_id → dev_id` map for CHIP callbacks (which only ever know a node ID), and
  needs its own counter and collision-avoidance rules. `(kind, node_id)` fixes
  the actual defect — kind inferred from magnitude — at a fraction of the blast
  radius, and leaves `dev_id` available if a kind ever needs a non-integer key.
- **A string identifier.** `notify_t` is a fixed-size struct in a 32-slot queue
  and the attribute caches are fixed arrays compared with `==`; strings would
  cost RAM per slot and turn every hot-path lookup into `strcmp`. A vendor's
  native string ID belongs in its own subsystem's table.
- **Keeping the synthetic ranges and adding `kind` as advisory metadata.** Leaves
  every magnitude guard in place and so leaves the bug class intact.

content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

refactor(devices): identify a device by (kind, node_id)

Modbus devices used to live in a reserved node-id range
(0x0100000000000000 | n), so "what kind of device is this?" was answered by
testing the magnitude of an integer. That constant was duplicated across three
repos with two copies already drifted to a stale value, ~10 call sites each
re-encoded the same magnitude test, and it leaked a cross-repo contract: bit 63
had to stay clear purely because the app decodes node_id into a signed int.

Kind is now explicit data. flux_dev_kind_t lives in the neutral header
devices/flux_device_kind.h (not under matter/, so no backend owns the taxonomy),
DeviceKind rides the wire as an added field, and every registry lookup takes the
pair — flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id) and friends. FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and
flux_is_modbus_node() are gone; the magnitude guards collapse into one registry
question, which also rejects any future non-Matter kind instead of letting it
through on a small id.

Per-device CoAP requests may pass &kind=<n>; when it is absent the controller
resolves the kind from the registry rather than inferring it. flux-ctl and the
integration tests now send it explicitly.

Persisted state migrates in place, guarded by a version key rather than a size
check: measured, the v0 and v1 records are the SAME size (88 and 16 bytes — kind
fell into existing padding), so an unmigrated record is silently misread, not
rejected. _Static_asserts pin those sizes so a future field change fails the
build instead of the migration. The legacy base survives only as the migration's
input, mapping old ids to a kind exactly once.

Verified on hardware: all 10 devices survive the upgrade with names intact and
correct kinds (2 modbus / 8 matter), vendor and product ids decode cleanly
(a misread record would garble precisely those), Modbus readings and Matter
attributes both flow, and the migrated energy roles still classify grid import
across the reboot.

ADR-0015 supersedes ADR-0009.

fabric can only ever address Matter devices, so only the controller port acts on

content.content:
11 candidate messages
Grounded answer: **rooms are purely app-local today.** `Room` + `MatterDevice.roomId`, persisted in SharedPreferences under `'rooms'` (`device_store.dart:15`), and the shared proto has **no room concept at all** — grep for room/label in `flux.proto` returns only an unrelated comment. The controller doesn't know rooms exist.

## Why that placement will hurt

You already have the cautionary tale in-tree: **energy roles are app-local and pushed one-way**, and nothing reads them back. The consequences are recorded pain — roles reset to `none` blank the house energy view, and they're wiped whenever a device is re-added. Rooms are the same shape of data and will reproduce it exactly:

- **Two phones disagree permanently.** You're running `.229` and A063 right now; rooms set on one are invisible on the other, forever.
- **Reinstall or clear-storage loses the whole layout** — the same class of loss as the phantom-controller episode earlier.
- **Re-adding a device drops it back to "No Room"**, because `roomId` lives on the app's device record and a re-add mints a fresh one.
- **The controller can't use rooms** for anything — no per-room energy attribution, no "run the dishwasher when the kitchen is cheap", no room-scoped automation. Given the energy-management pivot, that's the expensive one.

## Three candidate homes

**1. App-local (today).** Simple, works offline, no wire contract. But it's per-phone by construction, and rooms are a property of the *home*, not of a handset.

**2. Controller (recommended).** Same model as the device registry itself: controller is authoritative, app caches for offline display. Survives reinstalls, agrees across phones, and makes rooms available to controller-side logic.

**3. Matter User Label cluster (0x0041).** The spec's own answer for room assignment, fabric-scoped, and readable by Apple/Google — genuinely portable. But it can't hold Modbus/synthetic devices, it's an optional cluster, and it can't store the *room list* itself (an empty room would simply vanish). Good as a **mirror**, wrong as the store.

## The suggestion I'd actually make

Don't add a third per-device metadata mechanism. The controller already has **two** ad-hoc ones: `name` inside `flux_DeviceRecord`, and a separate `energy_roles` NVS blob that the app pushes one-way. Rooms would make three.

Fold them into **one controller-side per-device metadata record** — name, room, energy role — with the app as a cache rather than the owner. That single move kills the roles-wiped-on-re-add bug, the two-phones-disagree bug, and the rooms question together, and it gives the energy log a room dimension (the CSV already carries `DEVICE_NAME`; a room column is the natural companion).

Two design details worth deciding up front: membership stays device-side (`roomId` on the record, not a room→devices list) since that's already the shape and avoids two-way consistency; and the room list needs its own small store so empty rooms survive.

**One sequencing point:** this should come *after* the `dev_id` refactor (tasks #13–21), not before. Room membership has to key on something stable, and keying it on today's `node_id` would just have to be migrated again — plus "fresh identity per add" means a re-added device loses its room unless the metadata record is keyed on something that survives, which is exactly the trade-off you already chose there.

There's one honest counter-argument: `deviceNameForNode` carries a deliberate comment about resolving names locally "instead of trusting stale names baked into controller-side data", so someone chose local authority for names on purpose. That reasoning holds for *display during a stale connection* — which the cache covers — but not for ownership.

Want me to write this up as an ADR with the proto sketch and migration path, or leave it as a note until the `dev_id` work lands?

feat(proto): rooms and per-device metadata owned by the controller

Rooms were phone-local (SharedPreferences), so two phones disagreed forever, a
reinstall lost the whole layout, and re-adding a device silently dropped it back
to "No Room" — the same failure the app-local energy roles already had. Both now
live on the device record the controller owns, with the app as a cache.

Room ids are small controller-issued integers rather than the app's UUIDs:
Device.room_id sits in a fixed-size NVS record where 2 bytes beats 37. Id 0 is
the "No Room" sentinel and is never stored or listed. Membership stays on the
device, not as a room→devices list, so there is only one copy of the
relationship.

DeviceMeta uses `optional` on every writable field: clearing a room and clearing
an energy role are legitimate writes, and without presence they are
indistinguishable from an untouched field.

EnergyRoleEntry/EnergyRoleMap are removed rather than deprecated. The role is
now Device.energy_class, written through the same DeviceMeta path — leaving a
second way to set one field is how the app's copy and the controller's drifted
apart to begin with. The app is not released, so there is nothing to keep
compatible.
