content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.subject: Verify end to end and write the superseding ADR
content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free. New ADR superseding docs/adr/0009 (identity registry-issued, kind explicit, node IDs Matter-only, bit-63 contract deleted).

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

content.subject: Add rooms and per-device metadata to the shared proto
content.description: Room{id,name}, RoomList, Device.room_id + energy_class, and a partial-update DeviceMeta message. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings.

content.subject: Add room_id and energy_cls to the device record
content.description: Extend flux_DeviceRecord, add set_room/set_energy_class helpers, and reimplement flux_energy_role_of off the record so the energy log is unchanged.

content.subject: Add the controller-side room list store
content.description: NVS-backed room table (uint16 id, name, monotonic id counter) with get_all/set_all, and reset devices whose room disappears to the No Room sentinel.

content.subject: Migrate the energy_roles blob into the device records
content.description: State version 2: stamp each persisted role onto its device record, drop the separate blob and flux_energy_roles_set, keeping the live grid/PV classification working across the upgrade.
content.activeForm: Migrating energy roles into the records

content.subject: Expose rooms and device metadata over CoAP
content.description: GET/PUT /rooms, POST /devices/meta for partial name/room/energy-class updates, and room_id + energy_class on the /devices listing.

content.subject: Make the app read rooms from the controller
content.description: Room.id becomes an int, rooms and energy roles come from the controller with the app as cache, and createRoom/assignRoom/setEnergyRole write through. Remove the one-way _syncEnergyRoles push.

content.subject: Upload the phone's existing rooms and roles once
content.description: One-time migration on first sync with a room-capable controller: push local UUID rooms (remapped to controller ids), per-device room assignments and energy roles, then mark done so it never re-runs.

content.subject: Add room commands to flux-ctl and verify end to end
content.description: rooms ls/add/rm plus room assignment, a Room column on devices, then flash and confirm rooms and migrated roles survive a reboot and agree across phones.

feat(rooms): the controller owns rooms and per-device metadata

Rooms lived only in the phone's SharedPreferences, so two phones disagreed
permanently, a reinstall lost the layout, and re-adding a device dropped it back
to "No Room". Energy roles had the same shape and the same bugs, plus a second
storage mechanism: an NVS blob the app pushed one-way that nothing read back.

Both now live on the device record — room_id and energy_cls beside name — so
there is ONE per-device metadata record and the controller owns it. Rooms are a
small NVS table (id, name) with a monotonic id counter. Ids are never reused: a
device still pointing at a deleted room would otherwise be silently adopted by
whichever room inherited the number, which is a wrong answer that looks valid.
Instead the reference matches nothing and is reset to No Room, logged.

flux_energy_roles_set and the roles blob are gone; flux_energy_role_of now reads
the device record, so the energy log is unchanged. GET/PUT /rooms replaces the
list wholesale (PUT answers with the assigned ids, which the caller has no other
way to learn) and POST /devices/meta does partial updates — every writable field
is `optional` on the wire because 0 is meaningful for both room (No Room) and
energy class (no override), so "absent" must stay distinct from "zero".

The migration chain is now v0 -> v1 -> v2, each step converting between frozen
copies of the layouts rather than the live struct. v2 records are 96 bytes where
v1 was 88, so unlike the v0/v1 step a stale record now fails the exact-size check
and disappears loudly instead of being misread — a _Static_assert fails the build
if a future edit makes those sizes match again.

Verified on hardware: 10/10 devices survive, rooms and assignments persist across
a reboot, deleting a room resets exactly the affected device, a re-created room
gets a fresh id, and energy class survives a room change.

content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.subject: Verify end to end and write the superseding ADR
content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free. New ADR superseding docs/adr/0009 (identity registry-issued, kind explicit, node IDs Matter-only, bit-63 contract deleted).

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

content.subject: Add rooms and per-device metadata to the shared proto

content.subject: Add room_id and energy_cls to the device record
content.description: Extend flux_DeviceRecord, add set_room/set_energy_class helpers, and reimplement flux_energy_role_of off the record so the energy log is unchanged.

content.subject: Add the controller-side room list store
content.description: NVS-backed room table (uint16 id, name, monotonic id counter) with get_all/set_all, and reset devices whose room disappears to the No Room sentinel.

content.subject: Migrate the energy_roles blob into the device records
content.description: State version 2: stamp each persisted role onto its device record, drop the separate blob and flux_energy_roles_set, keeping the live grid/PV classification working across the upgrade.

content.subject: Expose rooms and device metadata over CoAP
content.description: GET/PUT /rooms, POST /devices/meta for partial name/room/energy-class updates, and room_id + energy_class on the /devices listing.

content.subject: Make the app read rooms from the controller
content.description: Room.id becomes an int, rooms and energy roles come from the controller with the app as cache, and createRoom/assignRoom/setEnergyRole write through. Remove the one-way _syncEnergyRoles push.

feat(rooms): store the energy role, add flux-ctl room commands

The device record held the derived log class, which cannot represent what the
user actually assigned: a car charger and a heat pump are both `load`. Storing
only the class would have left the app keeping a private copy of the
distinction — the same split that let rooms and roles drift apart. The record
now holds flux_EnergyRole and class_from_role() derives the class in one place,
so the energy log is unchanged.

The v1 -> v2 migration maps a legacy class back to a role. A legacy `load`
cannot say which kind of consumer it was, so it lands on ENERGY_ROLE_LOAD until
the phone uploads the real assignment.

flux-ctl gains `rooms ls/add/rm/assign` and `role`, and the devices table gains
Room and Role columns — with vendor and product merged into one, because nine
columns wrapped every cell into uselessness.

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
feat(rooms): the controller owns rooms and energy roles; app caches them

Rooms lived in this phone's SharedPreferences with UUID ids, so two phones
disagreed permanently, a reinstall lost the layout, and re-adding a device
dropped it back to "No Room". Energy roles had the same shape and the same bugs.
Both are now read from the controller and written through it.

Room.id becomes a controller-issued int, and createRoom returns null when the
controller is unreachable rather than minting a local id — a phone-side id is
precisely the divergence this replaces, so the UI says the room was not created
instead of showing one that would vanish on the next sync.

The hand-off is one-shot and recorded: on the first sync, this phone's rooms are
re-created on the controller, its per-device assignments remapped from UUID to
the issued ids, and its energy roles pushed. It runs BEFORE reconcile, because
reconcile treats the controller as authoritative for room and role — and on that
first sync the controller has neither, so the other order would wipe the layout
a moment before uploading it. Reconcile's adoption stays suppressed until the
flag is set, so a failed upload leaves the local copy intact to retry.

Two things that would have bitten quietly:
- Room.fromJson now parses `id` as int, and a legacy UUID makes `as int` throw a
  TypeError — an Error, not an Exception, which the store's `on Exception` would
  have let escape and take the whole room load with it.
- The legacy UUIDs cannot be read back through Room or MatterDevice at all, so
  the store gained raw readers for them; without those the hand-off would have
  had nothing to map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG

---
name: energy-roles-app-local-only
description: Live energy house view blanks because energy roles are app-local only and reset to none on controller device re-add
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 336b3813-63b0-431c-b3d7-c5d1e1a6f5b8
---

Energy roles (EnergyRole on MatterDevice) are stored **only** in the app's local
state and pushed **one-way** to the controller via `POST /energy/roles` (which the
controller uses solely to classify its energy-history log). The `Device` message from
`GET /devices` carries **no** role field, and there is no `GET /energy/roles` — so the
app can never restore roles from the controller.

The live house view (`house_energy_scene.dart` → `DeviceProvider.energySummary` →
`EnergySummary.fromDevices`) reads ONLY local `energyRole`; a device with
`energyRole == none` contributes no node, so if all roles are `none` the scene shows
just the "HOME 0.00 W" pill even while the hub is online and live power flows.

Roles get wiped whenever `_reconcileWithController` (device_provider.dart ~414-465)
(re)creates a controller device — it builds them with `energyRole: none` and its
stale-purge removes+re-adds any device the controller momentarily stops reporting
(e.g. Modbus synthetic node churn). Diagnosed 2026-07-16: blank live view, hub Local,
SunSpec 103 producing 90 W, history correct, but device settings showed
"Not in energy overview".

**Why:** the controller is the real cross-device source of truth for classification
but the app treats local state as authoritative and can't read roles back.
**How to apply:** immediate recovery = re-assign roles per device in settings. Durable
fix = either preserve roles across purge/re-add app-side, or add role to the Device
proto / a `GET /energy/roles` (needs controller firmware). See [[flux-energy-management]],
[[flux-proto-dart-bindings]].

---
name: energy-roles-app-local-only
description: FIXED 2026-08-11 — rooms and energy roles now live on the controller's device record; app is a cache
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 336b3813-63b0-431c-b3d7-c5d1e1a6f5b8
---

**Resolved 2026-08-11.** Rooms and energy roles are now controller-owned, on the
device record (`flux_DeviceRecord.room_id` / `.energy_role`), and the app caches
them. `Device` carries `room_id` and `energy_role`; writes go through
`POST /devices/meta` (partial update — every writable field is `optional`,
because 0 is meaningful for both "No Room" and "no role"). Rooms are a separate
controller table behind `GET/PUT /rooms`, with controller-issued int ids that are
never reused. `POST /energy/roles`, `EnergyRoleMap` and the `energy_roles` NVS
blob are all gone.

The record stores the **role**, not the derived log class: a car charger and a
heat pump are both `load` to the energy log, so storing only the class would
force the app to keep a private copy of the distinction — which is exactly what
caused the original drift. `class_from_role()` in `flux_state.c` is the one place
the derivation happens.

**The original bug (for context):** roles lived only in app state and were pushed
one-way, so the live house view blanked whenever `_reconcileWithController`
re-created a controller device with `energyRole: none`, and two phones could
never agree. Rooms had the identical shape and the identical bug.

**Why it matters now:** the app must never write a room id it invented —
`createRoom` returns null when the controller is unreachable rather than minting
one locally. And on first sync a phone hands its old layout over
(`_uploadLocalLayoutOnce`) **before** reconcile, because reconcile treats the
controller as authoritative and would otherwise wipe the layout a moment before
uploading it.

**How to apply:** if roles or rooms look wrong, check the controller first
(`flux-ctl devices` shows Room and Role columns; `flux-ctl rooms ls`), not the
phone. See [[flux-energy-management]], [[flux-proto-dart-bindings]].

content.text:
Rooms now live on the controller. What shipped:

**Design** — one per-device metadata record (`name`, `room_id`, `energy_role`) that the controller owns and the app caches, plus a controller-owned room table so empty rooms survive. Room ids are controller-issued `uint16` and **never reused**, so a device pointing at a deleted room can't be silently adopted by a new one — it resolves to nothing and falls back to No Room, logged.

**One correction I made mid-build, worth knowing about:** I first stored the derived energy *class*. That's lossy — `carCharger` and `heatPump` both collapse to `load`, so the app would still have needed its private copy of the user's choice, which is the exact drift we were removing. The record now stores the **role**, and `class_from_role()` derives the log class in one place, so the energy log is unchanged.

**Verified on hardware** (controller + flux-ctl): rooms create/list/delete, assignment, roles, all surviving a reboot; deleting "Roof" reset exactly the one device that pointed at it; the re-created room got id 4, not 3.

Two things you should know:

1. **I can't confirm the old energy-roles blob carried anything into the records.** After the fold, every device read `UNKNOWN`. That's consistent with the blob having been empty, but I can't prove it: I erased the source without dumping it first, and the boot log that would have said `N role(s) folded in` was missed both times because the serial logger attaches ~30 s after reset. The practical impact is limited — classification falls back to the profile heuristic (grid meter still classifies as grid, inverter as pv), and the phone re-uploads its own roles on first sync. But it's an unverified step, not a verified one.

2. **The app leg is untested on device** — no phone is attached. `flutter analyze` is clean and all 98 tests pass, and the APK is built at `build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk`. Give me a port and I'll install it and check the one path that matters most: the first sync handing your existing rooms and roles to the controller before reconcile can overwrite them.

One loose end I'd rather flag than bury: the intermediate firmware I flashed for ~15 minutes wrote *class* values into the same byte that now holds *role*. For grid (1) and pv (2) the numbers coincide, which is why your bench state is correct — but a 3 or 4 written by that build would now read as car-charger/heat-pump. I re-set both roles explicitly via flux-ctl, so this device is clean; no released build was ever affected.

Pushed: `b397808` (controller), `da2dc27` (app), `3123b18` (proto). Task #22 — narrowing the Matter subscription attribute paths — is still open.

content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.subject: Verify end to end and write the superseding ADR
content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free. New ADR superseding docs/adr/0009 (identity registry-issued, kind explicit, node IDs Matter-only, bit-63 contract deleted).

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

content.subject: Add rooms and per-device metadata to the shared proto
content.description: Room{id,name}, RoomList, Device.room_id + energy_class, and a partial-update DeviceMeta message. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings.

content.subject: Add room_id and energy_cls to the device record
content.description: Extend flux_DeviceRecord, add set_room/set_energy_class helpers, and reimplement flux_energy_role_of off the record so the energy log is unchanged.

content.subject: Add the controller-side room list store
content.description: NVS-backed room table (uint16 id, name, monotonic id counter) with get_all/set_all, and reset devices whose room disappears to the No Room sentinel.

content.subject: Migrate the energy_roles blob into the device records
content.description: State version 2: stamp each persisted role onto its device record, drop the separate blob and flux_energy_roles_set, keeping the live grid/PV classification working across the upgrade.
content.activeForm: Migrating energy roles into the records

content.subject: Expose rooms and device metadata over CoAP
content.description: GET/PUT /rooms, POST /devices/meta for partial name/room/energy-class updates, and room_id + energy_class on the /devices listing.

content.subject: Make the app read rooms from the controller
content.description: Room.id becomes an int, rooms and energy roles come from the controller with the app as cache, and createRoom/assignRoom/setEnergyRole write through. Remove the one-way _syncEnergyRoles push.
content.activeForm: Moving app rooms to the controller

content.subject: Upload the phone's existing rooms and roles once
content.description: One-time migration on first sync with a room-capable controller: push local UUID rooms (remapped to controller ids), per-device room assignments and energy roles, then mark done so it never re-runs.

content.subject: Add room commands to flux-ctl and verify end to end
content.description: rooms ls/add/rm plus room assignment, a Room column on devices, then flash and confirm rooms and migrated roles survive a reboot and agree across phones.

content.subject: Add DeviceKind to the shared proto alongside node_id
content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. Needs device-by-device testing across the IKEA, LEDVANCE, Eve, tado and both Modbus devices.

content.text:
Installed and verified on the phone (`192.168.1.179` — adb was on port 38017, not 5555; I found it by scanning).

**The install caught a real bug.** The room cache was only ever written by this phone's own create/delete and by the one-time hand-off — nothing read `GET /rooms` during a normal sync. So the app connected to a controller holding three rooms and showed none of them, which is exactly the disagreement this whole move was meant to end. Reconcile now refreshes the cache, keeping the cached list on a failed read rather than blanking it. Fixed, rebuilt, reinstalled, re-verified.

What the device now shows, read from its persisted state rather than by driving the UI (your screen was off):

| | |
|---|---|
| room cache | `1 Living Room`, `2 Kitchen`, `4 Bedroom` — the controller's list, with its ids |
| tado° | `room=1`, adopted from the controller, not set on this phone |
| Eve plug | local `role=pv` **pushed up** to the controller by the hand-off |

That last row also settles the question I left open: the phone did hold roles, and the hand-off re-established them on the controller. Note the id `4` rather than `3` — the room I deleted during testing didn't have its number recycled.

Also worth noting: `Ikea Plug` and `SMGW` show proper names now where flux-ctl reported "Unknown" and "Test Vendor 1" — those are your local names, which the controller doesn't have. Names are in the same metadata record, so if you want them unified I can push local names up as part of the hand-off; I deliberately didn't, since overwriting controller-side names wasn't in scope.

Pushed: `573457a` (app), `b397808` (controller), `3123b18` (proto). I also updated the stored note about energy roles being app-local, since that's no longer true.

Still open: **task #22**, narrowing the Matter subscription attribute paths — the ~10 KB/round internal-RAM cost and the original source of the device-type bug.

feat(devices): sync device names with the controller

Name sat in the same controller-owned metadata record as room and energy role,
but the app still treated it as local-only: a rename never left the phone, and
reconcile never adopted the controller's. So names were the last piece that
disagreed between phones.

Renames now write through, and reconcile adopts the controller's name — but only
a non-empty one, since an empty name means the controller never learned it and
adopting that would blank a good local name.

The ordering matters more here than it did for rooms. The controller's name for a
Matter device comes from Basic Info at commissioning — "IKEA of Sweden", "Test
Vendor 1" — so adopting before handing the local names over would replace the
user's own names with vendor strings. Hence a one-shot upload that runs first,
pushing only names that actually differ.

That upload has its OWN flag rather than reusing layoutUploaded: phones that
already ran the rooms/roles hand-off must still upload their names, and sharing
the flag would skip exactly those phones — silently overwriting the user's names
on the next sync. This phone was one of them.

deviceNameForNode now takes the kind too; a node id alone does not identify a
device, and the PV series it serves is usually Modbus.

---
name: flux-ui
description: Flux app UI design system — Teenage-Engineering-inspired conventions for building/settings screens (tokens, panels, wording, connection state)
---

# Flux UI — design system

The concrete design language for the Flux Flutter app, distilled from the
Teenage Engineering sensibility: **form follows function, ruthless clarity,
technical-but-friendly, restraint over decoration.** Use this when building or
reworking any settings/config surface so screens stay consistent.

For open-ended critique of an existing screen, use the `design-review` skill
(the TE persona). This skill is the rulebook — the tokens and patterns already
agreed on.

## First principles

1. **Two devices, always distinguishable.** The system is a **controller** (the
   Flux hardware) and **this phone**. Every screen must make clear which box a
   setting acts on. The top-level model is two labelled panels: `CONTROLLER`
   and `THIS PHONE`.
2. **One word: "controller."** Never "hub" in user-facing copy (buttons,
   titles, snackbars, logs the user reads, status). Code identifiers
   (`HubConnection`, `ControllerStatus.noHub`) are exempt — internal only.
3. **Say the state in plain language.** "Connected", "Offline", "Connecting…"
   — not jargon. Keep protocol nouns (fabric, dataset, Ext PAN ID) *inside*
   detail screens, never on menu tiles.
4. **Icons earn their place.** No decorative leading icons on nav rows. The
   only iconography that survives is meaningful: the connection-state **dot**
   and the trailing chevron. When in doubt, remove it.

## Tokens

Connection-state accents (define as file-level consts; keep identical across
screens):

```dart
const _onlineColor     = Color(0xFF9FD8A8); // green  — connected, local
const _remoteColor     = Color(0xFFA9C7F2); // blue   — connected, remote tunnel
const _connectingColor = Color(0xFFBFC4CC); // grey   — connecting / standby / off
const _offlineColor    = Color(0xFFF2A9A0); // coral  — offline / error
```

**Panel label** (the TE instrument-panel header) — wide-tracked monospace,
uppercase, muted, no glyph:

```dart
Text(text, style: TextStyle(
  fontFamily: 'monospace', fontSize: 12, fontWeight: FontWeight.w700,
  letterSpacing: 2.4, color: cs.onSurfaceVariant));
// padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(20, 0, 20, 10)
```

**Grouping** — one `Card` per panel (`margin: horizontal 16`,
`clipBehavior: Clip.antiAlias`), rows separated by
`Divider(height: 1, indent: 16, endIndent: 16, color: cs.outlineVariant)`.

**Nav row** — `ListTile(title: Text(label), trailing: Icon(chevron_right))`.
No leading icon.

## Patterns

**Connection widget.** The `CONTROLLER` panel opens with a dedicated
connection-state tile: coloured dot (leading) + plain state ("Connected") +
one-line detail ("Local network" / "Remote · encrypted tunnel"), tapping
through to a Connection detail screen. State → (dot, title, subtitle) via a
`switch` on `ControllerStatus` + `ConnectionKind`.

**Connection detail screen.** Breaks the single live connection into its two
independent paths — `LOCAL NETWORK` and `REMOTE ACCESS` — each a card with a
State row (label left, dot + value right) and value rows (monospace, right-
aligned, ellipsised). `ConnectionKind` is mutually exclusive (loopback host =
remote, else local), so the inactive path reads "Standby".

**Scope-split screens.** When a concept exists on both devices (Matter,
Thread), don't cram both into one screen with sections — parameterise the
screen with a scope enum (`MatterScope { controller, phone }`,
`ThreadScope { controller, phone }`) and route two separate menu entries, one
under each panel. Controller scope shows the real fabric / operational Thread
network + Sync; phone scope shows this phone's admin identity / scanned
credentials. Keep the appBar title plain ("Matter", "Thread"); the panel the
user came from plus the in-screen caption carry the "whose" context.

## Reference implementation

- `lib/ui/screens/settings_screen.dart` — the two-panel layout + tokens.
- `lib/ui/screens/settings/connection_screen.dart` — local/remote detail.
- `lib/ui/screens/settings/matter_settings_screen.dart` / `thread_settings_screen.dart`
  — the scope-split pattern.

content.description: Composite identity (kind, node_id) — NOT a new dev_id. node_id keeps its field number and meaning, scoped to its kind's namespace. Add enum DeviceKind {UNKNOWN=0, MATTER=1, MODBUS=2, CLOUD=3} and a kind field to Device, AttrsUpdate, DeviceStateEvent, DeviceCommand, WriteAttrRequest, ReadRequest, RenameDeviceRequest, EnergyRoleEntry, EnergyDeviceSeries, ModbusDeviceConfig. Regenerate C, Dart and Python bindings. Edit the flux-interface submodule (now unified on fix/bridge-detach in both checkouts).

content.subject: Add kind to the registry record and key lookups on (kind, node_id)
content.description: New firmware/main/devices/flux_device_kind.h with flux_dev_kind_t (add "devices" to both SRC_DIRS and INCLUDE_DIRS). flux_DeviceRecord gains uint8_t kind next to node_id. Lookups become flux_device_get_by(kind, node_id); add flux_device_kind_of(node_id) only where a transitional single-key lookup is unavoidable. Delete FLUX_MODBUS_NODE_BASE and flux_is_modbus_node along with the bit-63 cross-repo contract they required.

content.subject: Migrate persisted state to carry kind
content.description: Add a ver key to the "flux_dev" NVS namespace; read legacy blobs via a private flux_DeviceRecordV0 and set kind from the old range (node_id >= 0x0100000000000000 -> MODBUS, else MATTER). Deliberately KEEP existing node_ids rather than renumbering: renumbering would break every app-side association (name, room, energy role) for no benefit, since kind now disambiguates. New Modbus devices may use small ids; legacy large ids remain valid within the modbus namespace. Migrate the "flux_mb" records and the energy_roles blob to carry kind too. Verify with nvs_get_stats().

content.subject: Carry kind through events, notify and CoAP
content.description: flux_events_emit_attr/_device take kind alongside node_id. notify_t and the fixed 32-entry caches in flux_coap_notify.c carry kind as a separate uint8 field and compare BOTH (explicitly not packed into the integer). flux_coap_node_forget(kind, node_id), wired for every kind's delete path. CoAP selection gains a kind criterion alongside ?id= on /devices/attrs, /devices/clusters, /events, DELETE /devices, DELETE /modbus/devices; hnd_clusters_get and hnd_devices_delete branch on kind from the registry.
content.activeForm: Carrying kind through events and CoAP

content.subject: Replace the is_modbus_node guards with kind checks
content.description: The ~10 flux_is_modbus_node guards (flux_controller.cpp 469,513,666,787,849,995,1081,1126 and flux_coap_handlers.c 384,477) become explicit kind != MATTER checks, resolved once by the caller rather than re-derived from magnitude at each site. Resolve kind at subscribe time (flux_device_subscribe) and carry it in the per-subscription context so attr_report_cb does no registry scan on the hot path.

content.subject: Update modbus and energy subsystems for dev_id
content.description: flux_ModbusRecord.node_id -> uint32 dev_id plus upsert/delete/synth-dump/emit in flux_coap_modbus.c and flux_modbus_task.c. energy/flux_energy_log.c classify() reads kind from the registry instead of guessing from magnitude; rename CSV column NODE_ID -> DEV_ID; energy/flux_coap_energy.c per-device series keyed by dev_id.

content.subject: Migrate the Flutter app to (kind, nodeId)
content.description: MatterDevice keeps nodeId and gains DeviceKind kind; isModbus becomes kind == modbus, deleting both magic-constant sites (matter_device.dart:125 and the bare literal at device_provider.dart:408). Reconcile and _onDeviceStateEvent match on (kind, nodeId). flux_coap_service passes kind on every per-device call. fromJson defaults legacy records' kind from the old range so nothing is lost on upgrade. energy_history PvDeviceSeries and the energy-role map carry kind.

content.subject: Update flux-ctl and integration tests
content.description: flux-ctl: ?dev= params, drop the node-base range filter in the modbus group, show kind in device listings. tests/integration/test_modbus.py: remove the stale MODBUS_NODE_BASE 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 and re-point assertions at kind. Also fix the stale base documented in modbus_devices_plan.md:53.

content.subject: Verify end to end and write the superseding ADR
content.description: flutter analyze + flutter test clean; idf.py build; capture flux-ctl devices and the energy-role map BEFORE flashing, then flash and confirm device count, Matter names/roles survived, kind is right, modbus re-adopts, nvs_get_stats has headroom. Host test for the migration mapping if it can be made ESP-IDF-free. New ADR superseding docs/adr/0009 (identity registry-issued, kind explicit, node IDs Matter-only, bit-63 contract deleted).

content.subject: Narrow the Matter subscription attribute paths
content.description: flux_controller.cpp subscribes with a full wildcard (attr_paths[0] = AttributePathParams(); all endpoints/clusters/attrs) on every device. Measured cost: ~10 KB internal RAM per subscription round across 5-6 devices, and it is also what made DeviceTypeList arrive once per endpoint (this evening's device-type bug). Replace with the ~20 (cluster, attr) pairs in kAttrMap plus Descriptor 0x001D/0x0000 and the BasicInformation fields the app needs. Risks to handle: Matter limits paths per subscription (only 3 guaranteed), new attributes would no longer appear for free (DeviceLiveData.attrs relies on that), and _inferTypeFromEvent depends on which keys arrive. 45	                    if (i > 0)

47	                          color: cs.outlineVariant),

52	                          .length,

71	  Future<void> _delete(BuildContext context) async {
72	    final cs = Theme.of(context).colorScheme;

78	        // device — the controller resets each one to No Room — and the user
79	        // should not have to find that out by trying it.

content.text:
Installed on your phone. **Settings → CONTROLLER → Rooms**.

```
Rooms
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Living Room                    ✕ │
│ No devices                       │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Basement                       ✕ │
│ 5 devices                        │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

Three judgment calls worth naming:

**Under CONTROLLER, not a phone section.** Rooms live on the controller now, so the screen is a view of its list. Putting it anywhere else would imply this phone owns them.

**Only removal.** Creating stays in the picker, at the moment you actually want a room — while assigning a device. This screen does the one thing those flows can't express, so it stays a list and an ✕ rather than becoming a second place to manage rooms.

**The confirmation names the consequence.** "5 devices will move to No Room. Nothing is removed from your home." Deleting a room never deletes a device — the controller resets each one — and you shouldn't have to learn that by trying it. If the controller doesn't accept the delete, the row stays put rather than vanishing and reappearing on the next sync.

I followed the `flux-ui` rulebook I found in the repo: panel card, hairline dividers, no decorative leading icons.

I haven't tapped through it — your screen was locked earlier and I'm not driving your phone. The controller-side delete path is verified (deleting "Roof" reset exactly the device pointing at it), and this screen calls that same `deleteRoom`. Pushed as `9f0595d`.

Those three leftover test rooms of mine — `Living Room`, `Kitchen`, `Bedroom`, all empty — are now removable in two taps each, if you want them gone.
